primary_entity: infringement or for passing off referred to in section 13 4

context: Where a proprietor institutes a suit for infringement or for passing off referred to in section 13 4, the court may grant such relief as it deems just and equitable, including an injunction restraining the defendant from any further acts of infringement or passing off. Damages shall be assessed according to principles of fairness and proportionality, taking into consideration the extent of the plaintiff’s loss and the defendant's gain derived from the infringing activity. The court may also order the defendant to provide a full account of profits made as a result of the infringing conduct, provided that the plaintiff demonstrates reasonable efforts to ascertain such profits. Further, subject to any terms specified by the court, the proprietor is entitled to an order for the delivery up or destruction of all goods bearing the infringing mark or get-up. The defendant shall be responsible for all costs associated with compliance with this order.
primary_entity: infringement or for passing off referred to in section 13 4

context: Where a proprietor establishes that another has used, in connection with goods or services, a trade mark identical or confusingly similar to his registered trade mark, and such use constitutes infringement or for passing off referred to in section 13 4, the court may grant an injunction restraining the defendant from any further acts of such nature. This restraint shall extend to all forms of advertising, promotion, packaging, and distribution where the infringing use is likely to cause confusion amongst consumers regarding the origin or quality of the goods or services. Provided that, if the defendant proves they had used the mark in good faith before the relevant date, the court may grant such relief as it deems just, considering the extent of consumer deception and the proprietor’s demonstrable commercial loss.
primary_entity: infringement or for passing off referred to in section 13 4

context: Any proprietor instituting proceedings under this Act against a person alleged to have engaged in infringement or for passing off referred to in section 13 4 shall be entitled to seek, by way of interlocutory relief, an injunction restraining the defendant from continuing such infringing activities pending final determination of the suit. Provided that, where the defendant has acted fraudulently or dishonestly in adopting or using the impugned mark, the court may, without prejudice to any other remedy available under this Act, award punitive damages not exceeding ten times the amount of actual damages proven. Further, upon finding infringement, the court shall order the defendant to undertake corrective advertising at its own expense, as determined by the court, to mitigate consumer confusion and restore goodwill associated with the registered trade mark.
primary_entity: infringement or for passing off referred to in section 13 4

context: Where a registered trade mark owner desires to grant a license conferring the right to use the trade mark, such license may be granted either exclusively or non-exclusively, subject to the terms stipulated therein relating to quality control and territorial scope of application. Any assignment of a registered trade mark shall include all rights pertaining to licenses previously granted under this Act, provided that the assignee undertakes to adhere to the conditions of those existing licenses. Failure to maintain such adherence may constitute infringement or for passing off referred to in section 13 4. The Registrar may require disclosure of details regarding any sub-licensing arrangements entered into by a licensee and shall have the power to intervene where such arrangements demonstrably prejudice the reputation of the trade mark. Further, a license granted under this Act is deemed assignable alongside the underlying trade mark registration.
primary_entity: infringement or for passing off referred to in section 13 4

context: Where a proprietor institutes a suit alleging infringement or for passing off referred to in section 13 4, the defendant may, subject to leave granted by the court, counter-claim asserting that the trade mark is invalid under this Act, or has become unregistrable. Such counter-claim shall be deemed a distinct cause of action and the proprietor may file a cross-appeal against any order dismissing their original claim for infringement. The court may, in its discretion, direct separate hearings for the determination of validity and the merits of the alleged infringement. Provided that, if the defendant’s counter-claim is successful, the relief granted to the proprietor shall be limited accordingly. Any party aggrieved by an order made under this provision may appeal to the appellate forum as provided herein.
primary_entity: infringement or for passing off referred to in section 13 4

context: Where a registered trade mark is alleged to be used in relation to goods or services not identical with those in respect of which it is registered, an interested party may institute proceedings before the relevant jurisdictional authority alleging infringement or for passing off referred to in section 13 4. Such proceedings shall be conducted according to the prescribed procedure and rules of evidence applicable under this Act. The authority shall provide a reasonable opportunity to both the trade mark proprietor and the alleged infringer to present their respective cases, including cross-examination of witnesses. Further, an application for cancelling registration may be made by any person claiming interest in the matter, demonstrating that the registered trade mark has become devoid of distinctiveness or has been abandoned through non-use exceeding a specified period as provided herein. The authority shall consider all submissions and evidence before rendering its decision, which shall be final subject to appeal under the prescribed appellate mechanism.
primary_entity: infringement or for passing off referred to in section 13 4

context: Where a proprietor establishes that another has used, in connection with goods or services, a trade mark identical or confusingly similar to his registered trade mark, and such use constitutes infringement or for passing off referred to in section 13 4, the court shall order the cessation of the infringing activity. This includes, but is not limited to, prohibiting the manufacture, advertisement, distribution, and sale of goods bearing the infringing copy. Further, the proprietor may elect to pursue either damages sustained as a direct result of the infringement or an assessment of profits derived from the unauthorized use. The court may also order the destruction of all materials used in connection with the infringing act, subject to regulations regarding hazardous waste disposal. Failure to comply with such orders shall render the offender liable for further penalties and contempt proceedings.
primary_entity: infringement or for passing off referred to in section 13 4

context: Where a registered trade mark is utilized in connection with agricultural produce, the Agriculture Commissioner may grant licenses permitting specified persons to apply for, or use in association with, such produce, a representation substantially identical to the registered mark, provided that such license explicitly defines the geographical area of application and the types of agricultural commodities covered. Any assignment of such license shall be subject to prior approval from the Agriculture Commissioner and must include provisions ensuring continued adherence to quality standards as stipulated within the original licensing agreement. Failure to comply with these conditions constitutes infringement or for passing off referred to in section 13 4, rendering the licensee liable for damages proportionate to the misrepresentation caused to consumers regarding the origin or nature of the agricultural product. The owner of the registered trade mark shall retain ultimate control over quality assurance protocols.
primary_entity: infringement or for passing off referred to in section 13 4

context: Where a proprietor institutes suit alleging infringement or for passing off referred to in section 13 4, the defendant may, subject to leave granted by the court, counter-claim asserting that the trade mark registration is invalid due to prior use of an identical or deceptively similar sign under honest practices. Such counter-claim shall be accompanied by evidence demonstrating continuous and extensive usage predating the date of application for design registry registration relating to the contested mark. The court may require the proprietor to demonstrate ongoing bona fide commercial use of the trade mark, failing which the counter-claimant shall be entitled to a declaration negating the proprietary rights claimed. An appeal from any order granting or refusing leave under this provision lies to the appellate forum as provided herein.
primary_entity: infringement or for passing off referred to in section 13 4

context: For the purposes of this Act, "infringement or for passing off referred to in section 13 4" shall include the use of a trade mark in relation to goods or services which are identical or confusingly similar to those associated with the registered trade mark, irrespective of whether such use occurs within India or abroad. This definition extends to acts that create a false or deceptive impression concerning the origin, sponsorship, or approval of any goods or services. Nothing herein shall restrict remedies available under other laws relating to unfair competition. Farmers engaged in seed saving and exchange, exercising varieties farmers rights as provided herein, are deemed not to infringe unless commercial exploitation occurs beyond customary practices.
primary_entity: infringement or for passing off referred to in section 13 4

context: An aggrieved party, having filed an appeal against any order passed under this Act concerning infringement or threatened infringement of a registered layout-design, shall be required to remit an appeal fee proportionate to the value of the claimed damages and the complexity of the legal issues involved. The appellate authority may, upon application supported by affidavit demonstrating financial hardship, waive or reduce such appeal fee in whole or in part; however, any such waiver is subject to review and may be revoked if it is subsequently determined that the applicant misrepresented their circumstances. Failure to remit the prescribed appeal fee within thirty days of the notice of appeal shall render the appeal void ab initio. Further, where an interlocutory application is made during appellate proceedings, a separate appeal fee accompanied by a reasoned justification for the delay in payment may be imposed at the discretion of the authority.

Where a layout design owner desires to assign or license rights in a registered integrated circuit layout design, the assignment or license agreement shall clearly specify the scope of such rights granted, including but not limited to reproduction, adaptation, and commercial use. The assignee or licensee may further grant sublicenses subject to conditions stipulated within the original agreement and as provided herein. Any party aggrieved by an order passed under this Act relating to infringement or validity of a layout design may institute an appeal to the relevant judicial forum. An appeal fee accompanied by a security deposit equivalent to ten percent of the assessed damages shall be remitted at the time of filing the memorandum of appeal. Failure to remit such fees will render the appeal non-maintainable, subject to exemptions granted by the appellate authority on demonstration of financial hardship.

For the purposes of this Act, a “layout-design” includes any three dimensional representation of an integrated circuit or such other relevant data as may be prescribed. A person claiming to be the first inventor of a layout-design shall have the right to make a filing application with the Controller under this Act for registration thereof. Such filing application must contain particulars relating to the applicant, the layout-design itself, and any prior publication or use of the design. The applicant shall also provide a statement affirming that the layout-design is original and not derived from any existing work, subject to exceptions as provided herein regarding minor modifications. Any false statements within a filing application render it liable for rejection.

An applicant seeking registration of a semiconductor integrated circuit layout-design shall file an application with the Controller in the prescribed form and manner. The application must contain a full and clear representation of the layout, including any necessary technical specifications as determined by the Controller. Such representations may be in the form of drawings, photographs, or other visual media acceptable to the Controller. An applicant shall also provide a statement detailing the nature of the integrated circuit’s functionality and intended use. The filing application must be accompanied by the requisite fee, payable according to regulations prescribed under this Act. Prior publication of the layout-design does not preclude registration, provided that the application is filed within twelve months of such publication. Any alteration to the layout after the initial filing application will require notification to the Controller and may affect eligibility for registration.

An applicant seeking registration of a layout design shall, in the filing application, clearly specify the nature of the integrated circuit and provide detailed schematics demonstrating its unique topological features. The application must be accompanied by requisite fees as prescribed; failure to remit these fees will render the application void. Where an applicant has previously filed an identical or substantially similar layout design, the Controller may reject the subsequent filing application without further notice. Any person aggrieved by a rejection under this Act may appeal to the Intellectual Property Appellate Tribunal within sixty days from the date of communication of the order. The Tribunal shall consider any evidence presented and provide reasons for its decision, which is binding on both the applicant and the Controller. Remedies available include compensation for demonstrable financial loss incurred due to wrongful rejection.

An applicant seeking to obtain protection for a semiconductor integrated circuit layout-design shall file an application with the Controller in such form and containing such information as may be prescribed. The application must include a copy of the layout-design, a statement of the priority claimed, if any, and details regarding the applicant’s entitlement to seek protection under this Act. Where the applicant is not the original creator of the layout-design, the application shall specify the basis for such claim, subject to verification by the Controller. Any alteration or addition to the particulars contained in a filed application is permissible only with the written permission of the Controller and upon payment of the prescribed fee. The Controller may require the applicant to furnish further documentation or clarification deemed necessary for assessment of the filing application. Failure to comply with these requirements may result in rejection of the application as provided herein.

An application for registration of a layout design shall be filed with the Controller in such form as may be prescribed, and shall contain particulars relating to the applicant, including their address for service within India. The application must include a representation of the integrated circuit layout design, accurately depicting all relevant features, accompanied by a written description detailing its functionality and construction. Provided that an applicant who has previously filed an identical application in another country shall disclose such prior filing under this Act. Furthermore, the Controller may require submission of additional documentation to verify compliance with prescribed standards for clarity and completeness; failure to provide said documents within the stipulated timeframe will result in rejection of the filing application.

Any person seeking to obtain registration of a layout-design shall file an application with the Office, in the prescribed form and containing all particulars as provided herein. Failure to comply with the requirements regarding the form or content of such application shall render it liable for rejection without further notice. The Registrar may require amendment of any deficiencies discovered within the filed application; refusal to undertake these amendments constitutes grounds for immediate dismissal. Any person making a false statement in an application, whether material or not, is subject to penalties as determined under this Act and may be required to pay damages to affected parties. Repeated attempts to circumvent procedural requirements during the filing application process will attract enhanced fines.

Where a layout design owner intends to grant a license or assign ownership rights pertaining to an integrated circuit layout design for which a filing application has been made, such transfer shall be documented in a prescribed form and submitted to the Controller. The applicant may execute multiple licenses granting varying degrees of usage rights, including but not limited to reproduction, modification, and distribution, subject to conditions specified within the license agreement. Any assignment of ownership must explicitly state the entirety of rights being transferred and include consideration paid, if any, as provided herein. Further, a copy of such licensing agreements or assignments shall be appended to the original filing application for public record, ensuring transparency regarding permitted uses of the layout design. The Controller may require additional information substantiating the validity of the transfer.

Where an applicant disputes a decision regarding the acceptance or rejection of a filing application for a semiconductor integrated circuit layout-design, such dispute shall be referred to the Controller. The Controller may, after affording the applicant and the relevant authority an opportunity for being heard, pass orders as deemed appropriate, subject to appeal under this Act. Provided that any order passed by the Controller concerning the validity of claims made within the filing application is final and binding, barring appeals solely on grounds of procedural irregularity in the hearing process. The applicant shall be entitled to submit documentary evidence supporting their contention; however, the burden of establishing a material error lies with the appellant. Any appeal against an order under this Act must be filed within ninety days from the date of communication of the order.

The registered owner of a layout design shall be entitled to grant licenses conferring rights to utilize, reproduce, or commercially exploit the said layout design, subject to such terms and conditions as are agreed upon in writing between the parties. Any assignment of ownership of a layout design, whether absolute or conditional, must be executed by way of a deed registered with the Controller General under this Act. A licensee may further assign their rights relating to the licensed use provided that prior written consent is obtained from the original owner and such assignment is also duly recorded. Where disputes arise concerning the validity of a license agreement or an assignment, parties aggrieved may appeal to the Layout Design Appellate Board for redressal, as provided herein. The filing application for registration shall not preclude the registered owner’s ability to enter into licensing agreements prior to grant.

An application for registration, once filed, shall be deemed to be provisionally protected subject to verification as provided herein. Any person aggrieved by a decision regarding the acceptance or rejection of a filing application may appeal to the Intellectual Property Appellate Tribunal within sixty days from the date of communication of such decision. The appellate tribunal shall consider any relevant provisions act mark objections raised during the initial examination process and may, after affording the applicant an opportunity for being heard, confirm, vary, or reverse the order appealed against. Further, a challenge to the validity of registration based on prior publication or use of a similar layout-design design shall be permissible only through an appeal under this Act within one year from the date of such registration.

An application for registration of a layout design shall be accompanied by such particulars as may be prescribed, including detailed schematics and a declaration affirming originality and freedom from prior publication. Upon receipt of an application, the Registrar shall issue an acknowledgment and undertake a preliminary examination to ascertain compliance with the requirements under this Act. If any deficiencies are detected, the applicant shall be notified and afforded an opportunity for rectification within the time specified. Subsequently, the application is deemed to be referred to the Appellate Board sub for consideration regarding novelty assessment and determination of potential conflicts with existing registered layout designs, as provided herein. The Board’s decision on such matters shall be final subject to appeal to the relevant High Court.

Where a registered layout design owner desires to grant a license or assign their rights relating to a protected integrated circuit layout design, such license or assignment shall be in writing and executed by an authorized representative of the owner. The terms of any license granted under this Act may specify the field of use, duration, and geographical extent of the permitted exploitation. Further, where a license is assigned along with the underlying layout design rights, the assignee shall become the exclusive proprietor subject to any continuing obligations stipulated in the original licensing agreement. Any dispute arising concerning the validity or interpretation of such licenses or assignments may be referred to the Appellate Board sub for adjudication and binding determination, as provided herein. The Board’s decision shall be final and conclusive.

Subject to the provisions of this Act, a producer of a registered integrated circuit layout design may grant licenses granting rights to utilize the said layout design for commercial production. Such licenses shall specify the scope of permitted activities, including but not limited to manufacturing, importing, and distributing products incorporating the licensed layout design. Assignment of these licensing rights is permissible, provided that such assignment is documented in writing and registered with the Controller General. The Appellate Board sub-committee may be convened to adjudicate disputes arising from alleged breaches of license agreements or unauthorized assignments, considering factors such as reasonable royalty rates and the extent of infringement. Further, any producer seeking to enforce these provisions must demonstrate valid registration under this Act and adherence to prescribed guidelines relating to layout design protection.

For the purpose of this Act, "prescribed fees" shall mean the amounts specified in Schedule A, which are subject to revision as determined by the Central Government from time to time. The filing application fees for registration of a layout-design shall be remitted electronically or through demand draft payable at [City Name], and deemed paid only upon confirmation of receipt by the Controller General. Any applicant failing to remit the prescribed fees in full shall have their application considered withdrawn, provided that an appeal against such determination may be made to the designated appellate authority within thirty days from the date of notification. The amount of filing application fees is differentiated based on the nature of the applicant as defined under this Act.

An applicant seeking registration of a layout-design shall, upon submission of the application form as provided herein, remit the prescribed filing application fees to the Controller. The amount of such fees shall be determined in accordance with the classification of integrated circuits based on their complexity and manufacturing process, details of which are published by notification in the Official Gazette. Provided that an applicant who is a small enterprise, as defined under the Micro, Small & Medium Enterprises Development Act, may claim a concession in the filing application fees subject to submission of relevant certification documents. Failure to remit the requisite fees within thirty days from the date of acknowledgement of the application shall render the application liable for rejection without further notice. Any fee once paid is non-refundable and cannot be transferred to subsequent applications.

An applicant seeking registration of a layout-design shall remit filing application fees as prescribed in Schedule A, provided that a reduced fee may be levied for applicants qualifying as Small Scale Enterprises under the Micro, Small & Medium Enterprises Development Act. Failure to pay the requisite fees within thirty days from the date of demand shall render the application deemed abandoned and subject to removal from the register of pending applications. Any person aggrieved by an order requiring the payment of filing application fees may appeal to the Controller within sixty days of such order; however, this right of appeal is conditional upon demonstrating demonstrable financial hardship impacting their ability to comply with the fee schedule. The Controller shall consider any submitted evidence and may grant a temporary waiver or installment plan at his discretion.

An applicant seeking registration of a layout design shall remit, along with the filing application fees, a certified copy of any prior publication of the layout design, if such publication has occurred. The prescribed filing application fees are subject to revision as notified by the Controller General from time to time in the Official Gazette. Failure to submit the requisite fees will render the application void ab initio. Where an applicant elects to file multiple applications relating to variations of a single integrated circuit, a reduced fee shall be applicable for each subsequent application filed within a period of six months from the initial filing date, provided that such variations do not constitute substantially new layout designs under this Act. The Controller General may require further documentation substantiating the claim of variation and assess additional fees accordingly. Any refund of filing application fees is discretionary with the Controller General.

An applicant seeking registration of a semiconductor integrated circuit layout-design shall remit filing application fees as prescribed in Schedule A. The amount specified therein is subject to revision, which may be effected by notification published in the Official Gazette. Provided that an applicant who has previously submitted an incomplete application and subsequently furnishes all requisite documentation within ninety days from the date of initial submission shall only be liable for the difference between the original fee and the prevailing rate at the time of complete filing. Failure to remit the prescribed fees, or remittance of insufficient funds, will render the application deemed not filed under this Act. Any refund of such fees is discretionary with the Controller and governed by regulations as may be issued.

Any applicant seeking registration of a layout-design shall, upon filing an application under this Act, remit the prescribed filing application fees as determined by the Central Government. Failure to pay such fees in full at the time of submission will render the application void ab initio and subject the applicant to penalties not exceeding fifty thousand rupees for each instance of non-compliance. Repeated failure to adhere to fee payment schedules may result in a permanent bar from future applications under this Act, as determined by the Controller. The Central Government may, through notification in the Official Gazette, revise these fees periodically, provided that adequate notice is given at least three months prior to implementation. Any person found assisting an applicant in submitting a deficient application shall also be liable for prosecution and penalties.

Where a layout design is assigned or licensed to any person, the assignee or licensee shall be deemed to be the applicant for all purposes under this Act and may, subject to fulfilling all procedural requirements as provided herein, proceed with the filing application fees in respect of such assignment or license. The original registrant shall provide a duly authenticated declaration confirming the validity of the assignment or license agreement, detailing the scope of rights transferred and the duration thereof. This declaration must accompany the initial fee payment by the assignee or licensee. Failure to submit this declaration will result in the rejection of the application. Any subsequent transfer of rights under an existing layout design registration shall be notified to the Controller within thirty days, accompanied by a revised declaration reflecting the new assignment details and relevant fees.

An applicant aggrieved by a decision of the Controller regarding the assessment or refund of filing application fees may, within sixty days from the date of communication of such decision, prefer an appeal to the Intellectual Property Appellate Tribunal. The appeal shall be accompanied by a memorandum stating the grounds of appeal and the relief sought, and subject to payment of such additional fee as may be prescribed. Provided that if the applicant demonstrates undue hardship due to circumstances beyond their reasonable control, the Tribunal may entertain the appeal notwithstanding the delay in its presentation, after hearing arguments from both parties. The Controller shall furnish a copy of all relevant records pertaining to the assessment of filing application fees to the Tribunal within thirty days of receipt of notice of the appeal.

Where an applicant fails to remit the prescribed filing application fees within thirty days from the date specified in the acknowledgment receipt, the Office shall issue a notice affording fifteen days for compliance. Such notice may be served electronically or through registered post. Failure to comply with the notice does not automatically render the application abandoned; however, the Registrar is empowered to initiate proceedings for deemed abandonment subject to an opportunity being afforded to the applicant for reasoned objection. Any order of deemed abandonment shall be appealable before a designated appellate authority and the appellate authority may consider representations regarding financial hardship or inadvertent delay in remitting the filing application fees. For the purposes of this Act, a licence means licence, whether granted gratuitously or for consideration.

An application for registration of a layout design shall be accompanied by fees as prescribed, with the amount varying according to the nature and complexity of the integrated circuit. The fee payable upon initial filing is non-refundable, subject to provisions regarding withdrawal of an application under this Act. Any subsequent payments required during prosecution of the application, such as those relating to examination or grant, shall be detailed in publicly accessible schedules maintained by the Controller General. Disputes concerning the calculation or validity of these filing application fees may be initiated before a District Court having jurisdiction over the place where the applicant maintains its principal place of business.

An applicant seeking registration of a semiconductor integrated circuit layout-design shall remit filing application fees as prescribed in Schedule A, subject to adjustments notified periodically by the Controller. The amount payable shall be determined based on the denomination variety of the layout-design being applied for, with distinct fee structures applying to designs classified as simple, moderate, or complex, according to guidelines issued by the Office. Provided that applicants registered as Small Scale Industrial Undertakings, as defined under this Act, may claim a reduction in filing application fees not exceeding fifty percent, upon submission of relevant certification. Any deficiency in payment shall render the application deemed withdrawn until such time as the outstanding amount is remitted, and further processing will only resume after compliance.

Where a complaint alleging infringement of layout-design rights is received, the Controller shall initiate a procedure investigation to ascertain the facts and circumstances surrounding the alleged violation. Such investigation shall include examination of relevant documents, recording statements from interested parties including the complainant, the accused, and any witnesses identified during the process. The Controller may issue summons requiring attendance and production of evidence as deemed necessary for the purpose of this investigation. Any person failing to comply with a summons issued under this Act is liable to penalties as provided herein. The findings of the procedure investigation shall form the basis for subsequent proceedings relating to infringement claims.

Where an objection is raised against the registration of a layout design, the Controller shall initiate a procedure investigation to ascertain the validity of the claim. This investigation will encompass examination of the layout design documentation submitted and any prior art presented as grounds for rejection. The applicant shall be afforded reasonable opportunity to present their arguments and evidence in response to the objection. Should the Controller deem it necessary during this procedure investigation, they may require further clarification or modifications to the layout design. Any determination made following such an investigation shall be recorded in writing and communicated to all parties involved, subject to appeal as provided herein. The applicant may request a stay of proceedings pending the outcome of the investigation.

Where a complaint alleging infringement of layout-design rights is received, the Controller shall initiate an investigation into the matter. Such investigation may include inspection of premises, examination of persons and documents, and requisitioning of information from relevant parties as deemed necessary to ascertain the facts surrounding the alleged infringement. The complainant shall be afforded reasonable opportunity to present evidence in support of their claim, and the respondent shall similarly have a right to rebut such evidence and submit their own defence. Any party aggrieved by an action taken during the procedure investigation may appeal to the Intellectual Property Appellate Tribunal within sixty days from the date of communication of that action. The Controller shall issue orders based on findings derived from the investigation, providing remedies including injunctions and damages as provided herein.

Where a complaint alleging infringement of layout-design rights is received, the Controller shall initiate an investigation into the matter. Such investigation shall be conducted in accordance with the principles of natural justice and subject to any rules made in this behalf. The Controller may, at his discretion, direct any person having knowledge or expertise relevant to the alleged infringement to assist in the investigation, providing such assistance is not inconsistent with confidentiality obligations. During the course of the procedure investigation, the Controller shall have power to examine witnesses under oath and call for production of documents pertinent to the claim. Any party aggrieved by an order made during this process may appeal to the Intellectual Property Appellate Tribunal within a period specified herein. The findings of the procedure investigation are binding on all parties unless overturned by the Tribunal.

Where a complaint alleging infringement of layout-design rights is received, the Controller shall initiate an investigation in accordance with this Act. Such investigation may be undertaken suo moto or upon application made in the prescribed form, accompanied by evidence reasonably supporting the claim of infringement and payment of the requisite fee. The Controller shall serve notice on the complainant and the alleged infringer, affording each party a reasonable opportunity to present their case and submit documentary evidence. During the procedure investigation, the Controller may examine witnesses under oath or affirmation, and issue summons for production of relevant documents pertaining to the layout-design in question. Findings made during this process are subject to judicial review as provided herein.

Where a complaint alleging infringement of layout-design rights is received, the Controller shall initiate an investigation as provided herein. The investigating officer, appointed by the Controller, may enter any premises and seize materials relevant to the alleged infringement, subject to due process and with appropriate warrants where necessary. Any person obstructing such investigation shall be liable for penalties under this Act. The investigating officer shall record statements from all concerned parties, including the complainant, the accused, and witnesses. Failure to appear before the investigating officer may result in a fine or further action as deemed fit by the Controller. A report detailing findings of the procedure investigation shall be submitted to the Controller within ninety days, with reasons for any delay.

Where a complaint alleging infringement of layout-design rights is received, the Controller shall initiate a procedure investigation to ascertain the veracity of the allegations. Such investigation may include inspection of premises, seizure of materials and examination of witnesses, subject to due process as provided herein. The complainant shall be afforded an opportunity to present evidence in support of their claim, and the alleged infringer shall have the right to rebut such evidence and submit a defence. Any party aggrieved by any action taken during the procedure investigation may appeal to the Intellectual Property Appellate Tribunal within sixty days from the date of communication of that action. The Tribunal’s decision on an appeal under this Act shall be final, subject to further appeal to the Supreme Court.

Where a complaint alleging infringement of layout-design rights is received, the Controller shall initiate a procedure investigation to determine the veracity of such allegations. The complainant shall be afforded an opportunity to present evidence substantiating their claim, and the alleged infringer shall be given a corresponding chance to rebut it. During this investigation, the Controller may examine witnesses under oath and call for relevant documents pertaining to the design in question, including records relating to any patent applications or granted patents claiming similar functionality. Should the Controller find reasonable grounds to believe infringement has occurred, they may issue an order restraining further acts of infringement and directing compensation to be paid by the infringer to the rights holder. The amount of such compensation shall be determined based on the scale of the infringing activity and potential lost profits as a result.

Where a complaint alleging infringement of layout-design rights is received, the Controller shall initiate a procedure investigation to determine prima facie validity. Such investigation may include inspection of premises, seizure of materials and examination of witnesses under oath, subject to due process as provided herein. The Controller shall issue summons requiring production of relevant documents pertaining to the alleged infringing activity or trade mark recognised in connection with the layout-design. Failure to comply with a summons shall render the non-compliant party liable for penalties as prescribed. Any person aggrieved by an order issued during this procedure investigation may appeal to the Intellectual Property Appellate Tribunal within sixty days, provided that such appeal does not suspend the operation of the order.

For the purpose of this Act, an “application fee accompanied” shall mean a sum tendered in conjunction with the formal submission of an application for registration of a layout-design, which sum is determined according to the prescribed rates as notified by the Controller General. Such accompanying fees are deemed integral to the validity of the application and failure to remit the correct amount, or any applicable surcharge, renders the application liable for rejection under this Act. The amount of the application fee accompanied shall be adjusted periodically based on prevailing economic conditions, as provided herein, and such adjustments shall be published in the Official Gazette.

Where an applicant seeks registration of a semiconductor integrated circuit layout-design, an application fee accompanied by a certified copy of any prior publication or exploitation of the layout-design shall be remitted to the Controller. Failure to remit the prescribed application fee will render the application void ab initio and no further proceedings shall be entertained under this Act. The Controller may, at his discretion, permit rectification of deficiencies in an application within a period not exceeding thirty days from the date of communication of such deficiency, provided that any additional fees as determined by regulations made under this Act are paid promptly. Any person aggrieved by an order passed by the Controller relating to the acceptance or rejection of an application may appeal to the Intellectual Property Appellate Tribunal. The appellate tribunal shall have the power to award costs in relation to such appeals.

An applicant seeking registration of a semiconductor integrated circuit layout-design shall, along with the application submitted to the Controller, remit an application fee as prescribed in Schedule A. The amount of said application fee is non-refundable and subject to revision by notification published in the Official Gazette. Provided that, where an applicant is registered as a Small Enterprise under the Micro, Small & Medium Enterprises Development Act, 2006, or as a Start-up as defined under clause (iv) of section 2 of the Startup India Action Plan, they may be eligible for a reduced application fee, upon submission of satisfactory documentary evidence to that effect. The Controller shall verify such documentation and determine eligibility. Failure to submit requisite documentation at the time of application will result in the full prescribed application fee being levied. Any subsequent request for refund of the application fee accompanied by an amended application will not be entertained under any circumstances.

Any person making an application for registration of a layout-design, or for any matter ancillary thereto, shall pay such fee as may be prescribed. Failure to remit the requisite application fee accompanied by proof of payment within thirty days from the date of presentation of the application shall render the application void ab initio. The Controller may, subject to conditions specified in the regulations, entertain an application where the fee is deficient, provided that a request for rectification and full remittance is received within fifteen days of notification of deficiency. Repeated failure to comply with this provision, or providing false information regarding payment status, constitutes an offence punishable with monetary penalties as determined under this Act. The Controller shall maintain records of all fees paid and may conduct audits to ensure compliance.

Where an applicant seeks registration of a layout design, an application fee accompanied by certified copies of the drawings or plans constituting the layout design shall be remitted to the Controller. The amount of such fee is prescribed in Schedule A and may be revised from time to time through notification published in the Official Gazette. Failure to remit the correct application fee will render the application void ab initio, subject to provisions act shall allow for a period of thirty days for rectification upon written request demonstrating sufficient cause. Any person aggrieved by an order refusing registration or revoking registration may appeal to the Intellectual Property Appellate Tribunal within sixty days from the date of communication of such order. The remedies available under this Act include injunctions restraining infringement and damages proportionate to the loss suffered, provided that contributory infringement is actionable as provided herein.

Subject to the provisions of this Act, copyright in a work shall vest initially in the author thereof, but where such work is created during the course of employment, or for consideration paid by another person, the conditions subject copyright may vary as determined by registration. An application for registration of copyright shall specify the nature of the work and details pertaining to its creation, including whether it was generated under a contractual agreement assigning rights. The Registrar shall maintain a public record of all registered copyrights, accessible upon payment of prescribed fees. Any person claiming ownership different from that indicated in the initial authorship shall be required to demonstrate such claim through documentary evidence submitted during registration proceedings.

Subject to the provisions of this Act, copyright shall subsist in a work fixed in a tangible medium of expression only if such fixation is undertaken with due regard for existing contractual obligations. Where an author has assigned their copyright in a work to another party, subsequent reproduction or communication to the public of that work shall be deemed conditional upon adherence to the terms stipulated within the assignment agreement. Any alteration made to the original work without express written consent from the assignee, as documented and filed with the designated Copyright Office, will render such actions infringing under this Act. The Registrar may issue directives regarding the proper registration of assignment agreements pertaining to copyright ownership. Furthermore, any dispute arising concerning the conditions subject copyright shall be adjudicated by a competent civil court exercising jurisdiction in accordance with established legal procedures.

Subject to the provisions of this Act, copyright shall subsist in a work created by an author who is employed under a contract of service, but the conditions subject copyright therein shall be determined solely by the terms of that contract. Where such a contract contains stipulations restricting or expanding the scope of copyright ownership beyond the ordinarily permissible limits as provided herein, those stipulations shall be binding on both parties unless they are demonstrably unconscionable at the time of execution. Any dispute arising concerning the interpretation of such contractual provisions may be referred to arbitration in accordance with the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996; however, any party aggrieved by an arbitral award may appeal to the High Court within ninety days of its pronouncement.

Subject to the provisions of this Act relating to fair dealing, copyright in a three-dimensional design embodied in an Integrated Circuit layout shall subsist exclusively with the owner of that layout. However, where such layout is substantially derived from a pre-existing work protected under this Act, the conditions subject copyright therein are deemed to be those applicable to the original work. It shall be open to any aggrieved party to demonstrate before the relevant judicial forum that the alleged substantial derivation does not constitute infringement, provided that such demonstration establishes independent creation or other permissible justification as may be prescribed. The burden of proving absence of substantial similarity rests upon the claimant asserting non-infringement.

Subject to the provisions of this Act, copyright shall not subsist in any work which is certified by the Registrar of Copyrights as being primarily derived from traditional knowledge relating to folklore or indigenous art forms. For the purposes of this section, "traditional knowledge" includes knowledge, innovations and practices of indigenous communities that are passed down through generations. The Registrar may issue a certificate upon receiving an application demonstrating such derivation and establishing the source community’s consent for adaptation. Any work so certified shall be deemed to have conditions subject copyright, restricting commercial exploitation without prior authorization from the designated cultural custodians as specified in the certificate.

An entry register shall be maintained at the Patents Office for each patent granted under this Act and shall contain particulars relating to the application, grant, renewal, assignment, modification, and lapse of such patents. Every entry made in the entry register shall be deemed conclusive proof of the facts recorded therein subject to any appeal or revision as provided herein. The Controller may, at his discretion, prescribe the form and manner in which entries are recorded within the entry register; however, all entries must accurately reflect the official record pertaining to each patent. Any person aggrieved by an incorrect entry shall have recourse to remedies available under this Act.

The Controller shall maintain a comprehensive entry register for all registered designs, detailing particulars relating to each design’s registration and subsequent modifications. This entry register shall include, but not be limited to, the date of application, the name and address of the claimant, details of any prior published descriptions, and the prescribed fees paid. Further, every alteration or amendment to a registered design, including changes in ownership or variations to the design itself, must be recorded promptly within the entry register. The public shall have access to inspect this entry register during specified office hours, subject to reasonable restrictions as may be determined by the Controller. Any person aggrieved by an inaccurate entry may apply for rectification, and such applications will be processed according to procedures prescribed herein.

Where an application for a patent is granted under this Act, the Controller shall maintain an entry register detailing all particulars pertaining to the grant, including the date of publication of the invention and the name(s) of the applicant(s). This entry register shall be accessible for public inspection during prescribed office hours, subject to reasonable restrictions as determined by the Controller. Any person aggrieved by any entry made in the entry register may prefer an appeal to the Appellate Board within a period of sixty days from the date on which such entry was made, provided that the grounds of appeal are clearly articulated and supported by relevant documentation. Failure to comply with prescribed procedures during this appeal process may result in dismissal of the same. The Controller shall have the power to rectify any errors or omissions appearing in the entry register upon receiving a written request accompanied by supporting evidence.

The Controller shall maintain an entry register for each patent application and granted patent, recording all procedural acts undertaken under this Act, including but not limited to filing dates, examination requests, notices issued, and decisions rendered. Such entry register shall be deemed conclusive evidence of the actions recorded therein, subject to any demonstrable error or fraud proven before the Intellectual Property Appellate Board. The Controller may, at his discretion, provide electronic access to portions of the entry register, provided that appropriate security measures are implemented to prevent unauthorized modification or deletion of data. Any person aggrieved by an action recorded in the entry register may appeal under this Act. The entry register shall be preserved for a period not less than ten years from the date of grant of patent or abandonment of application, as applicable.

Where an application for a patent is filed relating to an invention comprising one or more biological materials, the Controller shall maintain a separate entry register specifically pertaining to such applications. This entry register shall record details including, but not limited to, the date of filing, the applicant’s name and address, the nature of the biological material involved, and any modifications made thereto during examination. The information recorded in this entry register is subject to periodic review by a designated committee appointed under this Act. Any alteration or addition to an existing entry shall be clearly indicated with the date and signature of the officer responsible. Access to this entry register may be restricted where national security concerns arise, as provided herein.

An application for rectification of an entry in the Patents Register may be made by any party claiming interest under this Act; and such application shall specify the particulars of the entry sought to be rectified and the grounds on which it is claimed that the entry is erroneous or contrary to law. The Controller, after affording opportunity of being heard to all interested parties, may order rectification accordingly. Any person aggrieved by an order made under this provision may appeal to the Appellate Board within a period of sixty days from the date of such order. Failure to comply with any direction issued by the Controller in relation to the entry register shall be deemed a cognizable offence and subject to penalties as provided herein.

Where a patentee elects to grant a license or assign their patent rights under this Act, the terms and conditions governing such licenses and assignments shall be recorded in an entry register maintained by the Controller. Such recording is mandatory where the consideration involves royalty payments exceeding ten percent of the net sales derived from the patented invention’s commercial exploitation. The entry register shall clearly specify the scope of exclusivity granted to the licensee, including geographical limitations and field of use restrictions, as agreed upon between the patentee and the assignee. Any subsequent modification or termination of such licenses or assignments must also be documented in the entry register within thirty days of the event occurring. Failure to record these alterations may render them unenforceable against third parties. The Controller shall publish notice of entries made in the entry register in a manner prescribed herein.

The Controller shall maintain an entry register for each patent application and granted patent, recording all procedural steps undertaken under this Act, including but not limited to requests for amendment, objections raised by third parties, and decisions rendered regarding novelty or inventive step. This entry register shall be accessible for inspection by any interested party upon payment of the prescribed fee, subject to restrictions imposed where such access would prejudice the interests of national security or trade secrets as determined by the Controller. Any person aggrieved by an inaccurate or incomplete record in the entry register may file a written objection with the Controller within sixty days of the relevant action; and the Controller shall consider such objections and make necessary corrections, providing reasons for any refusal to amend. Appeals against decisions regarding entries in the register lie before the Intellectual Property Appellate Board.

Subject to compliance with regulations framed under this Act, an applicant for registration of a geographical indication shall furnish three certified true copies of the map delineating the geographical territory to which the indication pertains. Such maps must clearly identify boundaries and relevant topographical features as determined by a recognized surveying authority. The Controller General may require further clarification or amendment of said maps if deemed necessary for accurate recordation. Furthermore, the register said geographical indications shall contain an entry register detailing all applications received, registrations granted, and any modifications made to registered indications. This entry register shall be maintained electronically and periodically updated, ensuring accessibility as provided herein.

Where a patent relates to an invention involving semiconductor technology, the Controller may, upon application by the patentee or assignee, direct that an entry register be maintained separately for recording assignments and licenses relating solely to such rights. This entry register shall contain particulars of every assignment or license granted, including the names and addresses of all parties involved, the extent of the rights transferred, and the consideration paid, if any. Any subsequent assignment of a licensed right under this Act shall also be recorded in the said entry register. The Controller may prescribe fees for recording entries in such an entry register. Provided that no license or assignment is deemed valid against third parties unless it has been duly recorded as provided herein.

The Controller shall maintain an entry register pertaining to all applications for patents relating to inventions involving processes for the manufacture of use certification trade marks, and such entry register shall record particulars including but not limited to the date of filing, applicant details, claims submitted, and examination reports issued. Any party aggrieved by any entry or omission in the entry register may within sixty days from the date on which such entry is made, file an appeal before the Appellate Board, subject to payment of the prescribed fee; provided that the appellate authority shall consider only those grounds specifically alleging errors of fact or law appearing in the record. The Controller’s decision regarding entries shall be final, unless overturned by the Appellate Board.

Subject to the provisions of this Act and rules made thereunder, a person claiming an interest in a patent may apply for registration of a licence patent relating to the granted patent. Such application shall be accompanied by a certified copy of the original patent grant and a detailed statement specifying the scope and terms of the proposed licence agreement. The Controller may require further clarification or documentation regarding the royalty rates stipulated within the licence, ensuring they are equitable to both the patentee and the licensee. Registration of a licence patent shall confer upon the registered licensee the right to exploit the patented invention as defined in the registered agreement, provided that such exploitation does not exceed the terms explicitly outlined therein. Any modification to the licensed technology requires prior approval from the Controller.

Where a patentee grants a licence patent conferring upon the licensee the right to make, use, exercise and vend an invention in India, such licence shall be subject to the terms and conditions stipulated therein. The patentee may enforce any covenants contained within the licence agreement against the licensee under this Act, provided that such enforcement does not impede the lawful exercise of the licensed rights. Any dispute arising from a breach of contract relating to a licence patent shall be adjudicated in accordance with ordinary principles of contractual law, subject to provisions regarding revocation proceedings as provided herein. The Controller may, upon application by any interested party alleging unreasonable terms within a licence agreement restricting competition or hindering access to the patented invention, inquire into the fairness and reasonableness of such terms.

Subject to the provisions of this Act and rules made thereunder, a patentee may grant a licence patent conferring on the licensee specified rights to make, use, exercise, sell, or import the protected invention. Such licences shall be granted in writing and may specify the field of exploitation, duration, and any royalties payable. An application for compulsory revocation of a licence patent under this Act may be made by any interested person demonstrating that the terms and conditions of the licence have been violated by the licensee, or that the licensee has otherwise acted contrary to the provisions of the agreement. The Controller shall give notice to both the patentee and the licensee before proceeding with any inquiry relating to such an application. Further, the Controller may require the parties to submit evidence and arguments pertaining to the alleged breach.

A licensee under a patent granted under this Act shall be entitled to exploit the patented invention to the extent specified in the licence agreement, subject to compliance with all conditions stipulated therein. The licensor may, provided that such action does not contravene any provision of the licence agreement or impede the licensee’s lawful exploitation of the patent, pursue remedies for infringement against parties other than the licensee. Any modification to the scope or duration of a licence patent shall require the written consent of both the licensor and the licensee, and notification thereof to the Controller. Further, the Controller may inquire into any dispute concerning the terms of the licence agreement if it appears that the interests of innovation or public access are adversely affected by its operation, as provided herein.

Any licensee operating under a licence patent shall be deemed an assignee for the purposes of actions relating to infringement of the patent in suit, and may institute such proceedings as if they were the registered proprietor. Provided that, where the licensor elects to pursue any action concerning infringement, the licensee shall not thereafter initiate parallel proceedings unless expressly authorized by the licensor in writing. Failure to obtain prior written consent from the licensor before commencing independent enforcement actions shall constitute a material breach of the licence agreement and render the licensee liable for damages equivalent to three times the royalties paid under the patent during the period of unauthorized action, subject to judicial review. The Controller may order cessation of such proceedings deemed prejudicial to the interests of the patent holder.

Subject to the provisions of this Act and rules made thereunder, a patentee may grant a licence patent conferring upon the licensee specified rights to make, use, exercise, sell, or import the protected invention. Such licence shall be in writing and clearly define the scope of the licensed territory and the duration of the license agreement. The patentee retains full ownership of the patent unless expressly assigned by deed, and may grant multiple licences concurrently without requiring consent from existing licensees. Any assignment of a patent, including assignments arising from a licence patent, requires registration with the Controller and shall be deemed invalid if not so registered within six months of the date of execution. The terms of a licence patent are governed by contract law principles, provided that such terms do not contravene any provisions relating to public interest or anti-competitive practices as may be prescribed under this Act.

Where a patentee grants a licence patent conferring rights to use an invention under this Act, any dispute arising regarding the scope or validity of such licence may be referred to arbitration as provided herein. The arbitral tribunal shall have the power to determine whether the terms of the licence are consistent with the provisions relating to equitable trade practices and restraint of abuse. Subject to appeal to the High Court on a point of law, the award of the arbitral tribunal shall be final and binding upon both the patentee and the licensee. It is provided that an application for revocation of the main patent may not be entertained if it is based solely on grounds arising from the terms of the licence patent granted by the patentee.

Subject to the provisions of this Act and rules made thereunder, a patentee may grant a licence patent conferring upon the licensee specified rights to make, use, exercise, sell, or import the protected invention. Such licences shall be assignable in accordance with the procedures prescribed under this Act, provided that any assignment of a licence patent requires prior notification to the Controller, detailing the terms and conditions thereof. The central government shall have the power to determine whether such assignments are prejudicial to public interest, particularly concerning access to essential medicines or technologies. Further, where a licence patent includes provisions relating to compulsory licensing or further sub-licensing, these clauses must be explicitly stated within the agreement and registered with the Controller. Any modification of the terms of a licence patent requires consent from both parties and subsequent registration.

An application for registration of a geographical indication shall be accompanied by a map of the area from which the goods originate, clearly delineating the boundaries of the geographical territory. The applicant shall also provide a statement detailing the qualities, reputation or other characteristics of the goods attributable to its origin, as well as the production methods employed within that defined geographical region. Where an application relates to agricultural products, viticultural products or foodstuffs, evidence demonstrating the traditional nature of such production practices may be submitted in support of the claim. The Registrar may require further clarification regarding any aspect of the application concerning the distinctive qualities linked to the geographical indication goods and their connection to the specified territory.

An application for the registration of a geographical indication shall be filed with the Registrar in such form and containing such particulars as may be prescribed. The applicant shall furnish evidence demonstrating that the quality, reputation or other characteristic of the goods originates from the specified geographical area. Where an objection is raised by any interested party under this Act against the proposed registration, the Registrar shall provide the applicant with a reasonable opportunity to submit its response in writing and be heard. The Registrar may require the production of further documentation substantiating the link between the goods and the geographical origin. Any alteration or modification to the registered geographical indication is subject to approval by the Registrar, provided that such changes do not affect the essential qualities associated with the geographical indication goods.

An application for registration as a geographical indication shall be accompanied by a certified map delineating the territorial boundaries of the area from which the goods originate, and this map must accurately reflect the traditional production zone. The Registrar may reject an application if the proposed name does not exclusively identify the agricultural product, foodstuff, wine, spirit or other product for which it is sought, or if the applicant fails to demonstrate a continuous link between the quality, reputation or characteristics of the goods and their origin within that geographical area. Further, any collective body applying under this Act must provide evidence of its representative nature amongst producers concerned with the geographical indication goods, subject to verification by the Registrar.

The proprietor of a registered geographical indication relating to tea may grant non-exclusive licenses conferring the right to use the indication on tea products meeting specified quality standards as provided herein. Such licenses shall be documented in writing and filed with the Registrar within thirty days of their execution, detailing the scope of permitted usage, duration, and any royalties payable. Assignment of rights under a geographical indication registration may occur only with the prior consent of the Central Government, ensuring continued adherence to production norms established for that particular geographical indication goods. Any subsequent owner acquiring such assignment shall be bound by all conditions precedent applicable to the original proprietor’s license agreements. The Registrar may, after due inquiry and subject to principles of natural justice, refuse registration of an assignment deemed detrimental to the reputation or distinctiveness of the registered geographical indication.

An appeal lies to the Intellectual Property Appellate Board from any order passed under this Act relating to the registration of a geographical indication goods, provided that the appeal is made within sixty days from the date of receipt of the order by the appellant. The Board may, after giving an opportunity of being heard to all parties concerned, confirm, modify or reverse the order appealed against. Any party aggrieved by any decision of the Intellectual Property Appellate Board may further appeal to the Supreme Court on a question of law arising out of the said decision. It shall be open for the proprietor of a registered geographical indication goods to institute suit in a court of competent jurisdiction for infringement thereof, subject to such conditions as may be prescribed.

Any proprietor of a registered geographical indication shall be entitled to institute civil proceedings for infringement under this Act and may seek remedies including an injunction restraining the use of the geographical indication or any confusingly similar indicator. Provided that where the alleged infringer has used a reference geographical indication, as defined herein, in good faith prior to the date of registration of the impugned geographical indication, and such use does not constitute unfair competition, relief under this Act may be granted subject to conditions determined by the relevant intellectual property tribunal. Damages shall be awarded to the proprietor for any loss suffered due to the infringement, taking into account factors including the extent of the infringing activity and the impact on the reputation of the geographical indication goods. Costs associated with litigation shall also be recoverable as provided herein.

A geographical indication, as provided herein, shall mean an indication which identifies goods originating from a specific territory or region where a quality, reputation, or other characteristic is essentially attributable to its geographical origin. For the purposes of this Act, a "geographical indication plaintiff" means any association representing the interests of producers whose goods bear the proposed geographical indication, or any person authorized by such an association to file for registration. Such authorization shall be evidenced in writing and filed with the Registrar. The geographical indication plaintiff may include cooperatives, trade unions, or other organizations engaged in promoting the production or marketing of goods conforming to the standards as defined under this Act.

An application for registration as a geographical indication shall be accompanied by a map of the area from which the goods originate, clearly delineating its boundaries. The Registrar may require the applicant to furnish further particulars regarding the quality, reputation or other characteristics of the goods, establishing their connection with the geographical origin specified in the application. Where an objection is raised against registration on grounds that the name indicates agricultural products exclusively produced in a territory outside India, the applicant shall be afforded an opportunity for a hearing under this Act. A successful *geographical indication plaintiff* seeking to protect the distinctiveness of the indication may apply for rectification of the register if it appears to them that any registered geographical indication is being used in a manner contrary to the provisions herein.

Any registered proprietor of a geographical indication shall be entitled to institute proceedings for relief against any person or entity infringing their exclusive right under this Act. Such infringement includes, but is not limited to, the unauthorized use of the geographical indication in connection with goods or services not conforming to the standards established for that indication, or the misrepresentation that goods originate from the specified geographic area. The remedies available to a geographical indication plaintiff shall include an injunction restraining further infringing activity and the recovery of damages sustained by reason of such infringement. Provided that, where the defendant proves they were unaware of the registration and had no reasonable ground for belief in its validity, the court may limit or deny the award of compensatory damages. Further, any goods bearing a false or deceptive indication are liable to be seized and destroyed as provided herein.

An application for registration as a geographical indication shall be accompanied by a certified copy of the resolution passed by the proprietor or producers authorizing him to file the application on their behalf, provided that such authorization shall specify the territorial limits from which the goods originate. The Registrar may require the applicant to furnish further particulars concerning the quality and characteristics of the goods, including details regarding traditional production methods employed in relation to those goods. Where an objection is raised against the registration of a geographical indication by any person claiming an interest, that person shall be deemed a *geographical indication plaintiff* for the purposes of this Act and may pursue remedies as provided herein. The Registrar shall provide the applicant and the geographical indication plaintiff with an opportunity to present their respective arguments in writing. Decisions regarding objections shall be published in the Geographical Indications Journal.

An application for registration as a geographical indication shall be deemed admissible only if it is accompanied by an affidavit, duly sworn before a Magistrate or Notary Public, verifying inter alia that the applicant fulfills all conditions stipulated under this Act concerning eligibility. The Registrar may require further documentation demonstrating exclusive rights to use the geographical indication within a defined territory, provided that such territory corresponds substantially with the geographical boundaries of the area from which the goods originate. Any person claiming to be a *geographical indication plaintiff* and alleging misuse or imitation shall furnish evidence establishing prior customary usage by producers in the specified region for at least three generations; failure to do so renders the claim non-maintainable, subject to appeal before the Appellate Board.

Any person claiming to be a *geographical indication plaintiff* aggrieved by the use of any registered or unregistered geographical indication in relation to goods, or by the application of a geographical indication in a manner likely to deceive or cause confusion, may institute a suit in the competent civil court. Such suits shall be actionable only upon proof of actual damages sustained or likely to be sustained as a direct result of such use or application. The Court may grant an injunction restraining any person from using the geographical indication complained of, provided that it is satisfied that such use constitutes unfair competition or detrimental impact on the reputation of the registered good. Failure to comply with an order under this Act shall render the offender liable for penalties as determined by the court and subject to further action including recovery of costs incurred by the geographical indication plaintiff.

Subject to the provisions of this Act, any registered proprietor of a geographical indication shall be entitled to grant licenses relating to the use of such indication. Such license may be exclusive or non-exclusive, and may relate to specific goods or classes of goods associated with the geographical indication. The terms and conditions of any such license shall be determined solely by agreement between the proprietor and the licensee, provided that such terms do not contravene the principles of fair trade as understood under this Act. A registered proprietor may assign their rights relating to a geographical indication, including licenses granted thereunder, to another person or entity with the prior consent of the Registrar. Any geographical indication plaintiff seeking enforcement of these assignment provisions must demonstrate adherence to established protocols for notification and recordation.

Subject to appeal to the Intellectual Property Appellate Tribunal, an action brought by a *geographical indication plaintiff* alleging misuse of a registered geographical indication shall be deemed frivolous if the Registrar determines, after providing the defendant with a reasonable opportunity for being heard, that the alleged use does not create confusion amongst consumers regarding the origin of the goods. The Tribunal may, upon review, uphold, vary, or reverse the Registrar’s determination as provided herein. Further, any order made under this Act concerning rectification of the register shall be subject to judicial review by a High Court within whose territorial jurisdiction the geographical indication is situated. A defendant found guilty of misuse may petition the Intellectual Property Appellate Tribunal for reconsideration if new evidence emerges demonstrating lack of consumer confusion.

An application for registration of a geographical indication shall be accompanied by such particulars as may be prescribed, including detailed information regarding the qualities, reputation or other characteristics which are attributable to the origin of the goods. The Registrar case shall consider whether the proposed name conforms with the provisions relating to distinctive character and freedom from deceptive practices under this Act. Where an objection is raised against registration on grounds that the geographical indication is non-distinctive, the applicant may submit evidence rebutting such objection. A geographical indication plaintiff seeking rectification of a registered geographical indication must demonstrate demonstrable prejudice resulting from the erroneous registration.
