Any unauthorized commercial use of registered works, including derivative creations, constitutes infringement copyright work and is subject to remedies available under this Act. Provided that fair dealing defences shall apply as provided herein, but only where such dealings do not substantially detract from the marketability of the original work.

Any reproduction of a substantial portion of a cinematograph film, including its musical score, shall constitute infringement copyright work unless such reproduction is undertaken for private and non-commercial use or with due authorization from the copyright holder. Provided that, where a layout design of an integrated circuit has been registered as a semiconductor integrated circuit layout design under this Act, any unauthorized adaptation of that design to create another layout design, intended for commercial exploitation, shall be deemed an act of infringement impacting the underlying copyright in the film’s artistic elements. Further, the Registrar Semiconductor may, upon application by a concerned party demonstrating reasonable grounds, issue interim orders restraining actions alleged to constitute such infringement pending final determination under this Act.

Any person found to have made a false statement or suppressed material information in respect of an application patent shall be liable to pay a pecuniary penalty not exceeding five hundred thousand rupees, and such amount may be recovered by civil suit. Where the Controller finds that any applicant has misrepresented the prior art during the examination process, the application may be rejected without further consideration under this Act. Further, any individual or entity complicit in facilitating such misrepresentation shall also face a similar penalty, subject to due process of law. The burden of proving compliance with the requirements for an application patent accordance rests entirely upon the applicant and their representatives. Repeated violations will result in revocation of granted patents as provided herein.

For the purposes of this Act, an “application india filed” shall mean an application for a patent which is first received by the Controller under section 10 and wherein the applicant has their domicile or place of business within India. Such an application shall be deemed to disclose the state of the art as it exists prior to the date on which the application was made available to the public anywhere in the world, subject to any claim for priority under this Act. An application india filed may contain provisional and complete specifications as prescribed herein, provided that the complete specification complies with all requirements outlined regarding clarity and enablement.

An application india filed for an invention relating to a novel process for the extraction of bioactive compounds from traditional medicinal plants shall be deemed incomplete if it does not include certified copies of all prior publications, including but not limited to journal articles and conference proceedings, which disclose information relevant to the claimed subject matter. The Controller may require the applicant to furnish further particulars regarding the origin and authenticity of such plant material used in the invention, provided that this requirement shall be waived where the applicant demonstrates compliance with established protocols for sustainable harvesting practices. Any request for amendment to the claims after the first examination shall be permissible only if it clarifies the scope of protection sought and does not introduce new matter beyond what is disclosed in the original application india filed.

Where an applicant has filed an application in India for a patent relating to a process or composition for the manufacture of a substance and subsequently discovers that the invention disclosed is not novel, the Controller may, subject to due notice being given to the applicant, grant a certificate of postponement. This certificate shall remain valid until the expiration of a period of six months from the date of publication of an advertisement in a trade journal specifying the particulars of the application india filed and the reasons for the postponement. During this period, the applicant may submit arguments or evidence demonstrating the novelty of the invention. Failure to do so within that timeframe will result in the application being deemed abandoned. Any person aggrieved by such a decision may appeal to the Appellate Board within sixty days from the date of communication of the order.

An application india filed for a patentable invention shall contain a clear and concise description of the invention sufficient to enable any person skilled in the art to put it into practice. The applicant shall furnish particulars relating to the priority claim, if any, asserted in the application, including the date of earliest filing and details of the earlier application. Where an application incorporates subject matter derived from more than one prior publication or previously filed application, a statement identifying such sources must be included with the application india filed. The Controller may require further clarification regarding the derivation of the invention if deemed necessary for examination purposes. Any alteration to the priority claim after the initial filing shall be accompanied by an affidavit explaining the reasons for the change and demonstrating its compliance with the provisions under this Act relating to priority.

An application india filed relating to a process for producing a novel pharmaceutical intermediate shall be deemed invalid if the applicant has previously published or publicly disclosed the invention outside India unless such publication or disclosure was made under conditions preventing exploitation of the patented subject matter. The Controller may, upon receiving an objection from any interested party regarding prior publication, require the applicant to furnish evidence demonstrating that the publication did not compromise the novelty and inventive step requirements as provided herein. Further, if the application incorporates subject matter derived from a previously filed application india filed by another person, the applicant must provide written consent from the original applicant confirming the transfer of rights and acknowledging compliance with all relevant provisions concerning divisional applications.

An application india filed after the expiration of a period of three years from the date of first publication of the invention anywhere in the world shall not be entertained unless the applicant satisfies the Controller, subject to appeal under this Act, that there existed exceptional circumstances which prevented such filing within the stipulated timeframe. Failure to demonstrate these exceptional circumstances will render the application liable for rejection and any fees paid towards processing it are forfeit to the government. Furthermore, where an invention is disclosed as being derived from a previously published work, the applicant must provide documented evidence demonstrating independent creation or substantial modification; otherwise, infringement proceedings initiated by third parties may be pursued with full legal recourse as provided herein.

An applicant for a patent who has entered into an agreement whereby rights to the invention are assigned or licensed to another party shall, within thirty days of such assignment or licensing arrangement being executed, file with the Controller a certified copy of the said agreement. This requirement applies irrespective of whether the application india filed was originally pursued by the inventor or their assignee. The Controller may require further details regarding the terms and conditions of any license granted, particularly concerning royalty rates and exclusivity provisions. Provided that such assignment or licensing does not prejudice existing third-party rights, the Controller shall register the change in ownership or permitted use as provided herein. Failure to comply with this provision will render the assignee liable for a penalty, and may impact their ability to enforce patent rights under this Act.

Where an application india filed relates to a process for producing a substance or article, and such process involves more than one stage, the Controller may require the applicant to specify each stage of the process in detail. Any party aggrieved by such requirement may appeal under this Act to the Appellate Board within sixty days from the date of communication of the said requirement. The Appellate Board shall hear arguments presented by both the applicant and the aggrieved party, considering whether the request for detailed specification is unduly burdensome or impedes the ascertainment of patentability as provided herein. Further, if the Controller finds that the applicant has failed to adequately respond to such a requirement, the application may be deemed abandoned subject to further appeal.

Where an application india filed for a patent relates to an invention which incorporates technology subject to existing licenses granted under this Act or prior assignments, the applicant shall provide detailed particulars of such licenses and assignments. The Controller General may require the applicant to notify all relevant licensees and assignees of the pending application, providing them with reasonable opportunity to raise objections or claim rights pertaining to the invention. Such notification shall include a summary of the claims as presently formulated in the patent application. Provided that where an objection is raised by a licensee asserting ownership based on a prior assignment, the Controller may require further evidence substantiating the validity and scope of such assignment under this Act. The applicant shall be obligated to cooperate with the Controller in facilitating communication between the parties involved, ensuring fairness and transparency throughout the examination process.

Where an application india filed contains claims diverging substantially from the disclosure within the complete specification as originally presented, and a notice of objection is served upon the applicant under this Act, the Controller may require the proprietor proposed registered to demonstrate a clear and consistent nexus between each such claim and the matter disclosed. Failure to provide satisfactory justification for said divergence, or where the Controller deems the claimed invention not to be fairly based on the original disclosure, shall render the application liable for rejection. An appeal against this decision lies to the Appellate Board, subject to the provisions regarding timelines and procedural requirements as provided herein, and the Board’s determination shall be final.

An application india filed relating to an invention shall be deemed to be incomplete if it does not include a statement specifying the class or classes to which the invention relates and its field of application. For the purposes of this Act, "field of application" means the technical area where the claimed invention is intended to be used or applied. Where an application india filed concerns a product or process that incorporates a geographical indication registered under this Act, the applicant shall disclose in the specification how the invention relates to and utilizes said geographical indication. This disclosure shall not confer any right over the geographical indication itself, as provided herein.

An applicant seeking registration of a utility model shall furnish a detailed record of the invention, including diagrams and descriptions sufficient to enable a person skilled in the art to reproduce the same. The Controller may require further clarification or amendments to the submitted documentation prior to proceeding with examination. For the purpose of determining novelty and inventive step, the *date filing application* is paramount; any publication or public disclosure made by the applicant or their successors in title prior to this date shall be deemed anticipatory and preclude registration unless an exception as provided herein applies. The record must clearly indicate the intended field of use for the utility model and specify any essential components or processes involved in its operation. Failure to comply with these requirements may result in rejection of the application.

Where an applicant has filed multiple applications claiming priority from a common earlier application, and it is determined under this Act that any of the later-filed applications do not fairly disclose the subject matter claimed as compared to the earliest application, the Controller may require the applicant to amend the claims to ensure consistency. Such amendment shall be permissible only if the amended claims are supported by the disclosure in the earliest application. Failure to comply with such a requirement within the time specified will render the later-filed applications liable for abandonment. The date filing application is crucial in establishing priority, and any deliberate attempt to obscure or misrepresent this date through multiple filings constitutes an offense punishable under this Act. Further, remedies including injunctions may be sought by aggrieved parties demonstrating prejudice arising from such deceptive practices.

For the purposes of determining patentability under this Act, the date of filing an application is a critical determinant. Where an applicant elects to disclose information relating to prior publications or public uses made before the date filing application, such disclosure shall be taken into account when assessing novelty and inventive step. An applicant may submit a request for extension of time for complying with requirements pertaining to the preparation of the patent specification; however, any such extension granted shall not affect the priority claim based on the original date filing application. The Controller General may, upon receiving an objection regarding the validity of a claimed invention referencing prior art discovered after the date filing application, direct a hearing to be held for consideration of the matter. It is provided that the applicant bears the burden of demonstrating the inventive merit notwithstanding any such post-filing disclosures.

Where an applicant seeks to amend a patent application after the initial date filing application, such amendment shall only be permissible if it does not alter the nature of the invention as originally disclosed. The Controller may allow amendments provided they are merely clerical or typographical in character, or clarify the description without introducing any new matter. Further, any amendment sought subsequent to publication under this Act requires prior approval from the Controller and must satisfy that the amended claims remain consistent with the disclosure present within the original application. Failure to comply with these conditions will render the amended patent susceptible to challenge during opposition proceedings, as provided herein.

Where an applicant fails to comply with the requirements regarding the statement of inventorship as provided herein, or where any alteration is made to such statement after the date filing application without prior approval from the Controller, the patent shall be deemed invalid. Any person aggrieved by a decision relating to the validity of a patent under this Act may appeal to the Appellate Board within sixty days of the order. The Controller may, upon receiving evidence suggesting fraudulent misrepresentation concerning the inventorship or the date filing application, initiate inquiries and may require the applicant to furnish further documentation. Failure to do so shall render the application liable for rejection. Penalties for false statements regarding the invention’s priority date will be subject to fines not exceeding five hundred thousand rupees.

Where an invention relating to a process for producing a substance has been patented under this Act and the patentee desires to grant a license or assign the rights pertaining thereto, the determination of the effective date of such licensing agreement shall be predicated upon the original date filing application. Provided that, if the assignment incorporates provisions concerning ongoing research and development related to improvements on the invention, the assignee may, subject to fulfilling all conditions precedent as stipulated herein, claim priority for subsequent patent applications arising from said research, referencing the initial date filing application as a basis for novelty assessment. Further, any transfer of rights shall be recorded with the Controller General within three months; failure to do so renders such transfer voidable at the discretion of the Controller.

Where an applicant files multiple applications relating to the same or similar inventions, and a subsequent application claims priority from an earlier filed application under this Act, the Controller may require the applicant to furnish a declaration specifying the relationship between such applications. Such declaration shall clearly identify the earlier application relied upon for establishing the date filing application and detail the inventive subject matter derived therefrom. Failure to provide a satisfactory declaration, or providing a declaration deemed misleading by the Controller, shall render the subsequent application liable for rejection. An appeal against an order of the Controller under this provision may be made to the Intellectual Property Appellate Board within sixty days from the date of receipt of the order, and the Board’s decision shall be final.

An applicant seeking patent protection for an invention relating to a novel type of agricultural implement shall ensure that the date filing application accurately reflects the earliest possible priority claim. Where an applicant has previously filed an identical or substantially similar application in another jurisdiction, the date filing application under this Act shall be deemed to be the later of either the date of the initial foreign filing or the actual date of submission within India. Provided that, if the invention incorporates improvements relating to specific goods, such as enhanced harvesting efficiency for rice paddies, and these modifications were not disclosed in the prior foreign application, a subsequent examination may be undertaken to assess novelty. The Controller shall have discretion to reject the application should inconsistencies arise between the claimed priority date and the documented details of the invention’s development.

Where an applicant fails to remit the prescribed registry fee within thirty days from the date filing application, the patent office may issue a notice requiring payment of the outstanding amount together with simple interest at the rate of twelve percent per annum. Failure to comply with such notice within one month shall render the application deemed abandoned and all rights accruing therefrom shall vest in the Union Government. Any person who knowingly submits a false statement or representation concerning the date filing application for the purpose of obtaining an undue advantage under this Act shall be liable to prosecution and may face penalties including imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years, and a fine not less than fifty thousand rupees.

Where a patent has been granted under this Act, the registered proprietor may, subject to any conditions specified therein, grant exclusive licences in respect of the patented invention. Such licence shall confer upon the licensee the right to exercise, or perform, all or any of the powers conferred by the patent, including but not limited to the right to make, use, and sell the patented article. Any assignment of a patent, whether absolute or conditional, shall be deemed to include an assignment of all licences granted in respect thereof. The date filing application for priority purposes shall remain paramount in determining the scope of any such licence or assignment. Provided that where infringement registered occurs due to actions taken prior to the grant of a license, remedies available under this Act shall apply as if the patent were held by the original proprietor.

For the purposes of this Act, a "specification filed proceeded" shall mean a document submitted to the Controller under this Act detailing an invention, and which has undergone examination as per the prescribed procedures. Such specification shall include, but not be limited to, a description of the invention sufficient to enable any person skilled in the art to make or use it, claims defining the scope of protection sought, and such drawings as are necessary to understand the invention. The term "specification filed proceeded" also encompasses amendments made to the original document during prosecution, provided that these amendments do not alter the nature of the invention as originally disclosed.

Where a patent has been granted under this Act, and the complete specification filed proceeded with contains information not disclosed in the original application, any person aggrieved may institute an action for damages against the patentee. Such damages shall be calculated based on the commercial detriment suffered by the claimant as a direct result of reliance upon the misleading or incomplete disclosure contained within the specification. Provided that, where the Controller determines that the deficiency in the specification arose from inadvertent omission and did not constitute fraudulent intent on the part of the applicant, the court may reduce or deny damages at its discretion. The patentee shall be deemed to have warranted the accuracy and completeness of the information presented in the specification filed proceeded with. This warranty is subject to the limitations imposed by this Act regarding novelty and inventive step.

Where an applicant elects to proceed with a patent application after publication under this Act, and a request for pre-grant opposition is filed within the prescribed period, the Controller shall serve a copy of such request on the applicant. The applicant may then file a written response addressing the grounds raised in the opposition. Subject to any procedural directions issued by the Controller, the applicant’s response shall be considered alongside the original application and accompanying documents. If the specification filed proceeded with reveals matter not disclosed in the complete specification initially presented, the Controller may require further clarification or amendment. The acceptance of such amendments is subject to ensuring that the amended claims remain consistent with the originally disclosed invention. Any decision regarding patent grant following opposition shall be recorded and made available for public inspection as provided herein.

Where a patent has been granted under this Act, the patentee shall have the right to grant non-exclusive licenses relating to the invention disclosed in the specification filed and proceeded with. Such license may be granted subject to any terms and conditions agreed upon between the patentee and the licensee, provided that the license agreement explicitly states the scope of the licensed rights and duration thereof. Further, a patentee may assign their entire interest in a patent or specific rights relating to it, including but not limited to licensing agreements already entered into, to another party by way of an instrument in writing. Any assignment shall be recorded with the Controller as provided herein. The assignee shall become vested with all rights and privileges which the patentee previously held under this Act concerning the specification filed proceeded with.

Where an applicant elects to proceed with a patent application following the publication of a notification under this Act inviting pre-grant opposition, and such opposition is sustained wholly or in part, the Controller may require the applicant to amend the claims to distinguish the invention from the prior art relied upon in the opposition. Such amendment shall not be permitted if it substantially alters the matter disclosed in the original specification filed proceeded with by the applicant. An aggrieved party challenging this decision of the Controller may appeal to the Intellectual Property Appellate Board, demonstrating that the amended claim effectively introduces a new inventive concept not previously present within the scope of the originally filed specification.

Any person aggrieved by an order passed under this Act relating to revocation or opposition proceedings may appeal to the Appellate Board within sixty days from the date of such order. Failure to comply with the requirements regarding service of notice as provided herein shall not invalidate any proceeding, but the Board may direct a fresh hearing if it considers that prejudice has resulted. Where a specification filed proceeded with discloses an invention relating to a product or process associated with an unregistered geographical indication, and the Controller determines that such use constitutes unfair trade practice or is likely to cause confusion amongst consumers, the application for patent shall be rejected. Penalties for wilful violation of this provision shall include fines not exceeding five hundred thousand rupees and imprisonment up to three years.

An applicant desiring to obtain a patent shall file a complete specification along with the application, detailing the invention and its utility. The specification filed shall include particulars regarding the technical field to which the invention relates, the background art known prior to the filing date, and a clear and concise description of the invention enabling persons skilled in the art to put it into practice. Where an applicant elects to proceed with the patent application after publication under this Act, they may appoint a practise patent agent to represent them during examination and opposition proceedings. The particulars disclosed within the specification filed proceeded shall be construed liberally against the applicant only if such construction is necessary to give effect to the intent of this Act.

For the purposes of this Act, an invention shall be deemed to have been filed for a period exceeding twelve months where the applicant, following the initial publication or public disclosure of any matter constituting the invention, but prior to the date of filing the patent application as provided herein, undertakes activities that would reasonably indicate an intention to commercially exploit said invention within the territory of India. Such activities include, but are not limited to, offering for sale, distributing, or demonstrating the invention publicly. The determination of whether india filed months constitutes a bar to patentability shall be assessed on a case-by-case basis considering all relevant circumstances.

An applicant seeking registration of a utility model shall file a request for extension of the period for completing the formalities relating to the grant of the patent under this Act if, owing to unforeseen circumstances arising after the date on which the application was filed, it has not been possible to comply with those formalities within thirty-six months. Such an applicant may submit evidence demonstrating that india filed months were impacted by events beyond their reasonable control, including but not limited to natural disasters or significant regulatory changes affecting patent prosecution timelines. The Controller General shall consider such evidence and may, subject to conditions as provided herein, grant the requested extension, which shall not exceed twelve additional months. Any further extensions require a fresh application and demonstration of continued extenuating circumstances.

Where an applicant files a request for extension of time under this Act to process a patent application, and such request is granted, the period for which the extension is allowed shall not exceed six months from the original deadline. Provided that if the Controller determines that exceptional circumstances exist, further extensions may be permitted, but in no case exceeding an additional three months. The applicant must demonstrate reasonable cause for the delay, supported by documentary evidence establishing the unforeseen nature of the impediment and diligent efforts to overcome it. Failure to provide adequate justification may result in rejection of the request. Furthermore, where India filed months after a corresponding application in a convention country, this shall not prejudice the validity of the patent granted under this Act.

An applicant seeking a patent under this Act shall file a request for institution of examination within six months from the date on which the application is deemed to have been made available for public inspection. Provided that, if an application has been published earlier than the date it is deemed to have been made available for public inspection, the time limit for filing the said request shall be reckoned from the date of such publication. Where the applicant fails to file a request within the stipulated period, the Controller may issue a notice requiring the applicant to show cause why the application should not be refused. The period specified in the notice shall not exceed thirty days. In cases where an invention is claimed to originate from research supported by funds received from outside India, the applicant must declare such funding and provide details of the grant agreement. It is further provided that india filed months after initial publication are considered for examination priority.

An applicant seeking patent protection for an invention relating to a novel pharmaceutical composition shall file a request for examination within twelve months from the date on which the application was first filed in any convention country, provided that such period may be extended under this Act if the applicant demonstrates reasonable grounds for delay. Where an application claims priority from a previous filing, the time limit for requesting examination is calculated from the initial india filed months of the earlier application. Failure to comply with this provision shall render the application liable for rejection unless the Controller deems it appropriate to grant a condonation of delay supported by satisfactory evidence of unavoidable circumstances preventing timely compliance as provided herein.

Any person aggrieved by an order passed under this Act may appeal to the Appellate Board within sixty days from the date of such order. The Appellate Board shall consider any question of law or fact arising out of the order and may confirm, modify, or reverse the order appealed against. Failure to file an appeal within the prescribed period shall be deemed a waiver of the right to appeal. Where a patent has been granted, and it is subsequently found that the invention was not novel or obvious at the date of filing, or that India filed months prior to the applicant’s priority date, the Controller may revoke the patent after due process. Penalties for false representation in connection with an application shall be as provided herein.

Subject to the provisions of this Act, any patentee or prospective patentee may grant a license to use and exploit a patented invention or an invention for which a patent application is pending, specifying the field of use, territory, and duration of such license. Such licenses shall be assignable under this Act in like manner as the patent itself. Where a license has been granted prior to the publication of the patent application, the term "india filed months" from the date of filing shall constitute the period during which the licensee’s rights are deemed vested, provided that the patentee provides evidence satisfactory to the Controller demonstrating the terms and conditions under which the license was initially executed. The Controller may require a declaration detailing royalty payments and other considerations associated with such licenses, ensuring transparency and preventing exploitation. Further assignments of sub-licenses shall be subject to similar disclosure requirements as primary assignments.

Where an application for patent protection has been filed, and a request for extension of time is made under this Act pertaining to the period between the date of filing and the date of grant, such request shall be entertained only if it demonstrates exceptional circumstances justifying deviation from standard timelines. The Controller may, after affording the applicant an opportunity for hearing, allow or reject the requested extension. However, where a challenge arises regarding the validity of the extension granted, alleging that the applicant failed to diligently pursue the application and that india filed months beyond reasonable expectations given prior art disclosures, such challenge may be brought before the appellate authority within ninety days from the date of publication of the grant. The appellate authority’s decision shall be final, subject to further appeal to the High Court on grounds of law alone.

Where an application for patent protection has been filed, and a request for extension of time is made under this Act, the Controller may grant such extension if satisfied that the applicant was genuinely prevented from completing the necessary formalities within the prescribed period. This prevention shall include circumstances where India filed months prior to the formal examination stage were impacted by unforeseen delays in obtaining requisite regulatory clearances or due to natural disasters affecting records management. The trade proprietor registered as the assignee of the patent application may petition for this extension, providing documentary evidence substantiating the impediment. Provided that any such extension granted shall not exceed a period of eighteen months from the original deadline and is subject to payment of prescribed fees. Failure to demonstrate genuine prevention will result in rejection of the request, without prejudice to other remedies available under this Act.

An applicant seeking to obtain a patent under this Act shall be entitled to claim the benefit of a prior application filed in a convention country, provided that the said prior application was filed not more than twelve months before the date of the Indian application. The right to claim priority as described herein shall arise only if the applicant furnishes a certified copy of the earlier application within such time as may be prescribed by the rules made under this Act. Failure to comply with these procedural requirements will render the applicant ineligible for claiming said priority, irrespective of any subsequent amendment or clarification sought in the Indian patent application. The Controller may require further documentation to verify the authenticity and completeness of the prior application details submitted. Any challenge to the validity of a patent based on issues relating to filed application priority must be brought before the Controller within the timeframe stipulated under this Act.

Where an applicant seeks to benefit from a filed application priority under this Act, and it is determined that such priority has been improperly claimed due to failure to comply with the prescribed timelines for claiming precedence, the Controller shall issue a notice requiring the applicant to demonstrate sufficient grounds for maintaining the claim. Failure to satisfy the Controller within the stipulated period will result in the application being deemed abandoned, subject to an appeal process before the Intellectual Property Appellate Board. Any person demonstrating demonstrable prejudice arising from the improper assertion of priority may further pursue civil remedies and seek damages as provided herein against both the applicant and their representatives. The burden of proof regarding proper compliance rests entirely upon the applicant.

An applicant who has filed an application for a patent relating to an invention may, subject to the provisions herein, assign or license the right to file such application, or any part thereof, to another person, provided that such assignment or license is executed in writing and duly attested. Where an application benefits from filed application priority based on a prior application made in a convention country, the assignee or licensee shall be deemed to have acquired the same rights and obligations as the original applicant concerning the priority date. Further, any subsequent assignment of the patent right after the grant of a license shall require notification to the Controller, detailing the scope and duration of the initial license agreement. The Controller may, upon receiving such notification, issue directions regarding the validity of the subsequent assignment under this Act.

Where an applicant seeks to benefit from a filed application priority under this Act, and where such priority is claimed based on an earlier application filed in a convention country, it shall be incumbent upon the Controller to ascertain whether the subsequent application incorporates all matter disclosed in the first. Should any matter not so incorporated be subsequently introduced during prosecution, the Controller may require the applicant to amend the claims to explicitly restrict their scope to the subject matter originally disclosed. An appeal lies against such a requirement under this Act, and the Appellate Board shall consider whether the amendment unduly prejudices the rights of third parties or renders the invention obvious in light of existing prior art.

For the purposes of this Act, a specification patent shall be deemed to include a detailed description of the invention sufficient to enable any person skilled in the art to make and use it, accompanied by one or more claims defining the scope of protection sought. The term "specification" includes not only the abstract of the invention but also drawings, if any, which form part of the patent application. Subject to provisions regarding novelty and inventive step under this Act, a specification shall disclose the best method contemplated by the inventor for carrying out the invention. Provided that such disclosure does not compromise the commercial viability of the process, variations may be anticipated within the scope of the claims.

The Registering Authority shall, upon receipt of an application for registration of a specification patent, conduct a preliminary examination to ascertain whether the particulars specified therein conform with the requirements under this Act and the Regulations framed thereunder. The applicant shall furnish such documentary evidence as the Registering Authority deems necessary to substantiate the novelty and inventive step claimed in the specification. Where the invention relates to a process for producing a substance defined by its chemical composition, the application must clearly delineate the scope of protection sought through the specification patent. Any alteration or addition to the original specification after registration shall require prior approval from the Controller and may be subject to additional fees as prescribed.

Where an infringement action is brought under this Act, the aggrieved party shall be entitled to seek remedies including, but not limited to, permanent injunctions restraining further acts of infringement and damages commensurate with the loss suffered by the patentee. The measure of damages shall take into account the reasonable royalty that would have been paid had the infringing party licensed the specification patent from the patentee. Provided that, in determining such damages, the Tribunal may consider any profits made by the infringer attributable to the use of the patented invention, even if those profits are not directly related to sales of the infringing product or process. Further, the patentee shall be entitled to recover costs associated with the infringement action, subject to conditions as provided herein regarding proportionality and undue delay.

An application for a specification patent shall be accompanied by a declaration made by the applicant stating that the matter disclosed in the specification is true to the best of their knowledge and belief. The Controller may, at any time during the examination of an application, require the applicant to amend the specification or claims, provided that such amendment does not alter the nature of the invention as originally described. Any objection raised by the Controller under this Act relating to the clarity or support for the claimed subject matter shall be communicated in writing to the applicant, who shall have a period of three months from the date of communication to respond and address the concerns. Failure to adequately respond may result in the application being deemed abandoned. The applicant shall also furnish such documentary evidence as the Controller deems necessary to substantiate the novelty and inventive step of the claimed invention.

Where an applicant seeks to obtain a specification patent for a process by which a substance is produced, such application shall disclose the best method known to the inventor for carrying out the invention. The disclosure must include details sufficient to enable a person skilled in the art to reproduce the specified process and achieve the claimed result, subject to the provisions regarding trade secrets under this Act. Provided that, if the specification patent relates to a process involving microorganisms, the application shall further state whether the microorganism is deposited with an internationally recognized depository authority, and provide details of such deposit. Failure to comply with these disclosure requirements may render the specification patent invalid, as determined by the Controller.

Any person aggrieved by an order passed under this Act relating to the revocation of a specification patent may appeal to the Appellate Board within sixty days from the date of such order; provided that the Appellate Board shall not entertain any appeal unless it is satisfied that there are sufficient grounds for believing that the decision appealed against is erroneous and has occasioned undue hardship. Failure to comply with the prescribed time limit shall be deemed a ground for dismissing the appeal summarily, subject to considerations of natural justice. The Controller may, upon receiving evidence of infringement of a specification patent, initiate proceedings for recovery of damages as provided herein, including punitive damages not exceeding three times the proven loss or actual harm suffered by the patentee.

Subject to the provisions of this Act and rules made thereunder, any person claiming an interest in a specification patent may grant a license under that patent, either wholly or partially, for such consideration and upon such terms as they deem fit; provided that such license shall be recorded with the Controller within three months from the date of its execution. Where a specification patent has been assigned under this Act, the assignee shall be deemed to possess all rights and powers which the assignor possessed prior to the assignment. Further, any licensee may, with the written consent of the patentee or their legal representative, sub-license the licensed technology for specific applications as defined in the original license agreement. The Controller may require disclosure of royalty rates associated with such licenses upon application by an interested party demonstrating a legitimate need for information under this Act.

Where an objection is taken to a specification patent during examination alleging that the matter disclosed therein lacks novelty, it shall be incumbent upon the applicant to demonstrate, through documentary evidence and expert testimony, that the claimed invention constitutes a substantial advance over existing knowledge. The Controller may require the submission of comparative data illustrating the inventive step, and any failure to adequately address such requirements under this Act may result in rejection of the application. An appeal against such rejection lies to the Appellate Board, provided that the appellant establishes prima facie grounds demonstrating reasonable possibility of success based on a re-evaluation of the novelty assessment. The burden of proving lack of obviousness remains upon the petitioner challenging validity after grant.

The Register shall maintain a record of all specifications filed for registration under this Act, detailing the particulars of the applicant, inventor, and the subject matter disclosed therein. Where a specification contains an inventive step relating to a novel process or apparatus, it may be registered as a specification patent upon satisfying the Controller that the invention is capable of industrial application and does not involve use which is contrary to public morality or health. Failure by the patentee to disclose all information known to them relevant to the claimed invention, or subsequent discovery of such withheld data leading to demonstrable prejudice against third parties, shall render the specification liable for forfeiture directed conviction, subject to judicial review as provided herein. The Register shall be open to public inspection during normal business hours.

Where an application for a specification patent relates to an article having a registered layout under the Designs Act, 2000, the Controller shall, prior to granting the patent, issue a notice to the proprietor of the registered layout inviting objections relating solely to the extent that the invention claimed in the specification infringes upon the design protection afforded by such registration. Any objection received within the prescribed period shall be considered during examination and may necessitate amendment of the claims to ensure clarity regarding the inventive step. The applicant shall, upon receiving notice, have the opportunity to submit a written response addressing the objections raised. Failure to respond adequately may result in rejection of the application or limitation of the patent’s scope as determined by the Controller. This process is without prejudice to any other remedies available under this Act or any other law for design infringement.

An application for a specification patent relating to a semiconductor device shall be deemed invalid if the description does not adequately disclose the manner in which the invention may be made or used, subject to the proviso that such inadequacy is demonstrable by reference to existing prior art as of the date of filing. Furthermore, where the claimed invention incorporates a process involving photolithography, the specification must detail the specific wavelengths employed and the resist materials utilized, provided that deviations from these disclosed parameters would render the device non-functional according to established engineering principles. Any modification to the semiconductor’s architecture, not explicitly described within the specification, shall invalidate claims directed towards such modified design under this Act.

An examination application patent is deemed to have been laid before the Controller when the formal requirements of an application for a patent, as provided herein, are satisfied and the requisite government fee has been remitted. The filing date of an examination application patent shall be the date on which the application was first received by the Patent Office; however, subject to this, where an applicant seeks priority from a previous application, the relevant date shall be determined under this Act. An examiner may request further information or clarification regarding any aspect of the invention disclosed in the examination application patent to ensure compliance with the provisions relating to novelty and inventive step.

An applicant seeking registration of a patent may submit an examination application patent to the Controller within thirty-six months from the date of filing the original application or the priority date, whichever is earlier. The submission shall include all documents and information required under this Act as deemed necessary for assessment of novelty and inventive step. Provided that, if the applicant has previously published details of the invention in a manner not compliant with prescribed guidelines, the Controller may require further declarations attesting to the extent of prior disclosure. Any request for amendment to claims within an examination application patent must be accompanied by a reasoned justification demonstrating compliance with established legal principles and shall be subject to review by the examiner.

Where an examiner finds, during the course of examining an examination application patent, that the invention is not novel or does not involve sufficient inventive step, the examiner shall communicate such findings to the applicant and afford them an opportunity to file a written response addressing the objections raised. The applicant may amend the claims in the examination application patent to overcome these objections, subject to the limitations of novelty and inventive step as provided herein. Failure by the applicant to adequately respond within the prescribed time shall be deemed abandonment of the examination application patent. Any interested person may, after the publication of the application under this Act, file a post-grant opposition against the grant of the patent, asserting that it does not meet the requirements for patentability and seeking appropriate remedies including revocation.

An examination application patent shall be deemed to have been formally laid before the Controller upon receipt of the official fee as stipulated under this Act. The applicant may, at any time after the publication of the application under section 149, but prior to the determination of rights by the Patent Office, request an amendment to the claims or subject matter disclosed in the patent application, provided that such amendment does not alter the nature of the invention as originally claimed and is supported by the description. The Controller shall issue a notification regarding any such proposed amendments, inviting objections from third parties within a period prescribed herein. Any objection received shall be communicated to the applicant for response, after which the Controller may proceed with the examination process. Failure to respond to an objection within the stipulated timeframe will render the application liable to rejection as provided herein.

An examination application patent shall only proceed to substantive examination if the applicant has fulfilled all procedural requirements as provided herein. The Controller may direct that an application be deemed withdrawn where the requisite fee for examination has not been paid within three months of the date specified in the official notification, or such extended period as determined by the Controller. Provided that, if the applicant demonstrates satisfactory cause for the delay in payment, and provides evidence thereof to the satisfaction of the Controller, the Controller may condone the delay and permit the application to proceed. Further, any objection raised during examination regarding novelty or inventive step shall be addressed through a written response from the applicant within sixty days, failing which the application may be refused.

Where an examination application patent is granted and subsequently challenged through a pre-grant opposition proceeding, the Controller may, subject to due process, order the suspension of the patent’s enforcement pending resolution of said opposition. Any party aggrieved by such suspension or by the refusal to suspend enforcement may appeal under this Act to the Intellectual Property Appellate Board. Failure to comply with orders issued during the pendency of an opposition shall render the defaulting party liable for compensatory damages as determined by the Board, and subject to a penalty not exceeding five hundred thousand rupees. The Controller shall provide reasons in writing for any decision regarding suspension or refusal thereof; such reasons are open to judicial review.

Where an examination application patent relates to technology developed jointly by two or more entities, the applicant may execute a written assignment conferring upon one of those entities the right to prosecute the examination proceedings and manage all aspects of licensing relating to the invention. Such assignment shall specify the scope of rights granted, including any royalties payable to co-owners not party to the assignment. Further, where an application is assigned as provided herein, the Controller may require disclosure of prior agreements between assignors and assignees concerning the exploitation of the patented invention. Any subsequent assignment or license relating to the examination application patent shall be notified to the Controller within thirty days of execution, accompanied by a copy of the instrument creating such rights. The Controller shall maintain a record of all assignments and licenses affecting the subject matter of the examination application patent.

Where an examiner finds grounds to refuse an examination application patent, he shall issue a communication specifying the reasons for such refusal. The applicant may, within sixty days from the date of receipt of said communication, file a response addressing each objection raised by the examiner and submitting arguments or amendments as deemed necessary. Should the applicant fail to respond within the stipulated period, the application shall be deemed abandoned. However, the Controller may, subject to just cause shown, entertain a delayed reply. Any decision made by the Controller regarding an examination application patent is appealable to the Appellate Board under this Act, provided that the appellant demonstrates prejudice resulting from the Controller’s order.

Where an examiner, during the course of examining an examination application patent, discovers information which appears to establish that any claim is anticipated or obvious, he shall issue a communication to the applicant detailing the grounds upon which such conclusion is based. The applicant shall then have opportunity to file a written response addressing these concerns within three months from the date of receipt of said communication; failure to respond within this period shall be deemed an abandonment of the application. Should the applicant’s response fail adequately to overcome the examiner's objections, or if evidence presented by the applicant inadvertently substantiates information suggesting prior use inconsistent with a claim, such information may be considered as deemed falsify trade and will preclude grant of the patent. The Controller may, at any time, require further clarification from either party before making a determination.

An examination application patent shall not proceed to grant unless the Controller is satisfied that the invention disclosed relates to a process involving the transmission operation law as defined under this Act. Provided that, where an applicant has previously filed an identical or substantially similar application relating to the same invention, the Controller may require submission of a comprehensive comparative analysis detailing any modifications made and their impact on novelty and inventive step. Further, if the claimed subject matter incorporates elements derived from pre-existing knowledge accessible prior to the filing date, the applicant shall furnish documented evidence demonstrating sufficient inventive contribution over such knowledge. The Controller is empowered to reject the examination application patent if the requisite documentation is not submitted within the prescribed timeframe or deemed insufficient following assessment.

Subject to the provisions of this Act and rules made thereunder, any person owning an application for a patent may grant a license to use or exploit the invention disclosed in such application, either wholly or partially, to another party. Such license may be exclusive or non-exclusive, and shall specify the territory within which the licensee is authorized to exercise the patented right. Assignment of an examination application patent, including any associated licenses, requires registration with the Controller, and unless so registered, remains void against subsequent assignees or licensees. The High Court shall have jurisdiction to entertain disputes arising from such assignments or licensing agreements concerning the validity or scope of rights conferred under this Act. Further, a licensee may sub-license their rights provided that prior written consent is obtained from the patent owner.

For the purposes of this Act, an “application patent period” is defined as the duration commencing from the date of filing of a patent application and terminating twenty years from that same date, or such lesser period as claimed in the patent specification, whichever is shorter. This period shall be subject to extensions granted under this Act for delays in examination due to pending objections or requests for further information. An applicant may request an extension of the application patent period where unforeseen circumstances impede the completion of invention work prior to expiry. The extended period shall not exceed three years beyond the original expiration date, provided that adequate justification is furnished as per regulations framed under this Act.

An applicant seeking registration of an invention under this Act shall file a formal application specifying the particulars of the invention and claiming protection thereof. The application shall include a statement outlining the technical field to which the invention relates, along with detailed descriptions enabling persons skilled in the art to reproduce the same. Upon successful completion of examination and grant, the applicant is entitled to an application patent period of twenty years from the date of filing the application. Renewal fees for maintaining the application patent period shall be payable as per prescribed rates and timelines. Failure to remit such renewal fees may result in the application being deemed abandoned, subject to provisions regarding revival under this Act.

Where an application patent period has expired without grant or refusal of the patent, any person may petition the Controller to restore the application to the register. Such restoration shall only occur if the petitioner demonstrates reasonable grounds for failing to pursue the patent within the stipulated timeframe, and that no prejudice will result to other parties as a consequence of the delayed action. The Controller may require the petitioner to satisfy conditions relating to payment of fees and costs incurred by the office due to the delay. Further, where an application is restored under this provision, the application shall be deemed abandoned unless the Controller specifically directs otherwise; any subsequent examination shall proceed subject to all relevant provisions regarding novelty and inventive step as provided herein. The Controller’s decision on a petition for restoration shall be final, subject to appeal before the Intellectual Property Appellate Board.

An application for a patent may be granted subject to compliance with all applicable provisions herein. The Controller shall grant a patent unless he considers that the invention does not satisfy any condition specified under this Act. Where an application is filed, the applicant shall pay such fees as are prescribed; failure to do so will result in the application being deemed abandoned. An application patent period commences from the date of publication of the first examination report under this Act and extends for a term of twenty years from the filing date. The applicant may request an extension of this application patent period if, owing to circumstances beyond their control, they have not been able to complete commercial production of the patented invention within five years from the grant date; such requests shall be accompanied by supporting documentation as prescribed.

An application patent period shall extend to twenty years from the date of filing, subject to any adjustments arising from post-grant opposition proceedings as provided herein. Where an applicant has failed to comply with requirements regarding the furnishing of information under this Act, the Controller may, after giving the applicant an opportunity of being heard, extend the application patent period by a duration not exceeding six months. Such extension shall only be granted if the failure to furnish the requisite information was demonstrably unintentional and did not prejudice the interests of any other party. Furthermore, where a request for examination is delayed due to circumstances beyond the applicant’s control, the Controller may, upon satisfactory demonstration of such circumstances, grant an appropriate extension; however, this shall not extend the overall application patent period beyond twenty-four months from the original filing date.

An applicant seeking protection through an application patent period exceeding twenty years from the date of filing shall furnish a declaration to the Controller affirming that the invention does not infringe any existing intellectual property rights. Failure to submit this declaration within three months of the application’s publication, as provided herein, renders the application liable for rejection without further notice. Any person demonstrating demonstrable prejudice due to an applicant's non-compliance may petition the relevant authority seeking redress and imposition of a monetary penalty, recoverable from the defaulting applicant. The Controller shall have discretion to waive this requirement in cases involving compelling circumstances, subject to recording reasons thereof.

An applicant seeking to grant of a patent may enter into agreements whereby rights pertaining to the invention disclosed in the application are licensed or assigned to another party; provided that such agreements explicitly state the terms and conditions governing the exploitation of the patented technology. Where an assignment or license is executed during the application patent period, the assignee or licensee shall be deemed to step into the shoes of the original applicant for all purposes under this Act, including the right to pay prescribed fees and extend the term of the application. The Controller may require submission of documentation demonstrating the validity of any such agreement before proceeding with examination. Further, where an invention is jointly developed by multiple parties, agreements concerning licensing or assignment must clearly delineate each party’s respective rights and obligations during the application patent period, as provided herein.

An appeal lies to the Appellate Board from any order passed by the Controller relating to the determination of validity or revocation of a patent, including orders concerning the extension of an application patent period. Such an appeal may only be filed within sixty days from the date of communication of the order; provided that the Board may entertain appeals lodged out of time where it is satisfied that there existed reasonable grounds for the delay and that the delay has not prejudiced the other party. The Controller shall, in determining whether to grant an extension of the application patent period under this Act, consider any evidence presented by either the appellant or respondent demonstrating a substantial dispute regarding novelty or inventive step.

An aggrieved party seeking remedies relating to infringement of a patent may institute proceedings in the High Court, subject to furnishing security as determined by the court. The measure of damages recoverable under this Act shall be commensurate with the loss suffered by the patentee and shall include reasonable royalties which the complainant would have paid had the infringing activity been duly licensed. Where an application patent period has expired, any person may apply for and obtain a patent for the invention, provided that such subsequent applicant demonstrates to the satisfaction of the Controller that the invention was not commercially exploited in India during the term of the prior patent. The effect India patent has on existing commercial arrangements shall be considered by the court when determining equitable remedies.

An application patent period shall extend to twenty years from the date of filing, subject to any modifications or extensions granted by the Controller under this Act. Where an applicant seeks to amend the claims of an application during prosecution, such amendment shall not alter the matter disclosed in the original specification as filed; provided that the amended claims remain within the scope of the invention initially claimed. Any person aggrieved by an order passed by the Controller relating to the grant or refusal of a patent may appeal against such order to the Intellectual Property Appellate Board. The appeal shall be made within sixty days from the date of communication of the order, and the grounds of appeal must clearly state the errors of law or fact apparent on the face of the record. Further appeals are permitted under provisions as provided herein.

An applicant seeking protection through an application patent period shall diligently adhere to all stipulated procedural requirements as provided herein. The duration of such protection is contingent upon continued compliance with regulations concerning maintenance fees and publication protocols. Failure to remit the requisite fee within the specified timeframe, following notification by the india registrar, will render the patent liable for lapse. Furthermore, any alteration to the claims or subject matter of the invention after the initial filing date shall necessitate a formal request for amendment, duly approved by the india registrar prior to further processing under this Act. The applicant must also ensure that all supporting documentation remains accurate and accessible throughout the pendency of the application.

Subject to the provisions of this Act and rules made thereunder, any licensee granted rights under an application patent may, with the prior written consent of the applicant or patentee, assign such license, either wholly or partially, to any other person or entity. Such assignment shall not be effective until registered with the Controller General of Patents, Designs, and Trademarks in the prescribed form and manner; failure to register shall render the assignee’s claim void. The application for registration of an assignment under this Act shall include a copy of the license agreement being assigned. Where disputes arise concerning the validity or scope of such assignments, the High Court may be approached for resolution. An applicant seeking to enforce rights arising from an application patent period is deemed to have complied with all relevant provisions if they provide evidence of proper licensing and assignment procedures followed.

An application for registration of a utility model shall be deemed to be complete upon submission of all requisite forms and fees as stipulated under this Act. The Controller may, at any time after the completion of an application but before the grant of registration, require the applicant to furnish further particulars or submit additional documentation relating to the novelty and inventive step of the claimed invention. It is provided that such a requirement shall be accompanied by a reasoned explanation detailing the deficiencies perceived in the initial submission. Further, a patent shall examined only after the applicant has complied with any directions issued under this provision and paid any associated charges as determined by the Controller. The examination process may include an assessment of prior art publications to ascertain obviousness.

Where an applicant has failed to comply with any requirement of this Act or the Regulations framed thereunder, the Controller may issue a communication specifying the nature of such failure and requiring compliance within a time specified therein. Failure to comply with such communication will render the application liable for rejection. However, the applicant shall be afforded a reasonable opportunity to make representations against the proposed rejection, and the Controller shall consider any submissions made before proceeding further. A patent shall examined only after the applicant has fulfilled all procedural requirements as provided herein. Any person aggrieved by an order of the Controller relating to examination may appeal under this Act to the Intellectual Property Appellate Board within sixty days from the date of receipt of such order.

An application for a patent shall not proceed to examination unless the Controller is satisfied that the applicant has complied with all procedural requirements as provided herein. The request for examination must specify clearly the invention claimed and identify any prior publications relied upon by the applicant, subject to exemptions granted under this Act concerning trivial variations. Where an objection arises regarding the clarity or support of a claim during examination, the applicant shall be afforded an opportunity to amend the specification, provided that such amendments do not alter the matter originally disclosed. The Controller may require further clarification from the applicant at any stage and the patent shall examined only upon receipt of satisfactory responses.

Where an objection is raised by the examiner during the course of examination challenging the novelty or inventive step of a claimed invention, the applicant shall have the right to file a written response addressing such objections within three months from the date of communication. Such response may include arguments, evidence, and amended claims as deemed necessary; provided that any amendment to the claims shall not alter the nature of the invention as originally disclosed in the patent application. The Controller may, after considering the applicant’s response, either proceed with the examination or direct further clarification. Any party aggrieved by such direction may appeal under this Act to the Appellate Board within sixty days from the date of communication of the order, subject to a stay order granted by the Controller. A patent shall examined only after all objections are resolved or appeals exhausted.

For the purposes of this Act, a specification amended subsequent to the initial filing date refers to alterations made to the description of the invention, claims defining the scope thereof, or drawings illustrating the same. Such amendments shall adhere strictly to the principles of clarity and conciseness, ensuring that the technical field and inventive step remain unambiguously defined. An amendment is deemed invalid if it introduces matter not originally disclosed in the application, subject to exceptions permitted under this Act relating to clarification of claims. The amended specification shall be treated as a substitute for the original specification regarding all subsequent proceedings concerning patentability.

Where an application for a patent has been laid open to public inspection under this Act, and subsequently the applicant seeks to amend the specification, such amendment shall only be permissible with the Board’s consent. The Board may allow an amendment if it considers that the amended specification clearly defines the subject matter of the invention as claimed and does not go beyond the content disclosed in the original application taken as a whole. Any party aggrieved by a decision of the Board permitting or refusing such an amendment may appeal to the High Court within sixty days from the date of communication of the order, provided that the appellant demonstrates prejudice resulting directly from the Board’s action. The right to claim damages for any loss suffered due to reliance on the patent granted following a specification amended in this manner shall be subject to judicial determination.

Where an application for a patent has been laid before the Controller for determination of novelty and inventive step, and subsequently the applicant seeks to amend the specification, such amendment shall only be permissible with the written consent of the Controller. The amended specification must not alter the nature of the invention as originally claimed in the application; any alteration deemed material by the Controller will render the amendment impermissible. Following approval of an amendment, a fresh notice under this Act shall be published indicating the changes made to the original specification amended and inviting objections from interested parties within a period of thirty days from the date of such publication. The Controller may require further clarification or data relating to the amended claims before proceeding with examination. Any objection received after the expiry of the stipulated time shall not be entertained, subject to an application for condonation of delay supported by reasonable cause.

Where an application for a patent has been laid open for public inspection under this Act, and subsequently the applicant seeks to amend the specification, such amendment shall only be permissible with the prior approval of the Controller. The Controller may grant such approval if he is satisfied that the proposed amendments do not substantially alter the nature of the invention as originally disclosed or broaden the scope of protection sought beyond what was reasonably anticipated by a person skilled in the art at the time of the application’s initial filing. Any amendment to the specification shall be clearly indicated within the patent document, distinguishing between the original matter and the added subject-matter; failure to comply with this requirement renders the amended specification void. The Controller shall provide notice of any such *specification amended* to all known opponents under this Act.

Where the proprietor of a patent has elected to grant an exclusive license relating to the invention claimed in the patent, and subsequently amends the specification under this Act, such amendment shall not prejudice the rights granted to the licensee unless the amendment materially alters the scope of protection afforded by the patent as originally defined. The Controller may, upon application by any interested party, determine whether a specification amended in pursuance of section 84 has indeed resulted in a material alteration of the invention’s scope. Any assignment or further transfer of rights relating to an invention subject to a licensed patent shall be deemed valid only if it explicitly acknowledges and respects the existing license agreement. Provided that the licensee provides written consent, the proprietor may assign the entire interest in the patent, including any benefits arising from the specification amended.

Where an application for a patent has been laid open for public inspection and the complete specification is subsequently amended, such amendment shall only be permissible if it does not substantially alter the nature claimed for the invention. Any party aggrieved by the acceptance of an amended specification may appeal to the Appellate Board within sixty days from the date of publication of the amended specification under this Act. The Board shall consider whether the amendment introduces matter which goes beyond the disclosure in the original application, and if so, determine that the patent should not be granted or, alternatively, require further examination. It is provided that the Controller may, at any stage of the proceedings, direct a fresh search relating to the invention as affected by the specification amended.

For the purposes of this Act, a “patent outside India” means a patent granted by any competent authority in a country other than India, relating to an invention for which an application for patents has been filed in India, provided that such foreign patent was not obtained in violation of any provision under this Act or any rule made thereunder. The term "competent authority" shall include any governmental body or agency authorized to grant patents within the jurisdiction of the relevant country. An applicant seeking to rely on a patent outside India as prior art shall furnish an authenticated copy thereof, duly translated into English if originally in another language, subject to verification by the Controller.

An applicant seeking registration of a patent relating to an invention may, subject to the provisions of this Act and the regulations framed thereunder, disclose details pertaining to corresponding applications filed outside India. Such disclosure shall include, but not be limited to, the country or countries where the foreign application was made, the filing date thereof, and the status currently held by such patent application or granted patent. The Controller may require further documentation substantiating these claims, including certified copies of official records from the relevant foreign intellectual property office. Failure to provide accurate information regarding a patent outside India shall render the applicant liable for penalties as determined under this Act. This requirement applies equally whether the invention is novel and non-obvious within India or not.

An applicant seeking registration of a patent outside India shall furnish to the Controller, within three months from the date of filing the first application in India, a certified copy of the corresponding application filed in any other country. The Controller may require the applicant to submit further documentation demonstrating compliance with applicable foreign law regarding novelty and inventive step; such requirements shall be communicated in writing and allow for a period of sixty days for response. Failure to provide the requested information within that timeframe will result in suspension of examination proceedings until the deficiency is remedied. Where an application for a patent outside India incorporates subject matter disclosed in the Indian application, the applicant must notify the Controller upon grant or rejection by the foreign authority. This notification shall be accompanied by a certified copy of the decision.

Subject to the provisions relating to national security as provided herein, any person seeking to obtain protection for an invention under this Act may file a request for information regarding the status of corresponding applications for a patent outside India. Such request shall specify the jurisdiction where the foreign application was filed and provide certified copies of relevant documents pertaining thereto. The Controller may require the applicant to furnish further details deemed necessary to ascertain compliance with the requirements concerning simultaneous filing, or any other applicable provisions under this Act.
