Such actions are deemed to be an unfair trade practice and may result in penalties as determined by the competent authority. Provided that, a registered proprietor shall have the right to initiate legal proceedings against anyone who misrepresents or imitates their protected geographical indication.

Any individual or entity seeking to utilize a protected Geographical Indication for commercial purposes, including but not limited to manufacturing, processing, packaging, selling, or exporting goods associated with the indication, shall first obtain a license from the proprietor of the Geographical Indication as provided herein. Such licenses may be granted on such terms and conditions, including royalty payments and duration, as are deemed appropriate by the proprietor. Assignment of rights in a registered Geographical Indication, whether through sale, merger, or other transfer, requires prior notification to and registration with the Registrar, subject to payment of prescribed fees. A person contravenes provisions under this Act if they offer for sale goods bearing a licensed Geographical Indication without adhering strictly to the terms stipulated within their license agreement. Furthermore, any alteration to a registered Geographical Indication’s distinctive signs or marks requires express consent from the proprietor and subsequent approval by the Registrar.

An application for registration of a geographical indication shall include particulars as to the name of the agricultural product or good concerned, the territory from which it originates, the qualities, reputation or other characteristics which are attributable to its origin, and the manner in which the geographical indication is used. Where an objection is raised against the acceptance of an application under this Act, the applicant may submit their response within a period specified by the Registrar. The Registrar shall consider such objections and responses and may either accept or reject the application. Any person aggrieved by an order passed by the Registrar relating to registration or refusal thereof may appeal to the Appellate Board. This provision applies equally where action is taken for infringement or for passing off referred to in section 66.

Any party aggrieved by an order made by the Appellate Board may further appeal to the High Court within sixty days from the date of that order, and the High Court shall have jurisdiction to hear and determine such appeals subject to the provisions of the relevant Code of Civil Procedure. The determination of the High Court shall be final. It is provided that any suit for infringement or for passing off referred to in section 66 may be filed notwithstanding any appeal pending before the Appellate Board or the High Court.

Further, any proprietor of a registered geographical indication may apply to the civil court for an injunction restraining such unauthorized use. context: A person seeking to challenge the registration of a geographical indication may apply to the Registrar for leave to do so; such application shall specify the grounds upon which the challenge is based and provide all relevant documentation supporting that challenge. For the purposes of this Act, a “party proceeding” includes any individual or entity granted leave by the Registrar under this sub-section, as well as the registered proprietor of the geographical indication and any applicant for registration who is directly affected by the challenged application. The Registrar may, subject to just cause shown, grant or refuse such leave; provided that an appeal against a decision regarding leave does not operate as a stay of the original proceeding.

A party proceeding concerning the registration of a geographical indication may include any individual or body corporate claiming rights relating to similar goods or services as those for which registration is sought. Where an objection is raised against an application under this Act, the Registrar shall provide notice thereof to all registered proprietors and applicants for registration of geographically indicative products within the same class. Any such proprietor or applicant who desires to oppose the registration may, subject to prescribed conditions, apply to be joined as a party proceeding in respect of that opposition. The Registrar shall consider applications to join proceedings based on demonstrated interest and potential prejudice resulting from exclusion. Provided that any application for joinder must be filed within the time specified by the Registrar.

Any person aggrieved by an order passed under this Act relating to the revocation of registration of a geographical indication may appeal to the Intellectual Property Appellate Board within sixty days from the date of receipt of the order. The Appellate Board shall give notice to every party proceeding against whom the order is made, affording them an opportunity of being heard. Subject to such hearing, the Appellate Board may confirm, vary or reverse the order appealed against. Where a geographical indication is registered under this Act, no person other than an authorized user shall be entitled to institute any proceedings for infringement relating to that indication without first notifying the proprietor of the registration and providing them with a reasonable opportunity to protect their rights. Provided that, failure to comply with such notification requirement shall not preclude a party proceeding from seeking interim relief in urgent circumstances.

A party proceeding before the Geographical Indications Registry concerning the validity of a registered geographical indication may submit evidence demonstrating non-distinctiveness of the indication within the territory for which registration is sought. Such evidence shall be presented in a manner prescribed by the Registrar and must relate directly to consumer perception at the time the application for registration was filed, or during the period since registration, as applicable. The Registrar shall provide the registered proprietor with an opportunity to rebut such evidence through written submissions and oral arguments, subject to procedural rules established under this Act. Any decision regarding non-distinctiveness may be appealed to the Appellate Board within a timeframe specified herein. A party proceeding in good faith is entitled to reimbursement of reasonable expenses incurred if their appeal succeeds. The Registrar shall maintain records of all proceedings relating to geographical indication validity and make them accessible, subject to confidentiality restrictions as provided herein.

A party proceeding before the Geographical Indications Registry concerning the validity of registration for “Kanthaloor Pepper” shall furnish, within thirty days of notification under this Act, a detailed affidavit verifying their standing as a producer or trader directly involved in the production, processing, and packaging of pepper originating from Kanthaloor village. Such an affidavit must specify the geographical area from which the applicant sources its raw materials, and demonstrate adherence to quality control measures prescribed by the Spice Board. Provided that any party proceeding who fails to submit this affidavit within the stipulated timeframe shall be deemed to have abandoned their challenge unless a request for extension is made with adequate justification and approved by the Registry. Further, the Registry may require submission of additional documentation to ascertain compliance with relevant regulations.

Any person aggrieved by an order passed under this Act relating to the revocation or modification of registration of a geographical indication may appeal to the Appellate Board within sixty days from the date of such order. Failure to file an appeal within the prescribed time shall be deemed a waiver of the right to challenge the order. Where a registered proprietor institutes proceedings against any party proceeding in contravention of the provisions relating to use or production, the Registrar may intervene as a party and assist the Court with relevant technical information pertaining to the geographical indication's characteristics. Any penalty imposed for infringement shall be recoverable from the defaulting party as an arrears of land revenue, subject to judicial review.

A registered proprietor of a geographical indication may grant a license conferring the right to use such indication relating to goods for which the geographical indication is registered, subject to conditions specified in the license agreement. Any subsequent assignment of rights under this Act concerning a geographical indication shall include all licenses previously granted, unless the assignee expressly agrees otherwise in writing with the licensor. A party proceeding against a registered proprietor or licensee may seek discovery of any such license agreements relevant to the dispute. Further, where a geographical indication is jointly owned, consent from all joint owners shall be required for granting a license or assignment, provided that a single owner may petition the Geographical Indications Registry for permission to proceed if other owners are unreachable. The Registrar may issue directions regarding the terms and conditions of such licenses to ensure fair trade practices.

Where any person aggrieved by an order passed by the Registrar relating to the registration of a geographical indication, or by the acceptance or rejection of an application for registration, may appeal to the Appellate Board. The Appellate Board shall hear and dispose of such appeals expeditiously, subject to the provisions of this Act. Any party proceeding with an appeal under this section must demonstrate that they have suffered material prejudice as a direct consequence of the order appealed against. Provided that, where the Registrar’s decision concerns the rectification of the register, any interested party may petition the Appellate Board for review if they believe the rectification is contrary to law or public interest. The Board shall give notice to all affected parties before issuing any such determination.

A party proceeding concerning the validity of a registered geographical indication may apply to the Registrar for directions if it is demonstrated that the use of a similar mark on related goods creates confusion amongst consumers. Such application shall be accompanied by evidence substantiating the likelihood of such confusion, including market surveys and consumer perception data. The Registrar shall consider any objections raised by proprietors of marks registered in connection with identical or asimilar goods. Provided that, if the party proceeding is also a producer of goods conforming to the standard prescribed for the geographical indication, they must demonstrate adherence to those standards throughout their production process. Further, the Registrar may require submission of documentation verifying compliance with quality control measures relating to mark registered goods.

For the purposes of this Act, “Darjeeling Tea” means tea produced exclusively in the defined geographical area consisting of the Sadar, Kalimpong and Kurseong subdivisions of the Darjeeling district within the State of West Bengal; and such term shall include any tea which is processed or made ready for sale in that area. The Registrar may require evidence demonstrating adherence to traditional production methods as a condition of registration. An indication found to contain geographical elements not corresponding with the defined territory shall, subject to appeal under this Act, be deemed ineligible for protection. This Act shall apply equally to both loose leaf and bagged Darjeeling Tea.

Any proprietor seeking to enforce the rights conferred under this Act against any infringement shall file a suit in the High Court having jurisdiction over the territory within which the alleged infringement has taken place or is likely to take place. The court shall, upon receiving such a suit, proceed expeditiously and may grant such relief as it deems just and equitable, including an injunction restraining the infringing party from using the geographical indication in connection with goods or services for which it is registered. Further, the proprietor shall be entitled to claim damages sustained by reason of the infringement, calculated on the basis of lost profits or a reasonable royalty, whichever is higher. Provided that, where the infringer was unaware and had no reason to believe that the use of the geographical indication would constitute an infringement, the court may reduce the amount of damages awarded. The Act shall also empower the Court to order the destruction of infringing goods and materials.

An application for registration of a geographical indication shall be accompanied by such particulars deemed necessary by the Registrar, including but not limited to a map indicating the territorial boundaries of the geographical area of production or origin, and a statement detailing the qualities, reputation or other characteristics which are attributable to the geographical origin. The applicant shall also furnish evidence demonstrating that the goods originate from the asserted geographical territory and that the name conforms with the standards prescribed under this Act. Upon receipt of an application, the Registrar may direct the applicant to rectify any deficiencies in the particulars submitted. Any objection received by the Registrar concerning the distinctiveness or suitability of a proposed geographical indication shall be communicated to the applicant for response, as provided herein. The Registrar shall act expeditiously and shall record all proceedings relating to objections. This Act shall govern the procedures regarding hearings and appeals against decisions made under this process.

An application for registration of a geographical indication shall include a statement specifying the quality, reputation or other characteristics of goods which are attributable to the origin of such goods. The Registrar may require the applicant to furnish further particulars relating to the geographical boundaries of the area of production and/or processing of the goods. Where an objection is raised under this Act against the registration of a geographical indication, the objector shall be afforded a reasonable opportunity for being heard. Any person claiming interest in the opposition proceedings may appear and be heard as provided herein. The Registrar shall act fairly and impartially while considering such objections. This Act shall apply to goods produced and/or processed within a defined geographical area.

Any person who, without due cause and after receiving notice under this Act, uses any indication falsely purporting to be a geographical indication for goods with respect to which the said indication is registered, or in such manner as to mislead the public into believing that the goods originate from the area specified by the geographical indication, shall be liable to pay damages of an amount determined by the High Court. The court may, in addition to awarding damages, order the infringer to forfeit any profits derived from the infringing use. Further, where a registered proprietor establishes that the infringement has caused substantial damage to their reputation or goodwill, they shall act to recover such further compensation as is just and reasonable. This Act shall apply without prejudice to any other law for the time being in force relating to trade marks.

Any proprietor of an indication registered under this Act may grant non-exclusive licenses to use the geographical indication in relation to the goods for which it is registered, subject to such terms and conditions as are agreed upon between the parties and recorded with the Registrar. Such license agreements shall clearly delineate the scope of permitted activities, including but not limited to packaging, labeling, and advertising of the licensed products. The proprietor may also assign the right to use a registered geographical indication to any person, provided that such assignment is approved by the Registrar after due consideration of the impact on consumer protection and the integrity of the indication itself. Further, an assignee shall be bound by the conditions applicable to the original registration and act shall not permit them to alter or misrepresent the characteristics associated with the goods originating from the registered geographical area. The Registrar may require periodic reporting from licensees and assignees regarding compliance with these provisions.

Any person aggrieved by an order passed under this Act may appeal to the Appellate Board within sixty days from the date of such order, and the Appellate Board shall consider any question of law arising in the appeal. The Central Registry shall, upon receiving a notice of appeal, transmit all relevant records pertaining to the original proceeding to the Appellate Board without delay. An appeal shall not suspend the operation of the order appealed against unless the Appellate Board directs otherwise, provided that such direction may be given only after considering representations made by both parties. Further, any party dissatisfied with the decision of the Appellate Board may petition the Supreme Court under Article 136 of the Constitution, but this act shall not preclude recourse to alternative remedies available under law.

Any proprietor seeking to grant a license relating to the use of an indication registered under this Act shall, prior to such grant, provide notice to the Registrar specifying the geographical area covered by the registration and detailing the terms and conditions of the proposed license agreement. The Registrar may, after affording opportunity for objection to interested parties, issue directions regarding the permissible scope of such licenses, particularly concerning quality control measures applicable to goods bearing the registered indication. Assignment of rights in a registered geographical indication shall require prior approval from the Registrar, provided that such assignment does not alter the essential characteristics or reputation associated with the registration. Further, any subsequent transfer relating registration geographical boundaries must be notified to the office within three months and is subject to review under this Act.

Any person who, without due cause and after receiving notice under sub-section (1) of section 52, uses any authorized Geographical Indication in relation to goods not conforming to the standards established for that indication shall be deemed to have engaged in an act of proceeding infringement. Such infringement shall render the offender liable to pay damages proportionate to the loss suffered by the registered proprietor or producers’ association, as determined by the High Court. The amount of damages shall be recoverable as a civil debt and may include compensation for dilution of the distinctiveness of the Geographical Indication. Further, any goods bearing an infringing indication are subject to seizure and destruction under orders passed by the High Court. This Act shall binding on all persons within the territory of India, and its provisions extend to proceedings before any court or tribunal.

Subject to the provisions of this Act, and without prejudice to section 27, any registered proprietor of a layout-design may grant a license conferring the right to make an integrated circuit embodying the design, or any part thereof. Such licenses may be exclusive or non-exclusive, as determined by the grantor, and shall specify the geographical territory within which the licensee is permitted to exercise the licensed rights. The granting of a license does not prejudice the proprietor’s own ability to exploit their layout-design; however, assignment of the entire layout-design designations requires prior written consent from the Controller General. Where a layout-design has been assigned, any subsequent means transmission of ownership shall be deemed to include all licenses previously granted by the assignor. The assignee shall step into the shoes of the original proprietor concerning existing and future license agreements.

Where an assignor of layout-design rights purports to transfer such rights in favour of an assignee, and subsequently claims a continuing beneficial interest inconsistent with the terms of assignment, the validity of the purported transfer assignment vice shall be determined by examining the written agreement evidencing the transaction. Such examination shall consider whether the language employed clearly demonstrates an intention to fully convey all rights pertaining to the layout-design, free from reservations or conditions that would undermine the assignee’s exclusive exploitation thereof. It is provided that any ambiguity in the terms of assignment may be resolved by considering contemporaneous correspondence and conduct of the parties; however, such evidence shall not be admissible to contradict a clear and unambiguous provision within the written agreement itself, subject to principles of equitable estoppel.

For the purposes of this Act, "means transmission operation" with respect to a layout design shall signify the act of utilizing a layout design in the manufacture of integrated circuits or semiconductor devices. This transmission operation includes, but is not limited to, the direct application of the layout design data for fabrication processes and encompasses any subsequent modification or adaptation thereof undertaken solely for such manufacturing purposes. Nothing herein shall be construed to permit the commercial exploitation of a layout design beyond the scope of this defined means transmission operation, subject to provisions regarding reverse engineering as provided herein.

For the purposes of registration under this Act, "means transmission operation" shall include any process whereby data signals representing a layout design are electronically conveyed from one storage medium or processing unit to another, whether such conveyance is initiated by direct user action or occurs as an automated function within a system. This definition extends to encompass the transfer of layout designs via network connections, optical fibers, radio frequencies, and other analogous means, irrespective of the physical location of the transmitting and receiving devices. Provided that, where a transmission operation results in unauthorized duplication or modification of a registered layout design, such actions shall be deemed infringements under this Act, subject to any limitations prescribed by regulations framed hereunder.

Where an infringement of layout-design rights has occurred, the owner may institute civil proceedings for redress under this Act. Subject to provisions regarding limitation periods, such action must be brought within three years from the date the infringement came to the knowledge of the owner. The remedies available include damages equivalent to the loss suffered by the owner as a direct result of the infringing activity, or a reasonable royalty, whichever is higher. Furthermore, an injunction may be granted restraining the infringer from further engaging in the means transmission operation of the layout-design, and ordering the destruction of infringing copies or materials. Provided that the infringement was committed wilfully, enhanced damages not exceeding five times the actual loss suffered by the owner may be awarded. The court shall also consider any measures taken by the infringer to mitigate the harm caused.

For the purposes of this Act, "means transmission operation" includes the electronic or optical transfer of data representing a layout design from one storage medium to another, whether temporary or permanent, and such transmission shall be deemed an act of reproduction only if it results in a perceptible change to the original layout design. Any person engaged in the commercial provision of services facilitating such means transmission operation shall register with the Controller under procedures as provided herein. The Controller may, by notification in the Official Gazette, prescribe standards for registration and ongoing compliance relating to data security and integrity during transmission. Subject to any contractual agreements between parties, no civil action shall lie against a service provider solely on the basis of an incidental means transmission operation occurring within the normal course of their business. Provided that, such services must adhere to guidelines issued by the Controller regarding measures taken to prevent unauthorized copying or distribution.

For the purposes of this Act, "means transmission operation" includes any instance where data signals are processed and relayed through an integrated circuit layout design without direct human intervention, subject to verification protocols established by the Controller. Such transmission operations shall be deemed to occur when a signal traverses a pathway within the layout-design, irrespective of whether that pathway is actively utilized at any given moment. Provided that, if such transmission operation results in unintended modification or corruption of data signals, it shall not constitute infringement unless demonstrable negligence on the part of the design owner can be established. The Controller may issue guidelines regarding acceptable levels of signal degradation during a means transmission operation to ensure compliance with this Act and prevent frivolous claims.

Any person found to have, without authorization, engaged in the commercial exploitation of a registered layout-design, or having assisted another in so doing, shall be liable for damages. Such damages shall be assessed by considering the lost profits reasonably attributable to the infringing acts and may include compensation for loss of reputation suffered by the registrant. Where the infringement involves the unauthorized means transmission operation of integrated circuits, the Court may also order the destruction of all infringing layouts and any materials derived from them. Further, under this Act, repeated or flagrant infringements shall attract enhanced penalties, including imprisonment for a term not exceeding three years and fines which may extend to ten times the amount of damages proven.

The right to utilize a protected layout design, subject to this Act, may be granted through license agreement executed between the registered proprietor and another party, provided that such agreement explicitly defines the scope of permissible acts. Any assignment of rights under this Act shall include the transfer of all licenses previously granted by the assignee, unless otherwise stipulated in writing within the assignment deed. Furthermore, where a layout design is licensed for commercial exploitation, the means transmission operation relating to reproduction, adaptation or translation thereof requires prior written consent from the registered proprietor, and such consent may be subject to royalty payments as determined through mutual agreement or, failing that, by arbitration under the Arbitration and Conciliation Act. The license holder shall not sub-license the layout design without express authorization, and any unauthorized transmission is deemed a violation of this Act.

For the purposes of determining infringement under this Act, "means transmission operation" shall include any unauthorized reproduction or utilization of a layout-design where such reproduction is achieved through electronic scanning, photomechanical copying, or other technological processes that result in a substantially similar representation. Provided that, the mere observation of a registered layout-design by an individual employed within a manufacturing facility does not, per se, constitute infringement unless it can be demonstrated that such observation facilitated the transmission operation and was undertaken with the express intent to create a competing design. Subject to appeal before the Intellectual Property Appellate Tribunal, evidence presented shall establish both the means and the operation involved in the alleged unauthorized reproduction; failure to do so will render any claim untenable.

For the purposes of this Act, "means transmission operation" includes any instance where data representing a layout design is electronically transferred from one storage medium to another, or between processing units, whether such transfer occurs during manufacturing processes, simulation testing, or routine archival procedures. Such transmissions shall be deemed to occur irrespective of the physical location of the transmitting and receiving devices, provided that the transmission adheres to established protocols as defined by the relevant industry standards body. The Trade Marks Registrar may, upon application from a registered proprietor demonstrating reasonable grounds for concern regarding unauthorized data transfer, issue directives pertaining to secure transmission practices within designated manufacturing facilities. This provision is subject to compliance with prevailing cybersecurity regulations and shall not impede legitimate research activities approved under guidelines issued periodically.

Any person found, upon investigation under this Act, to have engaged in the unauthorized reproduction or importation for commercial purposes of a layout-design, where such act involves the means transmission operation of digital data relating to the said layout-design, shall be liable to pay damages equivalent to ten times the cost of establishing the layout-design. Further, any party seeking to challenge the validity of an infringement claim may submit an affidavit provided registrar, detailing evidence demonstrating fair use or lack of substantial similarity. Failure to comply with procedural requirements outlined herein regarding submission of such affidavits will render them inadmissible during subsequent proceedings. Repeated violations shall attract enhanced penalties as determined by the adjudicating officer and subject to judicial review.

For the purposes of this Act, "means transmission operation" includes any unauthorized reproduction or utilization of a layout design through electronic means, whether directly or indirectly, and irrespective of the number of copies made. This definition shall extend to instances where such reproduction or utilization is undertaken for commercial advantage or gain, subject to exceptions as may be notified by the Central Government. An aggrieved party alleging infringement under this Act may file an appeal before the designated Intellectual Property Tribunal within ninety days from the date of receipt of the order pertaining to the design register. Provided that, if the appellant demonstrates exceptional circumstances preventing timely filing, the Tribunal may condone the delay; such decision shall be subject to further appellate review.

For the purpose of this Act, a design registry is defined as an official record maintained by the Office, containing particulars relating to registered designs and applications for registration. The design registry shall include, but not be limited to, information regarding the applicant’s name and address, the date of application, representations of the design, claims made in respect thereof, and any subsequent modifications or renewals. Access to the design registry may be granted to members of the public subject to payment of prescribed fees and adherence to regulations as provided herein. The Registrar shall ensure that information within the design registry is accurate and readily accessible for inspection.

An application for registration of a layout-design shall be made to the Controller under this Act in such form and containing such particulars as may be prescribed. The applicant shall furnish with the application a representation of the layout-design in the manner specified by the regulations. Upon receipt of an application, the Controller shall acknowledge its receipt and assign it a registration number. The Registrar shall maintain a register of applications for registration, noting the date of filing and the assigned registration number. Any person may inspect the register of applications subject to any conditions imposed by the Controller. An entry in the design registry shall be conclusive evidence of the particulars contained therein relating to the layout-design.

Any person aggrieved by a decision of the Registrar relating to the acceptance or rejection of an application for entry in the design registry, or by any other action taken by the Registrar under this Act, may appeal to the Intellectual Property Appellate Tribunal. Such appeal shall be made within sixty days from the date on which the decision or action was communicated to the appellant. The Tribunal may, after giving notice to the respondent and opportunity of being heard, pass such orders as it deems fit, including ordering the rectification of any error appearing in the design registry. Further, where infringement of a registered layout-design is established, the remedies available shall include damages proportionate to the loss suffered by the owner, and an injunction restraining the infringer from further infringing acts, subject to principles of equity and fairness as provided herein.

An application for registration of a layout-design shall be made to the Controller in such form and containing such particulars as may be prescribed. The applicant shall furnish with the application a representation of the layout-design in the manner specified under this Act, along with an indication of the nature of the integrated circuit it relates to. Upon receipt of an application, the Controller shall issue an acknowledgment thereof and assign it a serial number. Any person interested may, within sixty days from the date of publication of the acceptance of the application for registration, file notice of opposition under this Act. The Controller shall consider any such opposition and may require the applicant or opponent to submit further information or attend hearings as deemed necessary. If the layout-design is found registrable, it shall be entered in the design registry maintained by the Controller.

An application for entry in the design registry shall be accompanied by a certified copy of the first published version of the integrated circuit layout-design, provided that such publication occurred outside India prior to the date of the application. The Registrar may require the applicant to furnish further documentation demonstrating compliance with international standards regarding mask works protection and detailing any modifications made since initial publication. Applications lacking requisite technical specifications or failing to adequately describe the layout-design’s functionality shall be deemed incomplete, and notice thereof will be served upon the applicant under this Act. Any subsequent amendment to an application must adhere strictly to prescribed formats and may incur additional fees as determined by regulations issued in furtherance of this purpose.

Any person who knowingly makes, uses, imports, or offers to sell any integrated circuit layout design infringing a registered layout design shall be liable to pay damages equivalent to five times the actual losses suffered by the owner of the registered layout design. Such losses shall include lost profits and reasonable royalty fees. The Central Government may, upon receiving a complaint from the registrant, issue an injunction restraining further acts of infringement as provided herein. Failure to comply with such an order shall constitute contempt of court and render the offender liable for imprisonment for a term which may extend to two years, or with a fine, or both. Applications for rectification of entries in the design registry are subject to penalties for false statements.

The registered proprietor of a layout-design in the design registry shall be entitled to grant non-exclusive licenses conferring rights to use the protected layout-design. Such licenses may be granted subject to terms and conditions as agreed upon between the proprietor and the licensee, provided that any such agreement explicitly states the scope of permitted acts including reproduction and commercial exploitation. Assignment of a registered layout-design or any interest therein shall require execution of a formal instrument witnessed by at least two witnesses and duly stamped according to prevailing law. The assignee shall be deemed the new registered proprietor under this Act, with all rights and obligations attaching thereto. Any license granted prior to assignment shall remain valid unless expressly terminated in writing by both parties. Further, the Central Government may issue guidelines regarding royalty rates for compulsory licenses as provided herein.

An application for entry in the design registry shall be deemed to be refused if the Controller is satisfied that the layout-design lacks originality or infringes upon any prior right. Any party aggrieved by such a refusal order may appeal to the Intellectual Property Appellate Board within sixty days of receipt of the order, stating the grounds of appeal and accompanied by a certified copy of the refusal order. The Appellate Board shall consider all relevant evidence presented by both the applicant and the Controller and may allow the appeal, dismiss it, or substitute the refusal with a direction for further consideration as deemed appropriate. Provided that the Central Government may, by notification in the Official Gazette, make rules prescribing conditions relating to appeals under this Act.

An application for entry in the design registry shall be made to the Registrar in the prescribed form and accompanied by the requisite fee. The applicant must satisfy the Registrar that they are the rightful trade proprietor registered as the owner of the intellectual property relating to the layout-design sought to be registered, or are otherwise duly authorized to make the application under this Act. Provided that, if an application relates to a layout-design which incorporates elements previously published or used elsewhere, the applicant shall furnish a declaration confirming such prior publication or use and detailing its extent. The Registrar may require further documentation substantiating ownership claims as provided herein, and failure to comply with these requirements will result in rejection of the application.

The owner of a registered design under this Act may grant licenses to any person or entity enabling them to exploit the design in accordance with the terms specified within the license agreement. Such licenses shall be assignable subject to prior written consent from the Design Registry, which consent shall not be unreasonably withheld. Any assignment or sub-license granted without such consent shall be deemed void. Where a layout-design is registered and subsequently incorporated into an application for a patent process, the owner may elect to include details of the design registration within the patent documentation provided that this does not prejudice the rights afforded under this Act. The Design Registry maintains records of all licenses and assignments relating to registered designs and shall publish particulars thereof in such manner as it deems appropriate.

A design registry is constituted under this Act to facilitate the registration of semiconductor integrated circuit layout designs. An application for entry in the design registry shall contain particulars specified by the Authority, including a representation of the layout design and details of the applicant. The Registrar, acting upon representations received from any person aggrieved by a decision of the Authority, may entertain an appeal against such decision. Subject to this Act, the Registrar’s determination regarding the novelty or originality of a layout design shall be final. Provided that, the authority registrar case record relating to registration shall be maintained as per regulations prescribed.

For the purpose of this Act, a “layout design registry” means an entity designated by the Central Government to receive, examine, and process applications for the registration of integrated circuit layout designs. The layout design registry shall maintain a public record detailing all registered layouts, including particulars relating to the applicant, the date of application, and any modifications or subsequent assignments as provided herein. Any person seeking to register a layout design under this Act must submit an application to the layout design registry in the prescribed form, accompanied by requisite fees and supporting documentation demonstrating originality and fixation of the design.

An application for registration of a layout design shall be made to the Controller in such form and containing such particulars as may be prescribed. The applicant shall furnish with the application a representation of the layout design in the manner specified under this Act, including any necessary technical documentation demonstrating its originality and intended functionality. Upon receipt of an application, the Controller may require the applicant to submit further information or clarification regarding the layout design’s features or prior art. A search relating to the layout design shall be conducted by the Registry to ascertain whether a similar layout design is already registered or pending registration. The Controller shall maintain a publicly accessible register of all layouts designs accepted for registration within the layout design registry, detailing the applicant's name and the date of acceptance.

Any person who, without authorization from the registered proprietor, makes, imports, distributes, sells or offers to sell any product which infringes a registered layout design shall be liable to pay damages. Such damages shall be assessed by considering the loss suffered by the proprietor as a result of the infringement, and may include reasonable royalties that the infringer would have paid had they obtained authorization. The Central Government may, through notification, prescribe guidelines for determining such damages. Further, an application for interim injunction restraining the infringing activity may be made to the Commercial Court having jurisdiction over the matter, subject to demonstrating a strong prima facie case of infringement under this Act. A proprietor seeking remedies shall provide evidence establishing their ownership and validity of registration within the layout design registry.

An application for registration of a layout design shall be made to the Controller in such form and containing such particulars as may be prescribed. The applicant shall furnish with the application a representation of the layout design in accordance with the regulations framed under this Act; provided that if the representation is in three dimensions, it shall be accompanied by views from different angles. Upon receipt of an application, the Controller shall issue an acknowledgment to the applicant and assign to the application a serial number. The Controller may require the applicant to submit further information or clarification regarding the layout design or the application itself. Any person aggrieved by any decision taken by the Controller relating to the acceptance or rejection of an application for registration in the layout design registry may prefer an appeal to the Appellate Board within sixty days from the date of communication of such decision.

An application for entry in the layout design registry shall be accompanied by a certified copy of the circuit diagrams pertaining to the layout design, demonstrating its unique characteristics. Such application must also include a declaration verifying that the applicant is the first owner of the layout design and possesses exclusive rights therein, subject to any prior agreements or assignments disclosed within the application. The Registrar may require further documentation substantiating ownership claims if deemed necessary for compliance with this Act. An applicant failing to provide all requisite information as stipulated herein shall have their application rejected without further notice. Any alteration to a registered layout design requires notification to the registry and approval, provided that such alterations do not substantially deviate from the original registration.

Any person who knowingly makes, uses, imports, or offers to sell any integrated circuit layout design infringing a registered layout design shall be liable to pay damages equivalent to five times the cost of the infringing device or process. Where such infringement is committed for commercial gain, the Court may, in addition to awarding damages, impose a further penalty not exceeding two million rupees. An application alleging infringement under this Act may be filed with the competent civil court having jurisdiction over the place where the cause of action arose; provided that the Central Government may, by notification, designate specific courts to exercise such jurisdiction. The layout design registry shall maintain a publicly accessible record of all registered layout designs and related enforcement actions.

Subject to the provisions of this Act, any registered owner of a layout design may grant a license to use the layout design in return for consideration. Such licenses may be exclusive or non-exclusive, and may relate to all or part of the rights conferred by registration under this Act. The terms and conditions of any such license shall be recorded with the Semiconductor Integrated Circuits Layout-Design Registry, along with details of the licensee and the duration of the license. Assignment of a registered layout design, including assignment of licenses granted in respect thereof, may occur subject to prior notification to the Registry. Any person acquiring an interest in a layout design by way of license or assignment shall be deemed to hold such interest as tenant-in-common with the original registrant unless otherwise specified in the recorded documentation maintained at the Layout Design Registry.

An application for entry in the layout design registry shall be deemed to have been rejected if the Registrar is satisfied that the layout design incorporates elements substantially derived from a previously registered layout design without due acknowledgement or authorization. Such rejection may be challenged by the applicant within sixty days of receipt of notification under this Act, through a written appeal submitted to the Controller. The Controller shall consider any evidence presented by the applicant demonstrating independent creation or legitimate use of the disputed elements, and may order further investigation if necessary. Decisions of the Controller are subject to judicial review as provided herein, but only on grounds limited to errors apparent on the face of the record concerning procedural fairness in the appeal process.

An application for entry of a layout-design into the layout design registry shall be deemed to have been improperly filed if it fails to accurately reflect the technical documentation submitted alongside. Any party aggrieved by an erroneous refusal of registration under this Act may appeal such decision within sixty days from the date of communication of the order, presenting evidence demonstrating compliance with the prescribed standards for layout-design protection. The Appellate Authority shall consider arguments pertaining to the originality and fixation of the layout-design, subject to a determination that it does not substantially replicate an existing registered work. Further, any applicant disputing the validity of another’s registration may initiate proceedings challenging the entry in the registry, provided that such challenge is made within three years from the date of publication of the registration.

For the purposes of this Act, the term "design registry central" refers to the designated authority responsible for maintaining records pertaining to registered designs and related applications. The design registry central shall maintain a publicly accessible electronic database containing details of all registered designs, including but not limited to the name and address of the claimant, the date of registration, and a graphical representation of the design. Applications for registration shall be processed by officers appointed by the Central Government, subject to appeals being heard before an appellate tribunal as provided herein. The design registry central may issue certificates of registration in the prescribed form.

An application for registration of a layout-design shall be made to the design registry central in the prescribed form and accompanied by the requisite fee. The applicant shall furnish such particulars relating to the layout-design as are required under this Act, including detailed schematics and descriptions demonstrating originality. Upon receipt of an application, the Registry may request further clarification or modifications to ensure compliance with the provisions herein. A search report pertaining to existing registered designs shall be provided to the applicant within thirty days. The design registry central shall maintain a publicly accessible record of all registered layout-designs, subject to any confidentiality requests as permitted under this Act and in accordance with established procedures.

Where a registered layout design has been infringed, the owner shall be entitled to seek relief in respect of damages sustained by reason of such infringement. Such damages shall include compensation for loss of profits, reasonable royalties, and any other consequential losses directly attributable to the infringing activity. The Central Government may, through notification, prescribe procedures for assessing and awarding these damages, subject to principles of fairness and equity. Further, an injunction may be granted by a competent court restraining the infringer from continuing such infringement, provided that the owner demonstrates a reasonable likelihood of further harm. Applications concerning rectification or invalidation of registrations shall be made to the design registry central, which shall adjudicate upon them according to established rules of procedure as provided herein.

Applications for registration of a layout-design shall be made to the design registry central in the prescribed form and accompanied by the requisite fee. The Registrar may require the applicant to furnish such further information or submit such additional documents as are necessary for proper examination of the application. Upon receipt of an application, the design registry central shall assign it a serial number and notify the applicant accordingly. Any person interested in the registration proceeding may, subject to conditions prescribed by regulations made under this Act, file objections within three months from the date of publication of the notification of the acceptance of the layout-design for examination. The Registrar shall consider any such objection and provide an opportunity for the applicant to be heard before making a decision. Decisions of the design registry central are appealable to the Intellectual Property Appellate Board as provided herein.

Applications for registration of a layout-design shall be made to the design registry central, in the prescribed form and accompanied by the requisite fee. The Registrar may require the applicant to furnish further particulars or submit additional documentation demonstrating compliance with the originality requirements as provided herein. Any application containing false representations concerning prior publication or use of the layout-design shall be deemed invalid under this Act. Subject to appeal to the Intellectual Property Appellate Board, the Registrar’s decision regarding the validity of an application is final. The applicant shall provide a clear and detailed representation of the integrated circuit layout being claimed for registration. Failure to do so may result in rejection of the application.

Any person who knowingly makes, uses, imports, or offers to sell any integrated circuit layout design infringing a registered layout design shall be liable to pay damages equivalent to five times the actual losses suffered by the owner of the registered layout design. The Central Government may, upon receiving a complaint from the aggrieved party, direct the Design Registry Central to investigate allegations of infringement and issue interim injunctions restraining the defendant from further acts of infringement pending final determination. Failure to comply with such an order shall constitute contempt of court and render the defaulter liable for penalties as determined by the presiding officer. The owner may also seek Anton Pillar orders under this Act to preserve evidence related to alleged infringements.

The owner of a registered semiconductor integrated circuit layout-design shall be entitled to grant licenses granting rights of use relating to the design, subject to conditions specified in the license agreement. Such licenses may be exclusive or non-exclusive, and the terms thereof shall be binding on all parties involved. Assignment of ownership or any such license requires registration with the design registry central, and notice published in the Official Gazette. Any subsequent transfer of rights must also be registered as provided herein to maintain validity. The Central Government may issue guidelines regarding royalty rates for licenses granted under this Act, ensuring equitable compensation to the owner while facilitating access for authorized users. Failure to register an assignment or license shall render it voidable at the option of any aggrieved party.

An application for registration of a layout-design shall be deemed to be improperly presented if it fails to clearly indicate the nature of the design and its intended use, subject to an appeal to the Intellectual Property Appellate Tribunal within sixty days from the date of communication of such determination. The Central Government may, by notification in the Official Gazette, establish regional offices of the design registry central for efficient processing of applications; however, any decision made by a regional office regarding acceptance or rejection of an application is subject to review by the head office and further appeal as provided herein. Any party aggrieved by a decision concerning the validity of a registered layout-design may institute proceedings before the Tribunal, demonstrating substantial prejudice arising from the alleged infringement.

Any person aggrieved by an order passed under this Act relating to the refusal of registration or revocation of a registered layout-design may appeal to the Intellectual Property Appellate Tribunal. Such appeals shall be made within sixty days from the date of communication of the order and shall be accompanied by such fees as may be prescribed. Failure to pay the requisite fee shall render the appeal inadmissible. The Central Government may, by notification in the Official Gazette, establish a *design registry central* for facilitating efficient processing of applications and maintaining records relating to layout-designs. Registered layout-designs are entitled to *exclusive rights* under this Act, and any infringement shall be subject to penalties as provided herein.

The design registry central to the administration of this Act shall comprise a Director and such other officers and employees as the Central Government deems necessary. Applications for registration of a layout-design shall be examined by an Investigating Officer appointed under this Act who shall ascertain whether the layout-design is original, valid, and not contrary to any provision herein. The Investigating Officer may require the applicant to submit further particulars or modifications to the layout-design as deemed appropriate during the procedure investigation. Any decision of the Director concerning registration is subject to appeal before such appellate authority as may be notified by the Central Government.

Any person aggrieved by an order passed under this Act relating to the rectification of the design registry central or concerning the invalidity of a registered layout-design may appeal to the Intellectual Property Appellate Tribunal. Such appeals shall be made within sixty days from the date of communication of the order and must specify the grounds upon which it is based, supported by relevant evidence. Failure to comply with these procedural requirements shall render the appeal inadmissible. Where a layout-design incorporates elements derived from a breeder registered variety, any challenge to its validity concerning those elements shall be subject to additional scrutiny regarding compliance with plant variety protection regulations. Remedies available on appeal include orders for injunctions preventing unauthorized copying and damages proportionate to the loss suffered by the aggrieved party.

An application for registration of a layout-design shall be accompanied by such particulars, drawings, photographs or other representations as are necessary to adequately define the design. The Registrar may require the applicant to furnish further information or clarification concerning the layout-design and its claimed originality, provided that such requests shall not unduly delay the processing of the application. Upon receipt of an application, the Registrar shall assign it a serial number and acknowledge its receipt to the applicant. A search of existing registered designs and pending applications shall be conducted as part of the design registry exercise. The applicant may request a certified copy of the search results under this Act. Any person aggrieved by a decision of the Registrar relating to registration may appeal to the designated appellate authority.

Where a registered layout design is infringed, the owner shall be entitled to seek remedies under this Act. Any person who, without authorization from the registered proprietor, makes, imports, sells, or offers to sell any product which infringes the registered layout design shall be deemed guilty of an offence and liable to pay damages as determined by the competent court. The amount of damages may include compensation for loss of profits, reasonable royalties, and other consequential losses suffered by the owner. Further, a person found in violation of these provisions may also face imprisonment for a term which may extend to two years. Application for rectification of entries in the design registry exercise shall be made within five years from the date of registration, subject to conditions as provided herein.

An application for registration of a layout-design shall contain particulars verifying ownership or right to apply, including details of prior publication. The Registrar may require submission of technical documentation demonstrating conformity with prescribed standards relating to circuit functionality; failure to comply will result in rejection. Any person claiming entitlement to the design, subject to fulfilling conditions as provided herein regarding assignment or inheritance, may file an application within three years from the date of first commercial exploitation anywhere globally. The design registry exercise is contingent upon a search confirming no identical layout-design exists already registered under this Act. Objections raised by third parties must be addressed through written submissions and supporting evidence before acceptance.

Any person who, having knowledge of a registered layout design, without authorization from the registered proprietor, makes, imports, sells, or offers to sell any integrated circuit embodying that design shall be liable to pay damages. Such damages shall be assessed at an amount not less than five times the cost of the infringing integrated circuits produced, imported, sold, or offered for sale, and not exceeding ten times such cost. The Central Government may, by notification in the Official Gazette, prescribe a procedure for determining the said costs. Failure to comply with prescribed procedures during a design registry exercise constitutes an offence punishable with imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years, or with fine, or both, as provided herein.

The owner of a registered layout design shall be entitled to grant licenses conferring rights to utilize the design, subject to the terms and conditions stipulated in the license agreement. Such agreements may include provisions regarding royalty payments, duration of exclusivity, and permitted geographical territories for exploitation of the layout-design. Assignment of ownership under this Act requires registration with the Design Registry exercise, and any such assignment shall be deemed operative only upon inscription in the Register. A licensee may further assign their rights to utilize the design, provided that prior written consent from the registered owner is obtained and documented within the relevant registry records. Failure to adhere to these stipulations renders any subsequent utilization or assignment voidable at the discretion of the original layout-design owner.

An application for registration of a layout-design shall be deemed to have been improperly filed if it fails to include a declaration by the applicant affirming originality and lawful derivation, subject to appeal before the Intellectual Property Appellate Tribunal. Any party aggrieved by a decision of the Registrar relating to acceptance or rejection of an application during the design registry exercise may within sixty days from the date of such decision file an appeal to the Tribunal. The Tribunal shall consider evidence presented by both the applicant and any objector, and may order further investigation if necessary. Decisions of the Tribunal are final, provided that a further appeal lies only to the Supreme Court on grounds specified under this Act concerning questions of law.

An application for registration of a layout-design shall include particulars prescribed under this Act relating to the applicant and the layout-design. The Controller General may require the applicant to furnish further information or submit certified copies of documents as deemed necessary for examination. A design registry exercise involves scrutiny by the Registry to ascertain compliance with all applicable provisions, including originality and absence of prior publication. Where a registered layout-design is subsequently the subject of a patent, that patent shall cease to have effect to the extent it relates to elements of the layout-design.

An application for registration of a layout-design shall be made to the Registrar in the prescribed form and accompanied by the requisite fee. The applicant shall furnish such particulars relating to the layout-design as are required under this Act, including detailed schematics and a description of its functionality. Upon receipt of an application, the Registrar may direct the applicant to rectify any deficiencies or provide further clarification. If the Registrar finds that the layout-design is registrable, subject to fulfilling all procedural requirements, he shall proceed with the design registry exercise as provided herein. Any person aggrieved by a decision of the Registrar relating to registration may appeal to the relevant instituted district court within sixty days from the date of such decision.

An application for registration of a design shall be accompanied by an affidavit verifying the correctness of particulars contained therein, including details pertaining to the proprietor’s entitlement to apply. The Registrar shall, upon receipt of such an application and after conducting a preliminary examination as provided herein, issue a notification inviting objections from any person claiming an interest in the design. Any objection received within the prescribed period may be considered by the Registrar, who shall provide the applicant with an opportunity for response before proceeding further. Should the Registrar deem the application to be in order following consideration of any objections and verification of the design affidavit registered, he or she may proceed with the registration process. The design registry exercise involves a rigorous assessment of novelty and originality, subject to established legal precedents.

For the purpose of this Act, a ‘layout design’ includes features relating to the arrangement or interconnection of elements which define an integrated circuit. The term 'element' shall encompass any circuitry, semiconductor material, or other component incorporated within the layout design. Where an application for registration is received, and the Controller determines that the layout design incorporates original features not previously disclosed, the registry shall place the application on record pending examination as to novelty and inventive step. Provided that such placement does not constitute a grant of exclusive rights under this Act, and subject to any objections raised by third parties within the prescribed period.

Upon receipt of an application for registration of a layout-design, accompanied by the prescribed fee, the registry shall place the application on record and assign it a unique identification number. The applicant shall furnish such documentary evidence as the registry deems necessary to establish ownership and originality of the layout-design. Where the layout-design incorporates elements previously registered under this Act, the registry may require a declaration detailing the nature and extent of such incorporation. Further, if any objection is raised by an interested party within the stipulated period, the registry shall place the objection on record and provide the applicant with an opportunity for rebuttal. The registry’s decision regarding objections shall be final subject to appeal under this Act.

Where a registered proprietor alleges that any person has contravened section 10 relating to unauthorized reproduction or importation of a protected integrated circuit layout-design, the aggrieved party shall institute proceedings before the relevant jurisdictional authority. Upon receipt of such an allegation and after providing due notice to all parties concerned, the registry shall place the matter for preliminary assessment regarding the prima facie validity of the claim. The Central Government may, subject to guidelines issued by it, direct the registry to undertake further investigation into any aspect of the alleged contravention. Any party dissatisfied with the findings of the registry following such an assessment may appeal to the Intellectual Property Appellate Tribunal within a period specified under this Act. Remedies available upon successful adjudication shall include injunctions and damages as provided herein.

Upon receipt of an application for registration of a layout-design, the Registrar shall conduct a preliminary examination to ascertain compliance with the prescribed formalities under this Act. If the application is found deficient in any manner, the Registrar shall issue a notification specifying the deficiencies and providing a period not exceeding thirty days within which the applicant may rectify them. Following such rectification or failure thereof, the registry shall place the application before the Layout-Design Examination Board for detailed scrutiny regarding novelty and originality as defined herein. The board’s recommendation, whether favorable or adverse to registration, shall be recorded in writing and forwarded to the Registrar. Where an objection is raised concerning a prior publication of the layout-design, the applicant shall have the opportunity to submit a written response demonstrating its distinctiveness. Subsequently, the registry shall place all relevant documentation before the Controller for final determination.

Where an application for registration of a layout-design is received by the Registry, the Registrar shall examine whether the applicant has complied with all prescribed formalities under this Act. Provided that if the application contains any deficiencies or omissions, the Registrar shall communicate such deficiencies to the applicant in writing, allowing a period not exceeding sixty days for rectification. Subsequently, subject to satisfaction regarding compliance and payment of requisite fees, the registry shall place the layout-design on public display for a minimum period of thirty days, inviting objections from interested parties as provided herein. Any objection received during this period shall be duly considered before proceeding with registration, ensuring adherence to principles of natural justice.

Where an application for registration of a layout-design is found to be in contravention of any provision under this Act or the regulations framed thereunder, the Registrar shall issue a notice requiring the applicant to rectify the deficiencies within a period not exceeding ninety days. Failure to comply with such notice shall result in the rejection of the application and the registry shall place a record of said rejection on the public register, noting the reasons for non-compliance. Any person aggrieved by an order rejecting an application may appeal to the Intellectual Property Appellate Tribunal within sixty days from the date of communication of the order. The tribunal’s decision is final, subject to further appeals as provided herein and penalties for wilful disregard of this process are prescribed under Chapter VI.

Where a registered layout-design owner desires to grant a license conferring rights to utilize the protected design, or to assign the entire ownership thereof, an application in the prescribed form shall be submitted to the Registry. Such applications concerning licenses shall specify the scope and duration of the permitted utilization, including details regarding any royalty payments due to the original owner under this Act. The registry shall place a record of such assignments or licenses on its public register, clearly identifying the assignor, assignee, licensor, and licensee, alongside the effective date and terms agreed upon. Provided that, any assignment or license granted prior to registration remains valid and enforceable, subject to the conditions stipulated therein. Further, the Registry may require supporting documentation demonstrating a clear chain of title where ownership has been transferred multiple times.

Where an application for registration of a layout-design is received, the registry shall place the application on record and issue an acknowledgment to the applicant. Any person aggrieved by any decision of the Registry relating to the acceptance or rejection of an application, or concerning the determination of priority under this Act, may within sixty days from the date of such decision file an appeal to the Intellectual Property Appellate Tribunal. The tribunal shall consider all relevant material placed before it and may allow or dismiss the appeal, subject to just terms and conditions as it deems fit. Provided that the applicant demonstrates demonstrable prejudice resulting from any procedural irregularity in the Registry’s actions, the appellate tribunal may order a rehearing by the registry.

For the purposes of this Act, a ‘design mark’ is defined as any symbol, letter, numeral, device, trademark or representation of an identifiable characteristic which is capable of distinguishing goods or services of one undertaking from those of another and shall be registrable if it is not descriptive of the characteristics or quality of such goods or services. The registry shall place design marks submitted for registration in a register of design marks, subject to verification by the Office under this Act. A party proceeding notwithstanding any opposition filed against a design mark application may submit counter-arguments within the timeframe prescribed as provided herein.

Where an application for registration of a layout-design is received by the Registry, the Registrar shall examine it in accordance with the provisions herein. If the Registrar considers that the applicant has complied with all requirements under this Act and the regulations made thereunder, the registry shall place the application on record for further processing. The registrar may require the applicant to submit such additional information or clarification as deemed necessary to ascertain compliance. Upon satisfactory verification of originality and novelty, a notice of acceptance will be published in the Official Gazette. Following publication, any person aggrieved by the proposed registration may file an objection within the prescribed time. Subsequently, if no valid objections are received, or all objections have been resolved satisfactorily, the proprietor registered layout shall be formally entered into the Register of Layout-Designs.

Upon receipt of an application for registration of a layout-design, the Registry shall place the application on record and assign it a unique identification number. The Registrar may require the applicant to submit further particulars or modifications to the application as deemed necessary for clarity and compliance with this Act. Any person aggrieved by a decision of the Registry relating to the acceptance or rejection of an application, or concerning any procedural matter under this Act, may appeal to the Intellectual Property Appellate Tribunal. Where it is determined, following judicial review, that a layout-design has been reproduced in violation of the provisions herein and with intent to deceive, the court directed forfeiture of all infringing copies and materials used in their creation shall be enacted without prejudice to any other remedies available under this Act or general law. The Registry shall maintain a publicly accessible record of all registered layout-designs as provided herein.

An application for registration of a semiconductor integrated circuit layout-design may be opposed by any person claiming an interest in the design or alleging that the registered layout-design infringes upon rights vested in them. Such opposition shall be made within three months from the date of publication of the acceptance of the application under this Act. The Registrar, after providing due opportunity for hearing to both the applicant and the opponent, may allow or dismiss the opposition. If the opposition is allowed, the registration shall stand cancelled as if it had never been effected; provided that any subsequent registrations deriving rights from the original registration are not thereby affected. Any party aggrieved by an order of the Registrar relating to cancellation registration may appeal to the Intellectual Property Appellate Tribunal within sixty days.

An application for the registration of a semiconductor integrated circuit layout-design may be subject to challenge and subsequent cancellation by any person alleging that the design does not satisfy the requirements of originality as provided herein, or that the applicant has misrepresented any material fact in relation to the design. Such an application for cancellation shall be made within four years from the date of registration, and must specify the grounds upon which it is based, supported by all relevant evidence. The Registrar may entertain such an application if satisfied that it is not frivolous or vexatious. Upon receiving a valid application for cancellation, the Registrar shall afford the registrant an opportunity to present its response and counter-evidence. A decision regarding cancellation registration shall be made after due consideration of both parties’ submissions.

An application for the *cancellation registration* of a semiconductor integrated circuit layout-design may be presented to the Controller by any person claiming an interest arising from a violation of this Act or any other law relating to intellectual property. Such application shall state the grounds upon which it is based, and shall specify the date from which such cancellation should take effect. The Controller shall serve notice of the application on the registered proprietor, affording them a reasonable opportunity to be heard in their defense, including presenting evidence and arguments against the proposed cancellation. Subject to any procedural requirements as provided herein, the Controller may require the applicant to furnish security for costs. If, after considering all relevant materials presented by both parties, the Controller finds merit in the application, an order of *cancellation registration* shall be issued, specifying the reasons for such decision and the effective date thereof.

An application for the cancellation registration of a layout-design may be presented to the Controller by any person claiming an interest adversely affected by the registration. Such application shall specify the grounds upon which it is based, including but not limited to instances where the layout-design was registered in contravention of section 7 or section 8 under this Act. The applicant must provide evidence substantiating the claims made within the application; failure to do so may result in its rejection. The Controller shall afford the registrant an opportunity to file a counter-statement responding to the allegations, and both parties shall be given reasonable time for such submissions. A decision regarding cancellation registration will only be rendered after due consideration of all relevant materials presented.

An application for the cancellation registration of a layout-design may be presented to the Controller by any person claiming an interest adversely affected by the registration. Such application shall state the grounds upon which it is based, and shall be accompanied by all relevant documents substantiating those grounds. The Controller shall serve notice on the registrant, affording them a reasonable opportunity to file a counter-statement. Failure of the registrant to respond within the prescribed period shall not preclude the Controller from proceeding with the application. If, after considering the submissions of both parties and any supporting evidence, the Controller finds merit in the cancellation grounds, registration shall be revoked. Any party aggrieved by an order granting or refusing cancellation may appeal under this Act to the Intellectual Property Tribunal.

The registered proprietor of a semiconductor integrated circuit layout-design may grant licenses or assign the entire interest in their registration to any person, subject to the terms and conditions stipulated in the agreement. Such licenses shall be enforceable as if they were covenants running with the land, provided that the licensee’s activities do not directly infringe upon another party's registered layout-design rights. Any assignment of a registration requires prior written consent from the Controller General, who may impose reasonable royalty obligations to protect competing interests.
