Provided that such documentation is deemed insufficient, a request for further clarification or experimental data shall be issued. The applicant shall comply with this request within the timeframe prescribed herein; failure to do so may result in rejection of the patent application.

Where a patentee, prior to the sealing of the register, has granted an exclusive license relating to the use or exploitation of any invention claimed in the patent application, such license shall be recorded in the prescribed manner within the register. The recordation shall include details of the licensee and the scope of the rights conferred under the license agreement. Subject to compliance with this Act, a licensee may assign their rights arising from such exclusive license to another party, provided that notice of any such assignment is also recorded on the register. An invention shall be deemed capable of industrial application if it can be manufactured or used in an industry, and where an exclusive license has been granted impacting its exploitation, the patentee retains responsibility for ensuring continued compliance with provisions relating to working requirements under this Act.

An applicant desiring to obtain a patent shall file an application with the Patent Office in the prescribed form, accompanied by the requisite fee. The application must disclose the invention clearly and completely for enabling any person skilled in the art to put the same into practice. Where the application relates to more than one invention, each of which is separately patentable, the applicant may include them in a single application, provided that they relate to a common subject matter. However, the examination process under this Act shall consider each such invention individually for novelty and inventive step. The particulars required in an application sub section (1) must be meticulously adhered to, failing which the application is liable to rejection. Any alteration made after the date of filing requires notification to the Controller.

An applicant seeking examination of a patent application shall, at the time of filing the application, furnish particulars relating to priority if claiming right of priority under this Act. The Controller may require the applicant to submit such further information or documents as he deems necessary for determining whether the claim relates to an invention that is novel and involves inventive step. Where an application contains multiple claims, each claim shall be clearly defined and supported by the description and drawings, if any, accompanying the application. Any amendment to the claims made after the first examination shall only be allowed if such amendment does not alter the scope of protection sought as originally disclosed in the application. The applicant’s attention is drawn to the provisions regarding the procedure for filing a request for pre-grant opposition under this Act and the timelines applicable thereto, particularly concerning the interpretation of *application sub section* (2) pertaining to grounds for objection.

An applicant seeking patent protection shall, in the application, clearly define the scope of the invention claimed, specifying all essential elements contributing to its novelty and inventive step. The description accompanying the application must disclose the invention in a manner sufficiently clear and complete as to enable any person skilled in the art to make and use it, provided that such disclosure does not compromise trade secrets legitimately maintained by the applicant. Where an application incorporates subject matter derived from prior publications or publicly available knowledge, the applicant shall provide documented evidence demonstrating diligent efforts undertaken to secure necessary authorizations or licenses relating thereto. The Controller may require further clarification under this *application sub section* if ambiguities exist regarding the claimed invention’s boundaries.

An applicant seeking grant of a patent shall, in the application, clearly and concisely describe the invention and how it can be performed, failing which the application is liable for rejection under this Act. Any false representation concerning the nature of the invention made within the application shall render the applicant subject to penalties as provided herein, including but not limited to fines extending up to one hundred thousand rupees and potential revocation of any patent subsequently granted based on that fraudulent disclosure. Furthermore, where an application sub section contains information deliberately concealed or misrepresented to mislead the Controller, a subsequent infringement action may be barred against any party demonstrably relying upon the published, inaccurate details.

Where an applicant for a patent, prior to grant, has entered into a contractual agreement assigning rights in the invention to another party, such assignment shall be recorded with the Patents Office within three months of the execution of the agreement. The application sub section (2) provides that any subsequent assignee may also record their interest upon providing satisfactory proof of title and payment of prescribed fees. Further, where an application has been made jointly by two or more applicants, and a license is granted to a third party relating to the invention claimed in the patent, such licensee shall be deemed to hold assignable rights subject to the terms of the license agreement as provided herein. The Controller may require submission of the complete licensing agreement for verification purposes. This provision does not preclude any applicant from retaining ownership or exercising rights pertaining to the patented invention.

An applicant aggrieved by a decision of the Controller rejecting an application, or requiring amendment thereof, may appeal to the Intellectual Property Appellate Board. Such appeal shall lie within sixty days from the date of communication of the order; provided that the Board may entertain appeals filed after the expiry of the said period if satisfactory reasons are tendered for the delay. The applicant bears the burden of demonstrating that the Controller’s decision was manifestly erroneous, particularly concerning the interpretation of novelty as applied under this Act to the invention claimed in the application sub section. The Board shall hear arguments from both parties and may direct the Controller to reconsider any aspect of the original determination.

An applicant seeking registration of an invention shall, in the application, clearly and concisely describe the technical field to which the invention relates and state the nature of the inventive step comprising the claimed invention. The Controller may require the applicant to amend the description or claims if they are unclear, ambiguous, or do not meet the standards prescribed under this Act. Where an application is filed jointly by two or more applicants, the rights and obligations of each applicant shall be governed as provided herein. A trade marks proprietor seeking to utilize a patented process must obtain prior written consent from the patent holder, subject to conditions determined by the Controller. The application sub section (2) provides that any person aggrieved by an order made under this Act may appeal to the Appellate Board within sixty days of such order.

Where an applicant, being a person resident outside India, seeks protection for an invention in India based on an international application form filed under the Patent Cooperation Treaty, the application shall comply with all requirements as provided herein. Failure to submit a complete and accurate international application form, including requisite translations where applicable, will render the application liable for rejection. Any attempt to circumvent these procedural safeguards through misrepresentation or concealment of information within the application sub section relating to priority claims shall be deemed an offence punishable with imprisonment and a fine not less than fifty thousand rupees. The Controller may, at any stage, require further clarification or documentation regarding the international application form.

An applicant seeking registration of a utility model may file an initial disclosure document in lieu of a formal application; however, such initial disclosure must be followed by a full application within six months from the date of its receipt. The initial disclosure shall contain sufficient particulars to enable a person skilled in the art to understand and implement the invention. Where an initial disclosure is filed, it shall be treated as a provisional specification for the purposes of this Act. A complete specification, including claims, abstract, and drawings where necessary, must be submitted within the stipulated timeframe; failure to do so will render the initial disclosure void. The provisional specification complete requirement applies irrespective of whether the invention relates to a process or an article.

Where a patent applicant has submitted a provisional specification relating to an invention, and subsequently seeks to assign or license rights in respect of that invention prior to the filing of a complete specification, such assignment or license shall be conditional upon the timely submission of said complete specification as provided herein. The terms of any agreement granting a license may include provisions for royalty payments calculated on potential future sales based on projections derived from the provisional disclosure, subject to adjustment should the granted patent’s scope differ materially from that initially claimed. Further, an applicant who has entered into an assignment or licensing agreement predicated upon a provisional specification complete shall be obligated to notify all assignees and licensees of any material amendments made to the invention during the period preceding the filing of the complete specification. Failure to provide such notification may render the assignee or licensee entitled to damages.

Subject to the provisions of this Act, any patentee desiring to grant a license in respect of a patented pharmaceutical product, or assign the rights pertaining thereto, shall provide a detailed inventory of all relevant documentation submitted during the prosecution of the patent, including but not limited to the provisional specification complete and subsequent amendments. This disclosure is mandatory irrespective of whether the license agreement concerns domestic manufacture or export patented pharmaceutical products for sale in foreign territories. The Controller may require further clarification regarding the scope of such licenses or assignments, particularly concerning royalties and sub-licensing arrangements. Any party receiving a license or assignment shall be bound by the terms stipulated within the patent grant itself, as well as any additional conditions imposed by the patentee relating to quality control measures for exported goods. Failure to comply with these disclosure requirements may render the license or assignment voidable under this Act.

For the purposes of this Act, shall priority date means the date first mentioned in the application as filed, or if the application was presented with a request for the appointment of a hearing, the date of that request, whichever is earlier. Where an applicant seeks to claim priority under this Act from an earlier application made in another country, such earlier application shall be deemed to be the original application for the purposes of determining novelty and inventive step, subject to any modifications as may be prescribed. The Controller may require evidence establishing the validity of the claimed priority date before proceeding with examination.

Where an applicant seeks to obtain a patent for an invention already described in a publication before the date of filing of the application, or where the invention was otherwise made available to the public before such date, the Controller may require the applicant to satisfy him that the invention did not at the time fall within the scope of any prior art. In determining whether an invention is obvious or anticipated under this Act, the publication shall be deemed to have been published on its advertised date, if any; otherwise, on the date it first became available to the public. For the purposes of assessing novelty and inventive step, the applicant shall priority date shall be taken into account in relation to such prior publications. Any person aggrieved by a decision under this provision may appeal to the Appellate Board within sixty days from the date of receipt of the order.

Where an applicant seeks to establish a shall priority date for a patent application filed in India, they must demonstrate that a corresponding earlier application was previously filed in a Convention country. Failure to provide satisfactory evidence of such prior filing within the prescribed period as provided herein will render the Indian application liable for rejection under this Act. The Controller may require the applicant to furnish particulars relating to the known patent office where the earlier application was made, including dates and reference numbers. Any attempt to fraudulently claim a priority date or mislead the Controller regarding the details of the prior application shall be deemed an offense punishable with imprisonment and a substantial monetary penalty.

For the purposes of this Act, shall priority date means the date first mentioned in the application as filed; provided that where an applicant claims priority from one or more earlier applications under the Paris Convention for the Protection of Industrial Property or the Protocol thereto, the said priority date shall be determined according to the rules prescribed herein. Where a claim specification amendment is made after the initial filing and incorporates subject matter not disclosed in the original application, the determination of the priority date shall remain anchored to the earliest disclosure consistent with the requirements of novelty and inventive step as provided herein.

The Registering Authority shall examine each specification to ascertain whether the claims are supported by the disclosure contained therein. A specification shall be deemed to support a claim if it describes the invention claimed with sufficient clarity and completeness for persons skilled in the art to carry out the invention. Where an applicant seeks to register a patent, the particulars of each specification claim must be clearly delineated within Schedule B appended to the application form; failure to adhere to this requirement may result in rejection under this Act. The Registrar may require further clarification regarding any ambiguity present in the specification claims and such clarifications shall be treated as part of the original filing. Provided that, amendments to a specification claim are permissible only if they do not alter the scope of protection sought.

Where an invention infringes a patent granted under this Act, the patentee shall be entitled to seek remedies including, but not limited to, permanent injunctions restraining the infringing party from further exploitation of the patented technology. The determination of infringement shall hinge upon whether the accused product or process falls within the scope of any one or more of the claims in the specification claim. Provided that, a finding of literal infringement is not required; equitable estoppel may be invoked where the alleged infringer has knowingly adopted practices substantially similar to those disclosed in the patent’s description. Subject to demonstrating reasonable grounds for believing the patent invalid, a party may challenge the validity of a patent by way of revocation proceedings before the Controller. The patentee shall bear the burden of proving that the specification claim clearly defines the scope of protection granted.

The Controller may, upon receipt of an objection from any person regarding the clarity or precision of a specification claim, direct the applicant to amend said claim within a period not exceeding sixty days from the date of such direction. Such amendment shall be permissible only if it does not alter the essence of the invention as originally disclosed in the complete specification and is consistent with the matter described therein. The Controller shall provide written reasons for any rejection of an amended claim, stating specifically how the amendment fails to meet the requirements under this Act relating to clarity and support within the original disclosure. An applicant aggrieved by such a direction may appeal to the Appellate Board as provided herein. Failure to comply with the Controller’s direction within the stipulated period shall render the specification claim liable for rejection. The determination of whether an amended specification claim is consistent with the complete specification shall be subject to judicial review.

Any person aggrieved by an order relating to the revocation of a patent, or the rectification of a specification claim, may appeal to the Appellate Board within sixty days from the date of such order. The Appellate Board shall have power to entertain appeals under this Act and shall pass such orders as it deems fit, subject to the provisions herein. Failure to comply with the prescribed timelines for filing an appeal shall render the appellant liable to a penalty not exceeding fifty thousand rupees, recoverable by way of fine. Further, any party seeking enforcement of a patent granted under this Act may apply to the relevant High Court for appropriate remedies in cases of infringement, provided that such application is made within three years from the date of the order appealed against.

Subject to the provisions of this Act, any patentee may grant an exclusive license to use or exercise their patented invention relating to a particular field of application described within the specification. Such licenses shall be assignable by the patentee, either wholly or partially, and may include the right to make, sell, hire, or import the patented article. The scope of such assignment shall not extend beyond the boundaries defined by the original specification claim, unless expressly agreed upon in writing between the parties involved. Further, any sub-license granted under an exclusive license is deemed an assignment for the purposes of revocation proceedings under this Act. A licensee may enforce the patent against infringement, provided that they adhere to the terms stipulated within the licensing agreement and do not act contrary to the interests of the patentee as determined by a competent authority.

The term "specification" shall encompass not only the detailed description of an invention but also any drawings or other materials incorporated therein to elucidate its functionality. A claim within a specification shall be construed strictly according to its language, but reference may be made to the remainder of the specification for understanding where ambiguity arises; however, it is provided that such interpretation shall not extend to importing limitations not explicitly stated in the claim itself. Disputes regarding the scope of a specification claim and whether an invention falls reasonably within said claim shall be subject to appeal to the Appellate Intellectual Property Tribunal, with consideration given to prior art disclosures and the skilled person's understanding as determined by the Controller.

Subject to the provisions of this Act, any patentee may grant a license to use, exercise, or have exercised the invention claimed in the specification relating to varieties registered under the Plant Varieties Protection Act, 2001. Such licenses shall be assignable by the patentee and may be granted wholly or partially, for specific territories, and for a term not exceeding the remaining period of the patent. The terms and conditions of any such license agreement must be clearly stated in writing and filed with the Controller within thirty days of execution. Failure to do so shall render the license unenforceable against third parties. Further, where a specification claim extends to a process by which a registered variety is produced, the licensee shall be bound by all restrictions imposed on the patentee under the Plant Varieties Protection Act concerning commercial exploitation.

The Registering Authority shall examine each application for registration of utility models to ascertain whether the claimed invention satisfies the criteria outlined herein. A crucial element of this examination pertains to the clarity and precision of the specification claim. The claim must define with particularity the subject matter for which protection is sought, distinguishing it from prior art as disclosed in the accompanying documentation. Failure to adequately delineate the scope of the invention within the specification claim may result in rejection of the application. Where ambiguity or uncertainty arises concerning the interpretation of a specification claim, the court shall cognizance of such matters and determine its meaning based on the entire disclosure contained within the patent application.

Where an invention relates to a process for producing a substance characterized by a specific molecular structure, the scope of protection conferred by a patent shall be determined solely by the terms of the specification claim. A person shall be deemed to have infringed a patent if, without leave from the Controller, that person makes, uses, or offers to sell any product in India which incorporates an element defined within the boundaries of such specification claim. Provided that, where the infringing copy is demonstrably produced through a process not explicitly disclosed in the specification but utilizing substantially equivalent means, it shall still be considered an infringement under this Act. The patentee may seek remedies including damages and injunctions against any party found to have committed such an infringing act, subject to considerations of proportionality as determined by the Controller.

An applicant seeking registration of a utility model under this Act shall furnish with the application a detailed specification describing the invention and its method of operation. The specification must clearly indicate the technical field to which the invention relates, along with a concise statement of the problem it seeks to address. Crucially, the date filing specification is paramount in establishing priority rights; therefore, all documents submitted relating to prior art or previous disclosures must be meticulously referenced within the specification itself. Any subsequent amendment to the specification shall not alter the original date filing specification unless such amendment is demonstrably consequential and does not broaden the scope of protection sought. The Controller may require further clarification regarding the technical details presented, provided that this request does not prejudice the applicant’s established priority.

Where an applicant fails to comply with the requirements relating to the date filing specification under this Act, and a person aggrieved demonstrates that such failure has caused demonstrable prejudice to their reasonable expectations regarding the patentability of an invention, the Controller may grant appropriate remedies. Such remedies shall include, but are not limited to, extending the time period for compliance, requiring the applicant to amend the specification to address deficiencies identified by the Controller, or, in circumstances where the prejudice is substantial and irreparable, permitting a third party to challenge the validity of the patent after its grant. The Controller shall provide reasons in writing for any such remedial action taken, and an opportunity for the applicant to be heard before exercising these powers. This provision applies irrespective of whether the non-compliance was wilful or inadvertent; however, the severity of prejudice will inform the nature of remedies available.

Where an applicant elects to file a divisional application relating to a pending patent application, the date of filing specification for the purposes of determining novelty and inventive step shall be the earlier date of filing of the parent application. Provided that, if the divisional application contains subject matter not disclosed in the parent application, only that portion of the claim pertaining to such new matter shall be assessed against the priority date of the divisional application’s filing. The Controller may require the applicant to furnish a statement clarifying the relationship between the claims of the divisional application and those of the parent application, particularly where there is ambiguity regarding the scope of inventive step. Further, any request for clarification or amendment under this Act relating to the specification shall be deemed part of the original disclosure for determining the date filing specification.

Where an applicant seeks to amend a patent application after the initial date filing specification, such amendment shall be permissible only if it does not alter the nature of the invention as originally claimed. Provided that any alteration introduced by way of amendment must have been adequately described and supported within the original disclosure. The Controller may require the applicant to furnish a declaration confirming compliance with this provision, attesting that the amended claims remain consistent with the initial inventive concept. Further, an amendment shall not be allowed if it introduces subject matter which was not disclosed in the complete specification initially filed; such restriction applies irrespective of any subsequent publications or prior art disclosures. The Controller may reject the application under this Act if he deems the amendment to materially prejudice the interests of other parties.

Where an application for a patent contains multiple inventions, and the claims extend beyond the subject matter initially described in the date filing specification, the Controller may require the applicant to divide the application into separate applications. Failure to comply with such a requirement within the time prescribed shall render the original application liable for rejection in its entirety. Any person aggrieved by an order requiring division of an application under this Act may appeal to the Appellate Board within sixty days from the date of receipt of that order, and any penalty for non-compliance shall be recoverable as civil debt. The Controller is empowered to impose a monetary fine not exceeding one hundred thousand rupees where it appears that the applicant has deliberately attempted to circumvent these provisions.

Where a patent has been granted under this Act and the rights pertaining thereto have been assigned or licensed to any person, whether in India or elsewhere, such assignment or license may include the right to file applications for patents for corresponding inventions in foreign countries. Provided that where an application for a patent is filed outside of India within three months from the date filing specification was made in India, and such application claims priority from the Indian application, the Controller may require evidence demonstrating due diligence on the part of the assignee or licensee to ensure compliance with applicable international treaties and conventions relating to patents. Further, any subsequent assignment or license shall be subject to the terms and conditions of the original agreement, as recorded with the Patents Office, and such recording shall be deemed conclusive proof of the validity of the transfer.

Where an objection is raised by the Controller regarding the validity of a patent relating to the date filing specification, the applicant shall have the right to submit written arguments and evidence rebutting such objection within sixty days from the date of communication of the said objection. Such arguments must specifically address the factual basis underpinning the claimed priority date. The Controller may require the applicant to furnish further documentation substantiating the asserted date filing specification, including but not limited to correspondence with foreign patent offices or declarations from inventors. Any order passed by the Controller under this Act relating to a disputed date filing specification shall be subject to appeal before the Appellate Board within ninety days of such order’s communication, provided that the appellant demonstrates prejudice resulting from the Controller's determination.

Subject to the provisions of this Act, a patentee shall have the exclusive right to exploit the invention for the term specified herein; however, such rights are assignable and licensable in whole or in part, either wholly or partially, and may be granted during the pendency of the application. Any assignment or license relating to a patent, or any interest therein, including the date filing specification, shall require registration with the Controller and shall be deemed invalid unless so registered within three months from the date of execution. Where an invention incorporates elements derived from a literary work protected under the law relating to copyright, the grant of a patent shall not prejudice such copyright; provided that the use of such copyrighted material is incidental to the patented process or product. The Controller may require submission of evidence demonstrating compliance with relevant copyright provisions as part of the examination procedure.

Where an applicant seeks to amend a patent application after the initial date filing specification, such amendment shall be permissible only if it does not alter the nature of the invention as originally claimed and is supported by the disclosure contained within the original complete specification. Any attempt to introduce subject matter not previously described, or which would substantially broaden the scope of protection sought, will constitute a material alteration, rendering the amended application liable for rejection. Furthermore, where imported samples are examined under the Customs Act 1962 during examination proceedings and found to embody elements inconsistent with the original disclosure, the Controller may issue an objection regarding novelty and inventive step; this decision is subject to appeal before the Intellectual Property Appellate Board.

Where an applicant seeks to amend a patent application after the initial date filing specification, such amendment shall be permissible only if it does not alter the nature of the invention as originally claimed and is consistent with the disclosure contained within the complete specification initially presented. The Controller may require the applicant to submit a reasoned explanation justifying the proposed alteration and demonstrating its adherence to these stipulations. Failure to provide satisfactory justification or evidence of consistency will result in rejection of the amendment request. Any challenge to the validity of the patent based on discrepancies between the amended claims and the original disclosure shall be subject to review by an instituted district court, acting as a forum for determining whether the alteration prejudiced any other party involved. The applicant bears the onus of proving that the amendment remains faithful to the initial inventive concept.

For the purposes of determining novelty under this Act, where an application for patent is filed claiming invention derived from a previously published document, the *date claim shall* be taken as the later of either the date of publication of said document or the filing date of the provisional application relating to the claimed invention. Provided that, if such publication was made by the applicant or their legal predecessor with the consent of the inventor, and without reasonable grounds for believing it would prejudice the rights of the applicant, this provision shall not apply. Subject to this exception, any prior disclosure will invalidate a claim’s patentability as provided herein.

Where an application for registration of a plant variety is filed and contains claims extending to territories outside of India, the determination of the effective filing date for such claims shall be subject to verification by the Registrar. The Registrar may require submission of documentary evidence demonstrating the initial publication or prior disclosure of the plant variety in each claimed territory. Should discrepancies arise between the asserted filing dates and the documented disclosures, the Registrar shall determine a revised date claim based on the earliest publicly available record establishing knowledge of the plant variety within that jurisdiction. Provided that this determination is made after affording the applicant an opportunity for representation under this Act, the adjusted date claim shall be binding for all subsequent proceedings relating to the registration.

Where an application for patent relating to a process for producing a substance is filed, and such process is claimed by way of a product claim, the date claim shall be construed strictly in accordance with the invention as described within the complete specification. Provided that, if it is demonstrated to the satisfaction of the Controller that the applicant has knowingly misrepresented any fact concerning the prior use or publication of the invention, remedies available under this Act may include revocation of the patent and imposition of a penalty not exceeding ten times the cost incurred by aggrieved parties in pursuing legal recourse. Furthermore, where an infringement action is brought based on such a product claim, the burden shall lie upon the claimant to establish that the alleged infringing substance was indeed produced using the patented process as described herein.

Where an application for a patent relating to an invention includes a claim for subject matter not described in the specification as originally filed, and such claim is subsequently amended to incorporate said omitted subject matter, the date claim shall be construed strictly in accordance with the principles of novelty and inventive step. The Controller may require the applicant to furnish a declaration affirming that the amended claim fairly reflects the disclosure contained within the complete specification at the time of the original filing. Provided that, if it is demonstrated to the satisfaction of the Controller that the omission was inadvertent and did not prejudice the public interest, an extension of the date claim beyond the initial filing date may be granted. Subject to this provision, any such amendment shall be deemed invalid if it introduces matter which could have been claimed but was not disclosed in the original specification.

Where an application for patent relating to a process for producing a substance is filed, and such process involves one or more steps previously known in the art, the date claim shall be determined with reference to the earliest prior publication disclosing each step involved, provided that the applicant demonstrates, under this Act, that the combination of said steps results in an unexpected technical effect not predictable by a person skilled in the art. Further, if the invention relates to a method of treatment of human disease, the date claim shall be subject to verification regarding compliance with regulations pertaining to clinical trials as prescribed by the Drugs and Cosmetics Act. The Controller may require submission of relevant data substantiating such unexpected technical effect or regulatory adherence before proceeding with examination.

Where an application for patent relating to a process for producing a substance is filed, and such process involves one or more steps where the claimed invention differs from the prior art disclosure, the date claim shall be construed strictly in accordance with the complete specification as originally filed. Any attempt to broaden the scope of the claims through subsequent amendments will render the application liable for rejection under this Act. Furthermore, any party demonstrating that a patent has been granted based on an improperly determined date claim may petition the Controller for revocation, and shall be entitled to recover costs incurred in pursuing such proceedings if successful. The burden of proving the validity of the initially claimed invention rests upon the patentee.

Subject to the provisions of this Act, where a patentee desires to grant an exclusive license under this Act relating to any invention for which he is entitled to apply for and has applied for or obtained patents, such license may be assigned or otherwise transferred, provided that the terms and conditions of such assignment or transfer are clearly documented and registered with the Controller. The date claim shall be deemed to be the date on which the application for registration of the assignment or transfer is received by the Controller, notwithstanding any prior agreements between the parties. Further, where a license granted under this Act includes the right to assign or sub-license the patent, such subsequent assignments or sub-licenses are also subject to registration as provided herein. The failure to register an assignment shall render the assignee not a true owner for all purposes under this Act.

Where an application for patent relating to a process for producing a substance includes a claim for the substance itself produced by that process, and such claim is deemed invalid under this Act due to non-patentable subject matter, the question whether the date claim shall be construed as referring solely to the process or encompass the resultant substance remains a matter of considerable dispute. It is provided that, in determining said date, the Controller shall consider not only the literal wording of the claim but also the technical context disclosed within the complete specification and any subsequent amendments filed. Further, an appeal against such determination may be made to the Appellate Board, subject to demonstrating prejudice arising from a misinterpretation of the inventive step involved.

Where an application for a patent relating to an invention made outside India contains one or more claims dependent upon a claim appearing in an international registration, and such international registration has been published under the Patent Cooperation Treaty, the date claim shall be taken as the filing date of the corresponding application in the country where the international registration was initially filed. Provided that, if the applicant fails to provide within six months from the date of request, particulars relating to the priority claim arising from said international registration, or if such particulars disclose a state of affairs which is not consistent with the requirements under this Act, then the application shall be deemed to have been filed on the date of the aforementioned request. Further, any subsequent amendment to claims referencing an international registration shall only be permissible subject to compliance with regulations pertaining to claim clarity and support for the invention.

For the purposes of this Act, “filing specification matter” means all information contained within a patent application’s written description, claims, and drawings, subject to any amendments or additions made during prosecution under this Act. Such matter shall include, but not be limited to, details regarding the invention's technical field, its construction, operation, and proposed uses. The filing specification matter must disclose the invention in a manner as would enable a person skilled in the art to make and use it. Provided that any alteration to the filing specification matter after the first publication of the application shall be permissible only with the Controller’s consent.

The Registrar shall, upon receipt of a request for registration of a utility model, conduct an examination to ascertain whether the filed specification matter adequately discloses the invention and enables its practice by a person skilled in the art. Such examination shall include verification of the clarity and conciseness of the description, ensuring that all essential elements contributing to the claimed functionality are explicitly detailed within the specification. The request may be rejected if the Registrar determines that the filing specification matter is deficient in adequately describing the invention or lacks sufficient support for the claims presented. Further, any amendment to the filed specification matter after the initial registration request shall only be permissible with prior written consent from the Registrar and subject to prescribed conditions regarding novelty and inventive step.

Where a patent has been granted based upon a filing specification containing information not adequately described to enable a person skilled in the art to practice the invention, and it is subsequently demonstrated that such deficiency resulted from an omission or alteration made without the consent of all prior inventors, the Controller may, acting on the application of any aggrieved party, order the patent to be amended. Such amendment shall only rectify the deficient matter and not introduce new subject matter beyond the originally claimed scope. The right to apply for rectification under this Act is subject to a limitation period of three years from the date of publication of the patent. Any person seeking such rectification must demonstrate prejudice resulting directly from the inadequate filing specification matter, and remedies for damages shall be pursued separately under applicable laws concerning contractual obligations.

The Controller may require an applicant to amend the filing specification matter to ensure clarity and conformity with the prescribed forms; such requirement shall specify the nature of the amendment sought and provide a reasonable period for compliance, not exceeding sixty days from the date of notification. Where an amendment is directed under this Act, it shall be accompanied by a statement indicating the prior version of the specification and detailing the changes effected. The applicant shall furnish a declaration verifying the accuracy of the amended filing specification matter, attesting that to the best of their knowledge, it fully discloses the invention as claimed. Failure to comply with a direction for amendment or to provide the requisite declaration may result in rejection of the application. Any person aggrieved by an order directing amendment may appeal to the Appellate Board within sixty days of receipt of the order.

Where an applicant seeks to amend a filed patent application, such amendment shall only pertain to details concerning the description and claims; alterations impacting the substance of the invention as originally presented are prohibited. The amended specification must fully disclose the subject matter sought to be protected, adhering strictly to principles of clarity and enabling disclosure. Further, any addition or modification to the filing specification matter requires explicit written consent from the Controller, obtained prior to publication under this Act. Such consent shall only be granted if the Controller is satisfied that the amendment does not substantially alter the nature of the invention claimed and maintains compliance with all relevant provisions regarding novelty and inventive step as provided herein.

Where a patent application contains deficiencies in its filing specification matter, rendering it unclear to a person skilled in the art regarding the scope of the invention claimed, the Controller may direct the applicant to amend the specification within a period not exceeding six months. Failure to comply with such direction shall result in the rejection of the application. Any party aggrieved by an order rejecting an application under this Act may appeal to the Appellate Board within sixty days from the date of communication of the order. The Appellate Board’s decision is final, subject to further appeal to the High Court on a point of law. Intentional misrepresentation concerning the filing specification matter shall be deemed a cognizable offence punishable with imprisonment and fine as provided herein.

Where a patentee desires to grant a license relating to an invention for which a patent has been granted under this Act, or intends to assign the entire interest in such patent, the licensing agreement or assignment deed shall explicitly detail all aspects of the filing specification matter pertaining to the claimed invention. Such disclosure must include, but not be limited to, descriptions of the inventive concept, detailed methodologies employed in its creation, and any supporting data presented within the original application documents. The Controller may require further clarification regarding this specification matter if deemed necessary for public understanding and transparency. Provided that the patentee ensures accuracy and completeness in these disclosures, such licenses or assignments shall be considered valid and enforceable as provided herein. Failure to adequately address the filing specification matter may render the license or assignment voidable at the discretion of the Controller.

Where an objection is raised by the Controller regarding the clarity or sufficiency of the filing specification matter contained within a patent application, the applicant shall have the opportunity to amend said specification and/or claims subject to the proviso that such amendments do not substantially alter the invention originally claimed. The Controller may require a written explanation accompanying any amendment, detailing the basis for its introduction and demonstrating compliance with the requirements under this Act concerning novelty and inventive step. An appeal against an order rejecting an application based on insufficiency of disclosure within the filing specification matter lies to the Appellate Board, provided that the applicant demonstrates demonstrable prejudice resulting from the Controller’s interpretation.

Where an application for patent registration is filed, the Controller shall scrutinize the filing specification matter to ascertain whether it adequately discloses the invention and its manner of operation. Should any deficiency arise concerning clarity or completeness within the specification, the applicant may be called upon to submit a response addressing such deficiencies within a period as determined by the Controller. Failure to satisfactorily address these concerns may result in rejection of the application under this Act. An aggrieved applicant retains the right to institute a court application seeking review of the Controller’s decision regarding the adequacy of the filing specification matter, provided that such an application is made within the prescribed timeframe and adheres to procedural requirements as provided herein.

Where an applicant seeks to amend the filing specification matter after the publication of the patent application under this Act, such amendment shall only be permissible if it clarifies or explains the originally claimed invention and does not introduce any new subject matter beyond what is adequately supported by the original disclosure. Any proposed alteration that substantially broadens the scope of protection sought will be deemed to contravene the principles of novelty and inventive step as provided herein. The Controller may, upon receiving an objection from a third party regarding such amendment, require the applicant to submit an evidence affidavit verifying the consistency between the amended specification and the original disclosure. Failure to satisfy the Controller’s requirements or providing a false statement in the affidavit shall render the application liable for rejection.

For the purposes of this Act, a “date claim” relating to an invention shall mean the earliest date upon which any feature of the claimed invention appears in a published document or publicly accessible source, irrespective of whether such disclosure constitutes prior art under this Act. The determination of a date claim shall be undertaken solely for the purpose of assessing novelty and inventive step as provided herein. Where an applicant seeks to incorporate subject matter disclosed in a previously filed application, the date claim pertaining to any new element introduced through that incorporation shall be determined by reference to the publication date of the earlier application. This assessment is without prejudice to considerations regarding obviousness.

An application for a patent relating to an invention shall contain a statement specifying the claims sought to be protected by the patent; and such claims shall define the scope of protection unequivocally. The Controller General may, upon receiving an objection from any person regarding the validity of a claim or the propriety of its inclusion in the patent specification, direct the applicant to clarify or amend the said claim. For the purpose of determining novelty and inventive step under this Act, the date claim is deemed to be the earlier of either the date of filing of the complete specification or the date claimed as the priority date by the applicant, provided that such priority date has been duly recorded in the prescribed manner. The applicant shall furnish all necessary documentation substantiating the priority claim within the timeframe stipulated herein.

Where an application for patent includes a claim for any invention described therein, and such claim relates to a matter already comprised in a prior publication or use, the Controller may require the applicant to furnish evidence establishing the date claim as the date on which the invention was first made available to the public through such publication or use. Failure to provide satisfactory evidence within the time specified by the Controller shall render the application liable for rejection under this Act. An appeal against an order requiring production of such evidence lies to the Appellate Board. Provided that, if the applicant demonstrates that the prior publication or use was obtained without their knowledge or consent, and they were diligent in preventing it, the requirement may be waived at the discretion of the Controller.

Where an application for a patent includes a claim relating to a method or process, and such claim is not supported by a description sufficient to enable a person skilled in the art to carry out the invention, the Controller may require the applicant to amend the claim to bring it into compliance with the requirements of this Act. Such amendment shall be permissible only if the amended claim fairly reflects the subject matter disclosed in the complete specification as originally filed. The determination of whether an amended claim is “fairly based” upon the original disclosure rests entirely within the discretion of the Controller, and he shall consider all relevant circumstances. For the purposes of assessing fairness under this provision, the *date claim* relating to any method or process invention shall be deemed to be the earliest date on which a complete specification disclosing the inventive step was filed by the applicant or their predecessor in title.

Where an application for a patent relating to an invention includes a *date claim* pertaining to a process by which a substance is produced, such claim shall only be considered valid if it explicitly identifies the specific reactants and reaction conditions employed in said process. Further, provided that the applicant demonstrates, through documented laboratory records maintained prior to the date of filing, that the claimed process was diligently pursued and resulted in reproducible yields meeting commercially viable standards, the Controller may grant a patent. However, should the applicant fail to provide such documentation or if it is determined that the disclosed process substantially replicates techniques previously described in publicly accessible scientific literature predating the application’s priority date, then the *date claim* shall be deemed invalid under this Act and subject to rejection.

Where an application for patent includes a *date claim* relating to an invention described therein, and it is established by evidence presented before the Controller that such *date claim*, if proven valid, would extend protection beyond the prescribed period under this Act, the applicant shall be subject to a penalty of not less than fifty thousand rupees but may extend to two hundred thousand rupees. The Controller may, after affording the applicant an opportunity for being heard, direct the amendment or rejection of the application insofar as it relates to the contested *date claim*. Failure to comply with such direction within thirty days shall render the application liable for summary dismissal. Any person aggrieved by a decision under this provision may appeal to the Intellectual Property Appellate Board within sixty days.

Where a patent has been granted under this Act and the invention incorporates technology developed by an entity distinct from the original applicant, such entity may, subject to fulfilling all procedural requirements as provided herein, apply for assignment of rights relating specifically to the portion of the invention constituting said technology. Upon satisfactory demonstration that the contribution was substantial and not merely incremental, the Controller shall issue a notice to the patent holder regarding the proposed assignment. The patent holder shall have thirty days to object, after which the Controller may grant or deny the application. In determining eligibility for assignment, the *date claim* of the invention shall be considered in relation to the date of demonstrable contribution by the applicant seeking assignment. Any license granted pursuant to this provision shall remain valid unless revoked under provisions relating to non-use.

Where an application for patent includes a claim relating to a method of use not described in the original specification filed under this Act, and such method was known prior to the date claim asserted by the applicant, the Controller may require the applicant to demonstrate with reasonable certainty that the inventive step embodied within the claimed method is inextricably linked to the matter disclosed in the initial application. Failure to satisfy the Controller’s requirements shall render the claim invalid, subject to appeal before the Intellectual Property Appellate Board. The burden of proving such inextricable linkage rests solely upon the applicant; provided that evidence demonstrating state-of-the-art knowledge prior to the asserted date claim shall be admissible and considered during appellate proceedings.

Where an application for a patent includes a claim incorporating subject matter not previously described or claimed in the prior art, and such claim is asserted to relate back to an earlier invention, the Controller may require the applicant to establish, with reasonable certainty, the date claim of that earlier invention. This determination shall be made based on documentary evidence demonstrating the applicant’s diligent pursuit of perfecting the invention as originally conceived. Failure to provide satisfactory evidence may result in the rejection of the application or limitation of the patent's scope. The rights afforded under this Act relating to a patent shall not extend to any matter which is already within the public domain, nor shall they prejudice existing proprietors trade marks lawfully used prior to the date claim established for the invention.

Where an application for a patent relating to an invention includes a musical work incorporated therein as an element of the inventive concept, and such incorporation is not explicitly described within the initial provisional application, the determination of the *date claim* shall be subject to rigorous scrutiny. The Controller may require the applicant to demonstrate that the subsequent inclusion of said musical work does not substantially alter the nature of the invention or introduce new matter beyond what was reasonably anticipated by a person skilled in the art at the time of the initial provisional filing. Provided that, if the applicant can establish that the inventive concept would have been obvious to incorporate the musical work based on publicly available information, the *date claim* shall not be prejudiced; however, this determination is subject to appeal under this Act.

For the purposes of determining patentability under this Act, a “claim shall date” is defined as the date on which an application for letters patent is initially filed with the Controller General. This date governs the assessment of novelty and inventive step relative to prior art disclosures. Where an applicant has previously published information pertaining to the invention, subject to any applicable grace period provided herein, the claim shall date may be earlier than the filing date of the current application; however, such earlier date will only apply if the publication was made by or on behalf of the applicant and under conditions that do not prejudice the rights of others.

The Registering Authority shall, upon receipt of a request for rectification of an invention registration, examine whether the recorded particulars pertaining to the claimed novelty are demonstrably inaccurate or misleading. Such examination includes verification of the initial application’s documentation and any subsequent amendments. Where it is established that a claim shall date was erroneously assigned due to clerical error or misinterpretation of prior art disclosures during the original assessment process, the Registering Authority may order correction of the record. This power extends only to errors directly impacting the ascertainment of priority; substantive challenges to patentability are reserved for proceedings under this Act. The applicant whose registration is being rectified shall be afforded an opportunity to present counter-evidence before a final determination is made.

Where an application for patent relating to an invention includes a claim incorporating subject matter not previously described or claimed in any prior document referred to in the application, and such incorporation constitutes a material modification of the originally filed claims, then the applicant shall be deemed to have abandoned their right to pursue validity based on the original filing date. The effective date from which a claim shall date for the purposes of determining novelty and inventive step will instead be the date of first publication of the modified claim, provided that such publication occurred prior to the grant of the patent or any opposition proceedings. Further, where an applicant seeks to amend claims substantially altering the scope of protection sought after the initial examination, they may do so only with the Controller’s express written consent and subject to a fresh fee payment as prescribed under this Act.

Where an application for a patent has been amended after the initial filing and such amendment incorporates subject matter not previously disclosed, the Controller may require the applicant to furnish a statement detailing the extent of the modification and its relationship to the original disclosure. The date upon which a claim shall date is determined by reference to the earliest priority date asserted in the application, provided that any subsequent amendments introducing new matter are considered for their impact on patentability. If an amendment introduces subject matter not disclosed in the prior art as of the initial filing date, and such introduction materially alters the scope of protection sought, the Controller may direct a re-examination of the claim’s validity. This determination shall be made after affording the applicant an opportunity to present arguments regarding the substantial similarity between the amended claim and the original disclosure.

Where an application for a patent contains claims relating to a method or process applicable to the production, preparation or use of any article or substance, and such method or process is not itself an invention under this Act, the claim shall date from the date of filing of the main invention if it meets all conditions as provided herein. Provided that, where the applicant demonstrates to the satisfaction of the Controller that the inventive step relating to the method or process was conceived after the initial priority date of the patent application and is inextricably linked to the functioning of the primary invention, a later claim shall date may be permitted. Subject to an examination under this Act, such permission will only be granted if the applicant provides detailed evidence substantiating the temporal relationship between the two inventions.

Where an application for patent relating to a process involves a substance produced by fermentation, and where the invention claimed is not itself the said substance, the claim shall date from the earliest date on which any description of the process falls within the scope of this Act. Provided that, if such a process has been described in a prior publication or use, the Controller may determine that the claim shall date only from the date of such publication or use, subject to due consideration being given to evidence demonstrating reasonable grounds for believing that the invention was not known before that date. Any party aggrieved by this determination may appeal under this Act within sixty days and shall be liable for costs as determined by the Appellate Board.

Where a patent has been granted under this Act and the proprietor desires to grant an exclusive license conferring all rights pertaining to the invention described and claimed therein, such license agreement shall clearly specify the field of exploitation for which the right is conferred. The licensee may, subject to the terms of the license agreement, assign or transfer the said exclusive license to any other person, provided that such assignment or transfer does not broaden the scope of the licensed field beyond what was originally stipulated in the proprietor’s license grant. For the purposes of determining whether a claim shall date back to an earlier priority application, the assignee under this provision shall be deemed to have stepped into the shoes of the original licensee and inherit all rights and obligations pertaining to the exclusive license agreement. The proprietor may revoke any such assignment or transfer if it is found that the terms of the license have been violated.

Where an application for patent relating to a process includes a claim directed to a substance produced by such process, and it is alleged before the Controller that said claim does not fairly represent the invention as disclosed in the complete specification, the date when such claim shall date may be determined based on evidence presented demonstrating inventive novelty arising solely from the subsequent modification of the described process. Provided that, if the applicant demonstrates to the satisfaction of the Controller that the substance was known or used by others prior to the alleged modification, the Controller may direct that the said claim shall date from the filing date of the earliest application claiming priority relating to the original process. This determination is subject to appeal under this Act.

Where a patent has been granted under this Act and the proprietor desires to grant an exclusive license relating to one or more claims contained therein, such license shall be deemed an assignment for the purposes of royalty payments as provided herein. The licensee may subsequently assign the said exclusive license to any other person, subject to the condition that prior written consent is obtained from the original patent proprietor. This requirement applies irrespective of whether the consideration for the initial licensing agreement involves a lump sum payment or periodic royalties. Further, in instances where an assignment occurs after the claim shall date, the assignee shall be obligated to notify the registrar person of such transfer within thirty days of its execution. Failure to do so will render the assignee liable to penalties as determined by the Controller.

For the purposes of determining entitlement to a patent under this Act, the term “priority date” shall mean the date on which the application for patent is initially filed in a convention country, subject to any subsequent claim for priority as provided herein. Where an applicant seeks to claim priority from a foreign filing, such claim shall be made within twelve months of the initial filing date and must be supported by documentary evidence acceptable to the Controller. The said priority date shall date filing irrespective of any amendments or additions made to the specification during prosecution under this Act. Any subsequent modification affecting the subject matter claimed cannot alter the established priority date.

The Registering Authority shall, upon receipt of a request for rectification of an entry relating to the registered design, examine whether such request is supported by evidence demonstrating substantial alteration affecting the character or reputation of the design. Where a patent application incorporates subject matter derived from previously published disclosures, the applicant shall provide a declaration affirming that all relevant publications have been identified and their content considered in formulating the claims. The priority date for inventive step assessment shall date filing of the initial disclosure, provided that such disclosure clearly anticipates at least one claim presently asserted under this Act. Any challenge to the validity of registration based on prior use may be addressed through a formal objection process as provided herein.

Where an application for a patent relating to an invention includes subject matter derived from prior publications, and such publication occurred before the date of filing of the said application, it shall be incumbent upon the applicant to provide a written affirmation confirming that the invention as claimed constitutes a novel and non-obvious advancement over the disclosed information. This affirmation must explicitly detail how the inventive step distinguishes itself from the pre-existing knowledge. Failure to submit such an affirmation will render the application liable for rejection under this Act. The priority date, shall date filing, remains unaffected provided that the applicant demonstrates, through expert testimony or documented evidence, a substantial and unforeseen contribution beyond what was previously available.

Where a patent has been granted under this Act and the proprietor desires to grant an exclusive license conferring all rights specified therein, including but not limited to the right to make, use, sell, offer for sale, and import the patented invention, such license may be assigned or transferred subject to the provisions herein. The consideration stipulated in any such assignment or transfer shall be deemed part of the record pertaining to the patent. Further, where an exclusive license is granted prior to the expiration of three years from the date of application for patent, a royalty shall be payable to the Government as provided under this Act; the amount thereof shall be determined based on the extent of exclusivity conferred and the anticipated market share. For the purposes of determining any claim relating to infringement or validity, the filing date shall date filing, irrespective of subsequent amendments impacting the scope of protection.

Where an application for patent relating to a process for producing a substance is filed, and it is subsequently alleged by a third party that the claimed invention incorporates elements derived from prior art not publicly available in India at the time of the initial filing, the Controller may, upon review of evidence submitted by both parties, determine whether such incorporation invalidates the patent. For purposes of assessing novelty and inventive step under this Act, shall date filing is to be construed strictly; any reliance on publications or public disclosures occurring after the aforementioned date will not be entertained unless it can be definitively established that such subsequent disclosure was a direct consequence of an unauthorized act by the applicant or their agents. The decision regarding validity may be appealed to the Appellate Board.

For the purposes of determining patentability under this Act, the term “priority date” shall date filing of the earliest application claiming priority to the invention; provided that where an applicant elects to pursue a design registered layout as part of the claimed invention, the priority date relating specifically to elements encompassed within said registered layout shall be deemed to be the date of registration of such design. Further, if multiple applications claim priority, the application with the earliest filing date amongst those claiming priority shall prevail in determining the overall priority date for the invention; subject to any modifications as may arise under provisions pertaining to divisional applications.

A specification patent shall define the scope of protection granted under this Act with precision and clarity. For the purposes of determining novelty and inventive step, the term "specification" refers to the written description of the invention accompanying an application for grant of a patent, including any drawings or other diagrams incorporated therein. The specification must disclose the matter which the inventor claims as his invention in such manner as to enable a person skilled in the art to make and use the same. Provided that, where the claimed invention incorporates elements derived from previously known technologies, the specification shall clearly articulate the synergistic effect resulting from their combination.

The Register shall maintain a publicly accessible record of all specifications submitted for registration under this Act, detailing the applicant’s particulars and the nature of the invention disclosed therein. Any person seeking to register a specification patent shall submit three true copies of the complete specification, accompanied by an abstract not exceeding one hundred and fifty words summarizing the technical disclosure. The Controller may require further clarification or modification of the specification prior to acceptance for registration, provided that such requests are communicated in writing within ninety days of initial submission. A specification patent shall include a claim defining the scope of protection sought, clearly identifying the inventive step. Any alteration to the registered specification requires prior approval from the Controller and is subject to a fee as prescribed.

Where an infringement action is brought under this Act, the aggrieved party shall be entitled to seek injunctive relief restraining the infringing activity, subject to the provisions regarding reasonable royalties and damages as provided herein. The patentee shall further be empowered to claim compensation for loss of profits resulting from the infringement, calculated on a basis that takes into account any measure of the infringer’s savings attributable to the use of the patented invention. A specification patent shall confer upon the patentee exclusive rights to make, use and sell the invention claimed therein within India, but such right is not absolute. The Controller may, under this Act, grant leave to parties interested to challenge the validity of a patent if they demonstrate sufficient cause for doing so.

Where an application for patents is filed relating to a process by which a substance is produced, such specification patent shall extend only to the use of that process for the production of that particular substance unless the claims specifically and clearly define the scope of protection sought to include other substances or processes. The Controller may require the applicant to amend the claims to clarify the relationship between the process and the substance produced, provided that any amendment does not alter the inventive concept disclosed in the original specification. Further, an objection raised by a third party under this Act relating to the clarity or precision of such claims shall be considered within six months from the date of the objection’s receipt. The applicant shall have thirty days to respond to said objections and submit revised claims as deemed necessary.

A specification patent shall be deemed invalid under this Act if it is established that the subject matter disclosed does not constitute an inventive step over prior art, provided that such determination considers whether the invention inherently possesses technical effect and utility sufficient to warrant protection. Furthermore, where a claim in the specification relates to a method of agricultural or horticultural practice, it shall be assessed with particular regard to its impact on food security and rural livelihoods, subject to demonstrating novelty and non-obviousness as provided herein. Any challenge to the validity of a patent may only proceed if the petitioner demonstrates reasonable grounds for believing that the invention was not adequately disclosed in the specification, failing which the claim will be dismissed.

Any person aggrieved by an order passed under this Act may appeal to the Appellate Board within sixty days from the date of such order; provided that the Appellate Board shall not entertain any appeal if it is satisfied that the delay in filing the appeal exceeds one hundred and twenty days without sufficient cause, and where sufficient cause is shown for such delay, the Board may excuse it. Further, a patent proprietor who knowingly makes false statements in the specification patent shall be liable to pay damages to any person prejudiced by those statements. The Controller may, upon receiving information regarding such fraudulent specifications, initiate proceedings for revocation of the patent under this Act and impose penalties as deemed appropriate.

Subject to the provisions of this Act and rules made thereunder, any person owning a specification patent shall be entitled to grant a license to use or exercise the patented invention to another party, either wholly or partially, for a specified period and on such terms as may be agreed upon between the parties. Such license agreement shall be in writing and duly executed by both licensor and licensee. Assignment of rights under a specification patent, including the right to grant licenses, may be made by instrument in writing and registered with the Controller. Provided that any assignment or license granted prior to registration under this Act shall be deemed invalid unless subsequently registered as provided herein. The Controller may, upon application by an aggrieved party, inquire into the reasonableness of royalty rates stipulated in such assignments or licenses and make recommendations accordingly.

Where an objection is raised during examination alleging that a specification patent shall not adequately disclose the manner in which to make and use the invention claimed therein, the examiner may require the applicant to amend the specification to clarify said disclosure; provided that such amendment does not extend beyond the scope of the originally filed application. The applicant shall be afforded a reasonable opportunity to respond to any such objection with counter-arguments or revised claims. If the applicant fails to adequately address the examiner’s concerns, and it is determined under this Act that the specification remains deficient in disclosing the invention, the application may proceed no further. Any decision made by the examiner regarding sufficiency of disclosure may be appealed before a designated appellate authority as provided herein.

A specification patent shall be deemed invalid if it is established, under this Act, that the subject matter disclosed does not meet the criteria for novelty and inventive step as provided herein. The Controller may, upon receiving notice of opposition from any person interested, direct the patentee to appear before him or submit written submissions addressing the grounds raised in the notice. Such a notice shall be accompanied by a statement outlining the specific reasons for opposing the specification patent, including but not limited to demonstrating prior publication or use that predates the filing date. The Controller shall provide an opportunity for both the patentee and the opponent to present evidence and arguments; provided that any claim construction during opposition proceedings shall be consistent with the original disclosure in the specification.

A specification patent shall disclose the matter in respect whereof protection is sought with sufficient particularity to enable the subject matter to be made or used by any person skilled in the art; provided that where the invention relates to varieties registered under this Act, the specification shall clearly identify such registered varieties and detail the characteristics distinguishing them from existing cultivars. The term "specification" as employed herein includes all drawings, claims, and abstract forming part of the patent application. Further, a specification shall not contain any matter which is extraneous to the claimed invention or which would unduly obscure the understanding thereof by a person skilled in the art.

For the purposes of this Act, "biotechnological process" means a process using biotechnology in any form; biotechnological process includes the use of microorganisms, cell lines, enzymes, genetic material and recombinant DNA techniques. An application for a patent relating to a biotechnological process shall be deemed to be non-obvious if it incorporates novel features arising from the application of such process. Where an invention is determined to involve a method of agricultural or horticultural practice, or the mere presentation of goods, that invention may be subject to examination under this Act; however, any claim found to fall wholly within these categories shall be considered *section withdrawn* and not patentable as provided herein.

Where any patent is granted and subsequently found by a competent authority to have been obtained through fraudulent means, including but not limited to the misrepresentation of prior art or the suppression of material information during examination, the Controller may, subject to due process and affording the patentee an opportunity for hearing, order the patent to be declared invalid. This declaration shall extinguish all rights conferred by the grant and render the patent unenforceable against third parties. Further, any party demonstrably prejudiced by the fraudulent procurement of the patent may institute civil proceedings seeking damages proportionate to their loss, as provided herein.
