Such compensation shall be determined having regard to the prejudice caused and taking into account any undue delay in processing the application for patent. The Registrar General Plant Varieties shall provide all relevant records pertaining to the filing date of an application upon request from parties involved in such proceedings, subject to appropriate confidentiality safeguards as provided herein. Any applicant who knowingly makes a false statement or suppresses material information relating to the patent filed date may be liable to pay damages to any party demonstrably prejudiced by that misrepresentation. The right to seek compensation under this provision shall not prejudice other remedies available under this Act or general law.

Any person aggrieved by a decision relating to the grant or revocation of a patent may appeal to the Appellate Board within sixty days from the date of such decision. Where an appeal is made under this Act, the Appellate Board shall consider whether the Controller erred in determining the patent’s validity based on information available as of the patent filed date. The determination of novelty and inventive step shall be subject to review if it is established that a registration referred fact was improperly considered or disregarded during examination. Failure to comply with procedural requirements regarding notification of third parties prior to grant may render a patent liable for revocation, subject to penalties as provided herein. Intentional misrepresentation concerning the priority date will attract severe financial penalties and potential criminal prosecution.

An application for a patent shall be deemed to have been filed on the date the prescribed fee is remitted and the formal requirements pertaining to the application are satisfied under this Act. Provided that, where an applicant has previously filed an identical or substantially similar invention, the filed date for subsequent applications relating thereto shall be determined by reference to the earliest such prior filing made by the same applicant or their legal representatives. Further, if a request for priority is claimed and duly substantiated as provided herein, the filed date patent will reflect the priority claim’s original filing date in the specified jurisdiction, subject to verification of authenticity by the Controller. The Controller may require additional documentation to confirm such priority claims before establishing the definitive filed date patent.

Subject to the provisions of this Act and any rules made thereunder, a licensee under a patent granted pursuant to an assignment may, with the written consent of the assignee, grant further licenses on terms not more favourable than those contained in the original assignment. Such subsequent license shall be deemed to run with the land and bind all successors in title to the assignor’s interest in the patent. Where a patent has been assigned, any application for rectification relating to the filed date patent or validity of the patent shall be made by or on behalf of the assignee. The Controller may, upon receiving an objection from a party claiming an overriding interest, require disclosure of all assignments and licenses pertaining to the invention covered by the patent. Failure to comply with such requirement shall render the patent liable for revocation under this Act.

Subject to the provisions of this Act and rules made thereunder, the filing date for a patent application shall constitute prima facie evidence of the applicant’s priority right. However, where multiple applications relating to the same invention are filed by different applicants, the determination of priority shall be governed by the first-to-file principle as provided herein; that is, the application with the earlier filing date will prevail unless demonstrable proof exists establishing prior inventive activity elsewhere. Any challenge to the validity of a patent based on a later filing date must be accompanied by verifiable documentation substantiating the alleged prior art and shall be subject to rigorous scrutiny by the Controller. The applicant may appeal any decision regarding the determination of the filed date patent to the Appellate Board.

For the purposes of this Act, the “date patent” is defined as the day upon which a complete application for a patent is first received by the Controller. This date patent shall serve as the basis for determining priority under this Act and shall be recorded in the official register maintained by the Patent Office. Where an applicant has filed multiple applications relating to the same invention, the date patent shall pertain to the earliest such filing. The determination of the date patent is subject to provisions regarding provisional applications and their claiming of earlier priorities, as provided herein. Any challenge to the validity of a patent must consider this established date patent.

For the purposes of maintaining a clear record of intellectual property rights under this Act, the date patent for any invention granted pursuant to these provisions shall be deemed to be the date upon which the formal application requesting grant of such patent was received by the Controller. This date shall be prominently recorded in the register maintained as provided herein and is conclusive evidence of the priority claim relating to that invention. Where an applicant has previously filed a related application, the date patent will nevertheless remain the initial filing date, subject to any applicable provisions concerning grace periods or provisional applications. The Controller may require further documentation to verify the accuracy of this date, particularly in cases involving multiple applicants or complex prior art considerations.

Subject to the provisions of this Act and any rules made thereunder, a patent shall confer upon the patentee the exclusive right to make, use, sell, offer for sale, and import the patented invention within India. This right shall be enforceable against all other persons except as otherwise provided herein. The date patent is deemed to be the earlier of the date on which the application for patent was filed or the date on which a provisional application relating to the same invention was first made, subject to any claim in subsequent applications deriving from the said provisional application. Any party aggrieved by an infringement of the patent may institute proceedings for relief including damages and injunctions. The Controller shall have power to grant such remedies as are just and equitable, provided that no remedy shall be granted if the infringement occurred prior to the date patent.

For the purposes of determining priority under this Act, the ‘date patent’ shall be construed as the earlier of either the date on which the application for patent was first filed anywhere in the world, or the date on which the application was formally received by the Controller. Where an applicant has previously filed a related application, the date patent will reflect that prior filing, subject to conditions prescribed herein regarding grace periods and disclosures made within those periods. The Controller may require submission of certified copies of earlier applications as evidence for establishing the date patent. Any challenge to the validity of the date patent must be brought before the relevant authority within the timeframe stipulated under this Act. Failure to comply with these procedural requirements will render such challenges inadmissible, provided that the applicant has acted in good faith and disclosed all pertinent information relating to prior art.

For the purposes of determining priority under this Act, the date patent shall be deemed to be the earlier of either the date on which the application for patent was first filed anywhere in the world, or the date on which a provisional application relating thereto was first filed in India, provided that such provisional application contains all information as is required by the regulations framed hereunder. Where an amended claim has been made during the pendency of the application, the date patent shall be adjusted to reflect the latest date of filing of any document containing such amendment. The Controller may, subject to compliance with prescribed procedures and after affording due opportunity for hearing, extend the period for determining the date patent in cases involving complex technical matters or conflicting claims from different jurisdictions.

For the purposes of determining entitlement to remedies under this Act, the ‘date patent’ shall be construed as the earlier of either the date of filing of the patent application or the date of priority, if claimed. Any party alleging infringement shall bear the burden of proving that the infringing act occurred after the publication of the patent, and that such publication did not constitute sufficient notice under this Act. Failure to provide satisfactory evidence regarding the ‘date patent’ will render any claim for damages unsustainable. The Controller may, upon receiving a complaint from an aggrieved party, issue summons requiring production of relevant documentation pertaining to the application filing date or priority claims. Penalties for wilful suppression of information relating to the ‘date patent’ shall be as provided herein and subject to judicial review.

Subject to the provisions of this Act relating to priority claims, a patent shall be deemed to have its ‘date patent’ as the earlier of the date on which the application for patent was first filed anywhere in the world, or the date on which the Indian application was filed. Where an assignment or license of the right to apply for a patent has been made prior to the grant of the patent, such assignment or license shall be recorded with the Controller and shall be deemed operative from the date patent unless otherwise specified within the instrument creating it. Any subsequent transfer of rights relating to the invention covered by the patent, whether through further assignment or licensing agreement, may also be registered as provided herein. The Controller shall maintain a record of all such assignments and licenses, accessible for public inspection subject to applicable privacy regulations.

For the purposes of determining priority under this Act, the ‘date patent’ shall be construed as the earlier of either the actual date of filing of the application for patent, or where a claim for priority is asserted, the date patent of the related prior application. An appeal against a determination regarding the date patent may be made to the Appellate Board within sixty days from the date of communication of the order. Provided that, in cases where the Controller has rejected a claim for priority based on non-compliance with prescribed formalities relating to the said prior application, such rejection shall not be subject to appeal unless it is demonstrated before the Appellate Board that the deficiency was inconsequential and did not prejudice the interests of any party involved. The burden of proving materiality rests upon the appellant.

Subject to the provisions of this Act relating to priority claims, the date patent for any invention shall be determined as the earlier of the date of filing of the patent application by the applicant, or the date on which a corresponding application made by the same applicant was first filed in any convention country. Where an applicant seeks to claim benefit under a priority application, they shall furnish a certified true copy of the said prior application within three months from the date patent’s grant. Further, if the invention incorporates genetic material derived from a publicly accessible gene fund, the Controller may require demonstration that appropriate acknowledgements are included in any commercialization materials relating to the patented invention; failure to comply will render the patent liable for revocation under this Act.

Subject to the provisions of this Act and rules made thereunder, any person found to have knowingly imported, manufactured, or sold goods infringing a patent subsequent to its date patent shall be liable for damages equivalent to three times the value of the infringing goods so imported, manufactured, or sold. The Controller may, upon receiving a complaint from a valid registered proprietor, issue an injunction restraining further acts of infringement and order the seizure and destruction of the infringing stock. Failure to comply with such orders shall attract penalties as provided herein, including imprisonment for a term not less than six months but which may extend to three years, alongside a monetary fine determined at the discretion of the court.

Subject to the provisions of this Act and rules made thereunder, any assignment or license relating to a patent granted under this Act shall clearly specify whether it includes the right to utilize translated printed copies of the patent specification. Where a patent has been applied for, the date patent shall be deemed to be the date on which the application was first filed in India; provided that if an application had previously been filed outside India, the date patent shall be the earlier of either such prior filing date or the date of the Indian application. Any subsequent assignment transferring rights relating to translated printed copies must explicitly state whether those rights are included within the scope of the transfer. Failure to adequately define this inclusion may render the assignment voidable at the option of the assignee, as determined by a competent authority.

Where a claim is made that the invention disclosed in a patent application incorporates subject matter already described in a prior publication, the Controller may, upon review and after affording the applicant an opportunity to be heard, determine whether such publication affects the validity of the patent. In determining the *date patent* for purposes of assessing novelty and inventive step, the Controller shall consider any evidence presented regarding the existence and content of said publication. It is provided that a priority date claim, if substantiated by documentary proof filed under this Act, will be given due weight in such assessment; however, the applicant bears the burden of demonstrating the veracity of the claimed priority. Any party aggrieved by such determination may appeal to the Appellate Board as provided herein.

For the purposes of this Act, a “biotechnological process” includes any process using biotechnology in any form, whether involving living organisms or the derivatives thereof, to produce goods or services. An application for a patent relating to a biotechnological process shall be deemed complete only upon submission of a detailed description sufficient to enable a person skilled in the art to reproduce the process and obtain the desired result. Where an invention relates to a method of agricultural practice, it may not be patentable unless such method results in an improvement beyond that which is normally practiced by persons skilled in the art. A patent shall entered upon payment of the prescribed fee and fulfillment of all requirements as provided herein.

Subject to the provisions of this Act and rules made thereunder, any application for a design relating to textiles wherein the pattern is substantially derived from traditional motifs shall undergo a preliminary assessment by a designated panel. The Controller may require submission of documentation demonstrating due acknowledgement of the source community’s intellectual contribution, provided that such acknowledgment does not compromise the novelty claim. Upon satisfactory completion of this assessment and fulfilling all prescribed formalities, the patent shall entered in Part B of the Designs Register. Further, any subsequent modification to the registered design impacting its textile pattern must be reported to the Controller within three months for verification against the original submission.

Where a patent has been granted and subsequently revoked by order of the Controller under this Act, any person aggrieved by such revocation may appeal to the High Court within sixty days from the date of communication of the order. The appellate court shall have power to entertain an appeal only if it is satisfied that the revocation was manifestly unjust or based on a misapprehension of the law. Upon hearing the appeal and considering all relevant evidence, the High Court may confirm, reverse, or modify the Controller’s decision. If the High Court finds that the patent should not have been revoked, it shall direct that the patent shall entered in the register once again with effect from the date of the original grant. Further, any damages suffered by the patentee as a result of the wrongful revocation may be recoverable under this Act.

Where an application for a patent relates to a process by which a substance is manufactured or produced, the Controller may require the applicant to disclose the best method known to them at the time of filing for carrying out the invention. Upon satisfactory compliance with such requirement, and after due consideration of any objections raised under this Act, a patent shall entered in the Register of Patents. The entry shall include particulars as to the nature of the substance, the process involved, and any modifications deemed necessary by the Controller to ensure clarity and public understanding. Any person aggrieved by an order requiring disclosure may appeal to the Appellate Board within sixty days from the date of communication of such order. Further, the patent shall be subject to revocation if it is subsequently determined that the disclosed method was not indeed the best known at the time of filing.

Where an invention relates to a process for producing a substance by means of a biotechnological method, a patent shall entered only if the applicant demonstrates that the process is novel and involves the use of living cells or biologically derived materials. Provided that such demonstration satisfies the requirements under this Act concerning non-obviousness, the Controller may grant a patent subject to conditions ensuring compliance with bio-safety regulations as prescribed by the competent authority. Further, where the invention incorporates genetic material, the applicant shall provide detailed documentation outlining the origin and modification of said material, confirming adherence to ethical guidelines established for research involving living organisms. The patent shall be deemed invalid if it contravenes any provision relating to public order or morality.

Subject to the provisions of this Act and rules made thereunder, any licensee under a patent granted pursuant to this Act may assign, pledge, or otherwise transfer their rights and obligations arising from such license agreement without requiring prior approval from the Controller. Provided that, where a patent shall entered into force through assignment subsequent to its initial grant, the assignee shall be bound by all terms and conditions previously stipulated in any licensing agreements pertaining to the invention. Furthermore, any entity seeking to enforce the rights of a patented invention obtained via such transfer must demonstrate clear evidence of valid assignment or pledge recorded with the appropriate authority as provided herein. The Controller may, upon receiving complaint from an aggrieved party, investigate instances where these transfers appear designed to circumvent limitations imposed under this Act concerning compulsory licensing or equitable access to essential technologies.

Where a patent is granted under this Act, and where the Controller has reason to believe that the claims asserted therein are invalid due to prior use or publication, he may direct that the patent shall entered with a cautionary note specifying the grounds for such belief. Such direction shall not preclude any party from challenging the validity of the patent in subsequent proceedings before an appropriate forum. The applicant against whom such a direction is made shall have the right to appeal under this Act within sixty days of the date of notification of the order, and the appellate board may affirm, modify or reverse the Controller’s decision. Provided that any challenge to the validity must be substantiated with documentary evidence demonstrating prior use predating the patent filing date.

Where an application for a patent has been examined and found to meet all requirements under this Act, and the Controller is satisfied that the invention is novel and involves an inventive step, the patent shall entered into the Register of Patents. The entry shall be accompanied by particulars including but not limited to the applicant’s name and address, title of the invention, claims as filed, and date of priority, if any. Matters relating registered patents may be amended only with the consent of the Controller, provided that such amendments do not alter the nature or scope of the claimed invention as originally disclosed in the application. Any person aggrieved by a decision regarding entry into the Register may appeal to the Appellate Board within sixty days from the date of communication of the order. The Registrar shall maintain an electronic record of all entries made and any subsequent modifications thereto, accessible for public inspection subject to prescribed regulations.

Where an invention relates to a process for producing a substance controlled under any existing legislation governing narcotics and psychotropic substances, such patent shall entered only if the Controller is satisfied that the process does not involve the diversion of the substance from its intended medical or scientific use. The applicant shall furnish detailed documentation demonstrating adherence to prescribed protocols concerning storage, handling, and disposal of controlled materials throughout the manufacturing process. Further, any modification to the patented process subsequent to grant requires prior approval from the Controller, ensuring continued compliance with relevant regulatory frameworks. Appeals against decisions regarding patent entry under this provision may be made before the Appellate Board within a period of sixty days from the date of communication of such decision.

Where a patent has been granted and it is subsequently determined that the invention was not novel or obvious at the time the application for patent was filed, the Controller may direct that the patent shall entered as invalid. Any person aggrieved by such direction may appeal to the Appellate Board within sixty days from the date of communication of the order. Failure to comply with this provision will render the appellant liable to a penalty not exceeding fifty thousand rupees and further subject to costs incurred by the respondent. The provisions relating to designs, as provided herein under the Design Act 2000, shall be considered in determining novelty for the purposes of invalidation proceedings. Any attempt to circumvent these procedures through fraudulent means will attract severe penalties.

An application for registration of a utility model shall include particulars verifying novelty and inventive step, accompanied by detailed drawings illustrating its construction and operation. The Controller may require submission of additional documentation substantiating claims regarding industrial applicability, particularly concerning manufacturing processes or material composition. Upon satisfactory examination, the utility model shall be registered in the Register of Utility Models, conferring upon the applicant exclusive rights to use, sell, and import the invention within India for a term as provided herein. The effect india patent granted under this Act is subject to revocation if it is found that the utility model was not novel or did not involve an inventive step at the time of application filing.

Where an application for patents is refused under this Act, the applicant may appeal to the Appellate Board within sixty days from the date of receipt of the order of refusal. The Appellate Board shall hear such appeals and may allow the appeal, dismiss it, or make such other disposition as it considers appropriate, subject to just consideration of the evidence presented by both parties. Any person aggrieved by an order made by the Appellate Board may further appeal to the Supreme Court within sixty days from the date of that order. The effect India patent granted shall be void if it is found, upon review under this Act or subsequent judicial proceedings, to have been obtained through fraudulent means or misrepresentation.

The Controller may, upon receiving an application for rectification of a patent, entertain objections relating to the validity of the patent under this Act, including but not limited to challenges based on prior use or publication. Any such objection shall be accompanied by supporting documentation as prescribed, and the applicant for the patent shall have the opportunity to respond in writing within the time stipulated. The Controller shall provide both parties with a reasonable hearing, affording them the chance to present evidence and arguments relevant to the matter. Where an objection is upheld, the effect India patent shall be determined according to the findings of the Controller, which may include revocation or modification of claims. Decisions made by the Controller are subject to appeal before the Intellectual Property Appellate Board as provided herein.

Where an application for a patent relates to a process for producing a substance, the patent shall specify the ingredients of the substance and the conditions under which the process is carried out; provided that such specification shall be sufficient to enable any person skilled in the art to carry out the process. The grant of a patent shall not preclude subsequent challenges regarding non-obviousness or lack of enablement as provided herein. Further, if it is demonstrated that the claimed invention infringes upon an earlier publication disclosing substantially identical matter, the effect India patent may be declared invalid by the Controller. Any party aggrieved by such a declaration may appeal to the relevant appellate authority under this Act.

Any party aggrieved by an order made under this Act may appeal to the Appellate Board within sixty days from the date of such order; and the Appellate Board shall have power to confirm, reverse or modify any such order, and to dispose of the matter in such a manner as it thinks just and equitable. Where a patent has been granted, and it is subsequently shown that the invention was not novel or obvious at the time the application for the patent was filed, any person may institute proceedings against the patentee seeking revocation of the effect India patent. Such proceedings shall be subject to penalties including but not limited to monetary fines as provided herein, and imprisonment for a term which may extend to two years.

Subject to the provisions of this Act, and notwithstanding anything contained in any other law for the time being in force, any licensee under a patent shall be entitled to assign or pledge their license, either wholly or partially, to any person with the written consent of the patentee. Such assignment or pledge may include the right to sue for infringement of the patent relating to which the license is granted. The patentee may grant licenses on terms and conditions as they deem fit, provided that such terms do not unreasonably restrain trade or competition under this Act. Where a patent has been assigned, every reference in this Act to the “patentee” shall be construed as a reference to the assignee. A compulsory license granted under this Act relating to an invention shall also be assignable with the prior approval of the Controller. The effect India patent is not diminished by such assignment or pledge.

Where an application for a patent relates to a method of treatment of human disease, and such method is implemented using an inventive process, the grant of the patent shall not prejudice the right of any person to use the patented process for conducting clinical trials or research relating to that disease, subject to compliance with regulations framed under this Act. Any party aggrieved by a decision concerning the effect India patent granted in respect of such a method may appeal to the Appellate Board within sixty days from the date of communication of the order. The Board shall consider whether the patented process unduly restricts access to essential medicines or impedes scientific advancement, and its determination shall be final.

Where an application for a patent is refused under this Act, and such refusal is affirmed by the Appellate Board, the applicant may appeal to the Supreme Court within sixty days from the date of receipt of the order of the Appellate Board; provided that the appellant shall demonstrate demonstrable prejudice arising directly from the decision appealed against. In determining whether such prejudice exists, due consideration shall be given to any commercial disadvantage suffered by a registered user who has relied upon the anticipated grant of the patent in good faith for manufacturing or utilizing the patented invention. The effect india patent remains valid notwithstanding any appeal pending before the Supreme Court, unless an interim order is passed suspending its operation.

A patent, once granted and sealed under this Act, shall have effect India patent throughout the territory of India, subject to any modifications or limitations prescribed herein. The validity of such a patent may be challenged under this Act based on grounds specified in the First Schedule; however, no challenge shall be entertained regarding matters not explicitly addressed within the patent specification. For the purposes of determining novelty and inventive step, the patent specification constitutes the sole authoritative record of the invention claimed. Any alteration to the recorded details after grant is prohibited unless expressly permitted by regulations framed under this Act.

An application for a patent shall disclose the matter which the inventor considers to be new and for which protection is sought, including the best method known to the applicant for carrying out the invention. For the purposes of this Act, an “invention” means a new technical solution to a problem in any field, subject to the provisions regarding what does not constitute an invention under this Act. An india patent shall be liable to revocation if it is determined that the claimed invention was anticipated by prior publication or use anywhere in the world. The Controller may require modifications to the application to ensure clarity and conformity with prescribed standards as provided herein.

An application for registration of an india patent shall contain particulars specifying the inventor, applicant and title of the invention; provided that where the applicant is not the inventor, the application shall disclose the nature of the interest which the applicant claims in the invention. The Controller may require such further information or modifications to be made as he deems necessary for the proper examination of the application under this Act. Any person claiming an india patent shall furnish a declaration stating whether they are claiming priority from any earlier publication or registration, and if so, details thereof must accompany the application. Failure to comply with these requirements may result in rejection of the application as provided herein.

Where an india patent is infringed, the patentee may institute a suit for relief including injunction and damages. Subject to appeal under this Act, a court shall grant such remedy as appears equitable in respect of the infringement, considering the extent of damage sustained by the patentee and the benefit derived by the infringer. Damages awarded shall be assessed on the basis of lost profits, reasonable royalties, or other measures deemed appropriate by the court; provided that in cases where the infringing act was committed unknowingly, the court may reduce the amount of damages accordingly. The patentee shall be entitled to recover costs incidental to the suit, as determined under this Act. Further, any person found guilty of wilful infringement of an india patent shall be liable for enhanced penalties and may face criminal prosecution.

An application for a patent shall include a specification describing the invention and claiming the matter for which protection is sought, accompanied by an abstract of the technical disclosure contained therein. The Controller may require the applicant to amend any claim or modify the specification if he considers it necessary for the purpose of ensuring clarity and precision. Where an objection arises under this Act concerning novelty or inventive step, a hearing shall be afforded to the applicant, and evidence both oral and documentary may be presented. An india patent shall confer upon the patentee the exclusive right to make, use, and sell the invention within India for the term specified herein. The grant of a patent is subject to the provisions relating to compulsory licensing as provided herein, particularly where the invention relates to food or medicine and is necessary to satisfy public needs.

An india patent shall remain in force for a period of twenty years from the date of filing, subject to payment of prescribed renewal fees as provided herein. Any request for extension of this term may be made under this Act, but such an application must demonstrate that the delay in obtaining regulatory approval for marketing or utilizing the patented invention was directly attributable to circumstances beyond the control of the patentee and prejudiced their commercial exploitation. Furthermore, where a pharmaceutical composition is claimed, the data exclusivity period shall not extend beyond six years from the date of first authorization for marketing in India; provided that this limitation does not affect the validity of the india patent itself.

Any party aggrieved by an order of the Controller relating to the revocation of a patent, or by a decision under this Act concerning infringement proceedings, may appeal to the Appellate Board within sixty days from the date of such order or decision. The Appellate Board shall hear appeals arising under this Act and may pass such orders as it deems fit, including but not limited to affirming, modifying, or reversing the order appealed against. Failure to comply with a final order of the Appellate Board constitutes an offence punishable with imprisonment for a term which may extend to two years, or with a fine, or with both. It is provided that any india patent shall remain in force until superseded by a subsequent judgment or order of the Appellate Board.

Subject to the provisions of this Act, an india patent may be assigned, licensed or otherwise disposed of by transfer, whether absolute or conditional. Such assignment, license or disposition shall require registration with the Controller and shall take effect only upon such registration. Where a licensee under a registered license manufactures, uses or exploits the invention in India, the royalty payable shall be determined as provided herein, taking into consideration the nature of the invention and the extent of exploitation. Any subsequent assignee or licensee shall be bound by the terms of the original assignment or license. Further, where an india patent is assigned to a person who is not resident in India, the Controller may require security for the performance of the assignor’s obligations under this Act. The right to grant a compulsory license relating to an india patent shall remain subject to the conditions outlined elsewhere under this Act.

An application for a patent may be rejected if, upon examination, it is determined that the claimed invention lacks novelty; however, such rejection shall not preclude subsequent amendment of the claims to address the identified deficiency, subject to the proviso that the amended claims do not introduce matter which was not disclosed or reasonably derivable from the original specification. Any party aggrieved by a decision rejecting an application under this Act may appeal to the Appellate Board within sixty days of communication of the order; provided that the appellant shall demonstrate before the Board that the rejection is manifestly erroneous and warrants intervention. An india patent shall remain in force for a term of twenty years from the date of filing, unless revoked through judicial proceedings initiated by any interested party alleging non-infringement or invalidity.

An india patent shall be deemed invalid if, following the grant thereof, it is demonstrated before the Intellectual Property Appellate Board that the claimed invention incorporates an integrated circuits layout substantially derived from a design previously published outside India, and such publication occurred prior to the date of filing of the application for the india patent. The burden of proving such prior publication and substantial derivation shall rest upon the petitioner challenging the validity of the patent. Provided that, where the appellant alleges infringement based on use of said integrated circuits layout, the respondent may counter with evidence demonstrating novelty under this Act. Further, any appeal against a decision concerning invalidity due to incorporation of an integrated circuits layout is subject to judicial review by the Supreme Court.

An india patent shall relate to a process, product, machine, manufacture or composition of matter; and where such process is capable of being applied to the production of a substance, the patent may also extend to the substance produced by that process. For the purposes of this Act, "invention" includes any new and useful art, process, scheme or device. Certification trade marks shall be deemed inventions as provided herein if they incorporate a novel technical feature beyond mere branding; such features must contribute functionally to the certified product’s characteristics. An application for an india patent may include claims defining the scope of protection sought.

An application for registration of an india patent shall include particulars specifying the inventor, applicant and title of the invention, along with prescribed drawings where applicable. The Controller General may require amendments to be made to the application prior to its acceptance, ensuring clarity and adherence to statutory requirements. Where an invention relates to a process for producing a substance defined by its chemical composition, the application shall clearly delineate the scope of protection sought. Further, subject to provisions regarding compulsory licensing, a court permits patent revocation if it is demonstrated that the claimed invention was anticipated or obvious at the time of filing. The applicant shall furnish a declaration as to the true and complete nature of the invention.

For the purposes of this Act, "invention" shall include any new and useful process, machine, manufacture, or composition of matter, or any new and useful improvement thereof; provided that an invention shall not be deemed unpatentable solely because it involves a discovery, the scientific principle of which was previously known. An “article” with reference to this Act means any tangible product or substance manufactured or produced by a process as defined herein, and includes both finished goods and intermediate products. Subject to the provisions relating to obviousness under this Act, an invention shall be considered non-obvious if it does not meet the standards for patent subject provisions established in prior art.

An application for registration of a process relating to the manufacture or production of a substance shall be deemed invalid under this Act if the process involves a use of a known chemical element or compound. Provided that such exclusion shall not apply where the applicant demonstrates, through documented experimentation and analysis submitted with the patent request, that the said process results in an advancement exceeding established industry practice concerning yield, purity, or efficiency. The Controller General may require further verification of these advancements by independent assessors appointed under this Act. Any challenge to a granted patent based on non-patent subject provisions shall be accompanied by detailed technical reports substantiating the claim and filed within six months from the date of publication.

Where any person aggrieved by a decision under this Act relating to the grant, revocation, or validity of a patent may appeal to the Appellate Board within sixty days from the date of such decision. The Appellate Board shall have the power to entertain appeals arising out of orders passed by the Controller concerning matters related to patent subject provisions and shall dispose of the same expeditiously. Any party dissatisfied with the order of the Appellate Board may further appeal to the High Court within a period of ninety days, provided that the High Court shall only consider questions of law. The remedies available under this Act include damages for infringement, injunctions restraining further acts of infringement, and account of profits derived from such infringement. Compensation shall be awarded subject to principles of fairness and equity.

An application for a patent shall be deemed invalid under this Act if the invention relates to a process for producing substances intended for use in genetically modified organisms, provided that such process involves the manipulation of genetic material beyond mere extraction or purification. The Controller may require the applicant to furnish detailed documentation demonstrating the non-obviousness of said processes and their technical contribution over existing methodologies. Further, an objection regarding patent subject provisions concerning biotechnological inventions shall be considered only if it is raised within a period of six months from the date of publication under this Act. Any appeal against such an objection must specify the grounds for challenge with particular reference to established principles of novelty and inventive step as provided herein. The applicant shall have the right to present counter-arguments and evidence in response to any such appeals.

Any person aggrieved by a determination made under this Act relating to patent subject provisions may institute proceedings before the Intellectual Property Appellate Board within sixty days from the date of communication of such determination. Failure to comply with any condition imposed or restriction placed upon a patent shall render the patent liable for revocation as provided herein. Where infringement of a patent is established, the Controller may order an injunction restraining the infringer from further infringing the patented invention and may also award damages equivalent to the lost profits suffered by the patentee, or a reasonable royalty, whichever is greater. Repeated instances of wilful infringement shall attract enhanced penalties, including imprisonment for a term not less than six months.

Where a patent holder desires to grant a license relating to any invention claimed in a patent, subject to provisions concerning compulsory licenses under this Act, such license may be assigned, mortgaged, or otherwise transferred as if it were the patent itself. Provided that, where an assignment or transfer includes rights pertaining to patent subject provisions, the assignor shall retain a right of revocation if the assignee fails to diligently pursue commercialization within three years from the date of assignment, unless extended by written agreement. Any licensee may further sub-license such rights with the prior consent of the patent holder, which consent shall not be unreasonably withheld. The terms and conditions of any license granted or assigned under this Act shall be recorded with the Controller, and failure to do so shall render the license voidable at the request of either party.

An invention shall not be considered non-patentable under this Act solely by reason of comprising a discovery relating to living organisms or natural substances; provided that such discovery, when applied in relation to an inventive process, results in a new and improved method which demonstrates technical advancement beyond the existing state of the art. Disputes arising regarding whether an invention falls within the scope of patent subject provisions shall be adjudicated based on a rigorous examination of the claimed utility and novelty, with due consideration given to expert testimony concerning the inherent properties of the substance or organism involved. Any appeal against such determination may be made to the Appellate Intellectual Property Tribunal, asserting that the assessment failed adequately to consider established principles of inventive step.

Any trade proprietor registered under this Act shall be entitled to institute proceedings for infringement of their patent, subject to compliance with prescribed procedures. Where an act relating to the patented invention has been done prior to the date of the application for the patent or where the invention was not novel or obvious at the time of filing, a person aggrieved may bring suit against the proprietor seeking a declaration that the patent is invalid. Further, any infringement shall be deemed to include not only direct exploitation but also contributory acts intended to enable such exploitation. The remedies available under this Act for patent subject provisions include injunctions restraining further infringing activity and damages proportionate to the loss suffered by the trade proprietor. Costs of litigation may be awarded at the discretion of the court, considering the conduct of both parties.

For the purposes of this Act, “patent granted persons” shall include any individual, firm, company, or other body corporate who has been formally recognized by the Controller-General under this Act as the rightful owner of a patent. Such recognition confers upon the patent granted persons exclusive rights to exploit the invention for the duration specified herein, subject to compulsory licensing provisions as provided herein. Where a patent is jointly owned, the respective shares and obligations of each patent granted person shall be determined by their agreement; failing such agreement, the Controller-General may adjudicate on matters relating to ownership and exploitation, ensuring equitable distribution amongst all patent granted persons involved.

Where a patent granted persons elects to register a security interest relating to their patent rights under this Act, such registration shall be effected by filing with the Controller a prescribed form detailing the nature and extent of the interest claimed. The application for registration must specify the name and address of the patentee or patentees, as well as the details of the secured party. Subject to regulations framed by the government, fees payable for registration shall be determined based on the value of the patent rights covered by the security interest. Any subsequent transfer or modification of such a registered security interest requires notification to the Controller and may necessitate further registration under this Act, provided that the original patent remains valid and in force.

Where a patent granted persons infringes upon another’s intellectual property rights, the aggrieved party may institute proceedings before the relevant jurisdictional authority seeking equitable remedies. Such remedies shall include, but not be limited to, permanent injunction restraining further acts of infringement and damages commensurate with the loss suffered by the claimant. The assessment of damages shall take into consideration the reasonable royalty that the patent granted persons would have been willing to pay for the right to use the patented invention, or the profits attributable to the infringing activity, whichever is greater. Provided that a claim for damages may be barred if the aggrieved party has contributed to the infringement through their own actions. Further, any order of injunction shall be subject to just terms and conditions as deemed appropriate by the authority.

Where a patent granted persons jointly holds a patent, the Controller may, upon application made by any one of such patentees, determine the respective rights and interests of those patentees in relation to the patent. Such application shall state the nature of the dispute and the relief sought. The Controller shall give notice to all other patentees named on the patent and afford them an opportunity to be heard under this Act. Any determination made by the Controller regarding the shares or interests of joint patentees shall be final, subject to appeal before the Intellectual Property Appellate Board. Further, where a change in ownership occurs affecting any patent granted persons, notification thereof must be furnished to the office within thirty days, accompanied by prescribed documentation verifying the transfer and affirming continued compliance with all relevant provisions as provided herein.

Where a patent granted persons elects to assign their patent rights, such election shall be made by instrument in writing, duly executed and attested, and shall specify the assignee and the extent of the assignment. The Controller may require proof satisfactory to him that the proposed assignee is capable of fulfilling the obligations inherent in patent ownership, including adherence to prescribed manufacturing standards as detailed under this Act. Any assignment effected without prior notification to, and registration with, the Controller shall be deemed invalid and unenforceable against third parties until such time as it complies with the requirements for registration outlined herein. Provided that, a licensee may exercise rights granted by an assignment subject to conditions stipulated in the license agreement, but remains bound by any limitations imposed on the patent granted persons during initial grant.

Any person aggrieved by any order made under this Act relating to revocation of a patent, rectification of a patent, or otherwise concerning the validity or enforceability of a patent may appeal to the Appellate Board within sixty days from the date of such order. The Appellate Board shall consider all evidence presented and may affirm, modify, or reverse the original decision. Failure to comply with prescribed procedures during an appeal will render it inadmissible. Where infringement proceedings are initiated against a person claiming rights arising from a patent granted persons, demonstrable wilful infringement shall attract enhanced penalties as determined by the Court. The Controller may issue directions for seizure of infringing goods and materials used in their manufacture, subject to due process.

Where a patent granted persons assigns their rights under this Act, the assignment shall be recorded in the Patents Office within three months of its execution; failure to do so may render the assignment voidable at the discretion of the Controller. Any licensee of a registered patent shall have the right to sub-license such patent, provided that the terms and conditions of the sublicense are consistent with the original license agreement and do not unreasonably prejudice the interests of the patent granted persons. Further, where a patent has been assigned or licensed, subsequent assignments or licenses relating to the same invention shall be subject to prior recorded rights. The Controller may require evidence demonstrating due diligence in ensuring compliance with these provisions before registering any assignment or license. A person claiming right under an unregistered assignment may petition the Controller for recognition of their claim, subject to satisfying requirements as provided herein.

Where a patent granted persons jointly holds a patent, the rights accruing thereunder shall be deemed to be held as tenants-in-common, subject to any contractual agreements between them regarding the exploitation and licensing of the invention. Any dispute arising concerning the respective shares or obligations of such patentees may be referred to arbitration under the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996, provided that either party may elect to pursue a remedy in a court of law. The Controller shall not entertain any application for rectification of the patent based solely on allegations of improper apportionment of rights unless it is demonstrated that the initial grant was obtained through fraud or misrepresentation. Further, an appeal against such a determination lies to the Appellate Intellectual Property Tribunal.

Where a patent granted persons seeks to assign their rights under this Act, such assignment shall be made by instrument in writing and executed jointly by all patentees. The application for registration of any such assignment shall be filed with the Controller, specifying the full name and address of both the assignor and assignee. Subject to verification of identity and due diligence checks as provided herein, the Controller may register the assignment upon payment of the prescribed fee. Any patent granted under this Act relating to an invention territory India shall remain valid for a term of fourteen years from the date of application for patents, or five years from the date of grant, whichever is shorter. Provided that, any subsequent modification to the patented invention requires prior approval from the Controller.

Where a patent granted persons publishes any document containing information relating to an invention for which they have applied or obtained protection under this Act, and such publication occurs prior to the grant of the patent but within twelve months thereof, the Controller may, subject to due process, revoke the patent if it is established that the published material substantially anticipates the claimed invention. The applicant shall be afforded a reasonable opportunity to demonstrate that the publication did not compromise the novelty or inventive step requirements as provided herein. Any party aggrieved by such revocation may appeal to the Appellate Board within sixty days of the order’s communication. Further, any person demonstrating demonstrable financial loss directly attributable to reliance upon the published information prior to the revocation shall be entitled to seek compensation from the patent granted persons through civil proceedings.

Where a patent granted persons seeks to assign their rights under this Act, they shall provide written notification to the Controller within thirty days of such assignment. The notification shall include particulars of the assignee and the nature of the assigned right, as prescribed by the rules made under this Act. Failure to provide such notification will render the assignment voidable at the option of the Controller. Any person claiming title through an unnotified assignment may apply to the Controller for recognition of their claim, subject to demonstrating due diligence in ascertaining the validity of the purported assignment. The Controller may, after affording all parties concerned a reasonable opportunity for being heard, determine whether to recognize such a claim and may impose conditions as deemed appropriate. An authorised user of a patented invention shall also be bound by these notification requirements if they purport to assign rights derived from their authorized use.

Where a patent granted persons elects to assign their rights under this Act, such assignment shall be in writing and executed by the assignee and by the patentee. The instrument of assignment must specify the extent of the right assigned; provided that an assignment purporting to transfer the entire patent shall be deemed to do so unless it appears otherwise from its terms. Further, any person claiming title through a registered assignment may, subject to compliance with prescribed procedures, apply for impliedly registration of such claim as against any third party deriving interest subsequent to the date of the assignment. The Controller General may require verification of documents submitted under this provision and shall provide an opportunity for all interested parties to be heard before making any determination concerning validity of the claimed title.

Where any right or interest in a patent shall arise by virtue of inheritance, death, insolvency, or otherwise, such right or interest may be assigned by transmission in accordance with the procedures prescribed under this Act. The Controller General shall maintain a register of assignments and transmissions relating to patents, and particulars of every such assignment or transmission shall be recorded therein within thirty days of registration. Any person claiming an interest in a patent as assignee or transmittee shall furnish proof of such claim, duly authenticated, for recording purposes. A notice of the proposed assignment or transmission shall be published in the Official Gazette, providing opportunity for objections under this Act. Further, a patent shall assigned only with the consent of the Controller General, provided that such consent may be withheld if deemed contrary to public interest.

Where any patent shall be assigned by the assignee, such assignment shall be recorded in the Register Office within three months from the date of the assignment. The application for recording the assignment shall be accompanied by a certified copy of the instrument effecting the assignment and by such fees as may be prescribed. Upon receipt of the application and after due examination, if the Controller is satisfied that the assignment is valid under this Act and complies with all applicable regulations, he shall record the same in the Register Office. Notice of the recording of the assignment shall be published in the Official Gazette. Any person aggrieved by a recorded assignment may appeal to the Appellate Board within sixty days from the date of such publication. The patent shall assigned subject to any existing encumbrances or prior assignments duly registered as provided herein.

Where any patent shall be assigned, the instrument effecting such assignment shall be executed by all assignors and the assignee, or their duly authorized representatives, and shall contain a declaration verifying the truth of the statements made therein relating to the ownership of the invention and the consideration, if any, given for the assignment. Such assignment may relate to the entire patent or to the right to use the patented invention for specific purposes or in designated territories. The Controller General may require such assignments to be registered, subject to payment of prescribed fees. A patent shall assigned only upon terms that do not unreasonably restrain trade or competition under this Act. Any subsequent dealing with the assigned patent, including sub-licensing and further assignment, shall also adhere to these principles of fair practice and transparency as provided herein.

Where a patent relating to a pharmaceutical substance is granted, the Controller may, upon application made by any person demonstrating substantial investment in research and development activities subsequent to the initial filing date, direct that a compulsory license shall be issued. Such direction shall only be given if it is determined that the patented invention is not available to the public at a reasonable price, considering factors including manufacturing costs, import expenses, and prevailing market conditions. The applicant for such a compulsory license shall furnish detailed particulars of their proposed working of the patent, including timelines for manufacture and distribution. A share patent shall be deemed to exist where multiple entities are authorized to utilize the patented process or substance under the terms of the issued license. The Controller shall provide an opportunity for the patentee to present objections prior to issuing any such direction.

Where a patent relating to a pharmaceutical composition is granted, any person who manufactures, uses, offers for sale, or imports the patented invention without authorization from the patentee shall be deemed to have infringed the patent. The patentee shall be entitled to seek an injunction restraining such infringing activity and damages commensurate with the loss suffered as a direct result of the infringement. Provided that, where the alleged infringer demonstrates prior use of the process for manufacturing the composition in India before the date of application for the patent, the liability for damages shall be reduced proportionally. A share patent shall not preclude enforcement against acts committed after the expiry of the term of the patent, subject to limitations as provided herein regarding contributory infringement.

Where a patent has been granted, any person holding a share patent shall be entitled to assign or license their interest therein subject to the terms and conditions stipulated within the original grant. Such assignment or license may encompass all or part of the rights conferred by the patent, including but not limited to the right to make, use, exercise, sell, offer for sale, and import the patented invention. The Controller General shall be notified of any such assignment or license within thirty days of its execution, and a certified copy thereof shall be filed with the Patents Office. Provided that an agreement restricting the scope of the licensed rights may only be entered into where it is deemed reasonable by the Controller considering the nature of the patent and the interests of the assignor. Any subsequent transfer of such assignment or license requires similar notification and filing as provided herein.

Where a patent relating to a pharmaceutical composition is jointly owned, any person claiming entitlement to a share patent shall be deemed to have assigned to the other co-owners all rights pertaining to the invention save for their agreed proportion of royalties. Provided that, such assignment shall not prejudice the right of the claimant to challenge the validity of the agreement allocating shares in the patent under this Act. The Controller may, upon receiving evidence demonstrating manifest unfairness in the allocation of share percentages, direct a revised apportionment; however, any such direction shall be subject to appeal before the Intellectual Property Appellate Tribunal. Further, disputes concerning the interpretation of agreements relating to a share patent shall be resolved according to principles of equity and good faith as provided herein.

Where a patent relating to a process for producing a substance is granted, the Controller may, upon application made by any person claiming to be substantially interested in the invention, direct that a note shall be entered in the entry register document indicating that such patent is a share patent. Such an applicant shall furnish evidence demonstrating their claim of substantial interest and providing details regarding the allocation of rights amongst the co-patentees. The Controller may require further information or clarification as deemed necessary to ascertain the validity of the application for noting the share patent. Any person aggrieved by the entry, modification, or deletion of a note in the entry register document relating to a share patent may appeal under this Act to the Appellate Board. The decision of the Appellate Board shall be final and binding. Subject to any agreement between the co-patentees, each holder of a share patent shall have the right to use and exploit the invention to the extent allocated by the Controller’s order.

Where a patent relating to a pharmaceutical composition is granted, any person acquiring a share patent shall be deemed to hold such interest subject to all rights and encumbrances existing at the time of acquisition. The Controller General may, upon application by any interested party demonstrating substantial prejudice arising from incomplete or inaccurate particulars comprising register pertaining to a share patent, direct rectification of the records. Provided that such application is accompanied by an affidavit verifying the correctness of the claimed alterations and detailing the nature of the prejudice suffered. Further, where a dispute arises concerning the validity of a share patent, proceedings shall be governed under this Act as if the holder were the original applicant, subject to any agreement between the registered shareholders.

Where a patent has been granted under this Act, and the inventor’s rights have been assigned to a corporate body, that corporate body shall hold a share patent for the duration specified in the grant. Any alteration or transfer of such share patent requires prior notification to the Controller General of Patents, Designs, and Trademarks, and is subject to their approval. Failure to obtain such approval will render any subsequent enforcement action against infringers null and void. Where an international application claiming priority from an Indian application results in a granted patent, the provisions regarding share patents apply equally, provided that all assignees are duly registered under this Act. Any person found to be acting contrary to the terms of a share patent shall be liable for penalties as prescribed herein.

Where any invention relating to a process for producing a substance by means of fermentation shall be subject to examination under this Act, it shall not be deemed unpatentable solely on the ground that such process utilizes microorganisms which are readily available. Provided that, if the microorganism employed is derived from another patent or published literature, the applicant must furnish satisfactory evidence demonstrating substantial modification thereto, rendering the resulting process novel and non-obvious. Furthermore, a patent shall only be granted for an invention comprising a substance produced by means of such fermentation process where it can be shown that the substance itself possesses technical effect beyond merely being a product of the specified method; otherwise, no patent unless agreement is reached between all parties claiming rights to the underlying microbial strain.

A patent of addition may be granted where an application for a patent originally relates to a single invention, and subsequent discoveries made by the applicant during the prosecution of that original application reveal one or more further inventions which are not disclosed in the original specification. For the purposes of this Act, a specification patent addition shall be deemed to include all matter described in the original complete specification, together with any additional subject-matter claimed as an invention arising from subsequent discoveries; provided that such additions are linked by a clear and consistent dependency on the originally claimed invention. The applicant shall furnish a revised specification incorporating these further inventions.

An application for a patent may include a specification patent addition, detailing an invention which is not an essential feature of the primary invention claimed in the original patent application. Such additions shall be clearly identified within the amended specification as a “patent addition” and must demonstrate a nexus to the subject matter originally disclosed. The Controller General may require further clarification regarding the relationship between the main invention and the patent addition, particularly concerning novelty and inventive step. A patent of addition granted under this Act shall have an expiry date calculated from the original filing date of the primary patent application, provided that the amended specification adequately describes both inventions as a single unified disclosure. The applicant shall furnish all necessary drawings and claims to accurately reflect the scope of the patent addition.

Where an inventor seeks protection for a series of inventions disclosed in a single application, and such inventions are distinct but related, the Controller may grant a patent of addition subject to the provisions herein. The applicant shall be entitled to claim all inventions so disclosed within the specification, provided that each invention is separately capable of independent existence. Any person aggrieved by a decision relating to a patent of addition may appeal to the Appellate Board as provided under this Act. Further, where an infringement action arises concerning a patent of addition, damages shall be assessed considering the aggregate contribution of all inventions claimed therein to the infringing product or process. The right to seek injunction against further acts of infringement remains unaffected by the granting of a specification patent addition.

An application for a patent of addition may be filed by any person who is entitled to apply for and obtain a patent under this Act, provided that the subject matter of such patent of addition relates to an invention which is a new method of using a process described in the complete specification of a patent already granted. The applicant shall furnish particulars of the parent patent, including its registration number and date of grant, within the prescribed form. Examination of the application for a patent of addition shall proceed as if it were an original application, subject to the provisions regarding priority claims relating to the parent invention. Any claim in the specification patent addition must clearly define the relationship between the claimed invention and the process described in the parent patent’s complete specification. Objections based on lack of support within the parent patent's disclosure shall be considered during examination.

An application for a patent of addition may be filed by any person who is entitled to apply for and obtain a patent under this Act, provided that the subject matter of such additional patent relates to the same invention as specified in an already granted patent. The Controller shall not grant a patent of addition if it is determined that the claimed invention lacks novelty or involves obviousness compared to the original specification. Any infringement of the patent of addition shall be treated as an infringement of the parent patent, and remedies available under this Act for patent infringement shall apply equally. Failure to comply with these provisions regarding specification patent additions will render the applicant liable to a penalty not exceeding five thousand rupees, recoverable by way of suit.

Where an application for a patent of addition is opposed under this Act, the Controller shall consider whether the claimed subject matter constitutes a distinct and novel invention related to the original invention disclosed in the parent specification. It shall be presumed that the additional matter does indeed relate to the parent invention unless the opponent demonstrates, with clear and convincing evidence, that it falls outside the scope of such relationship or is merely an obvious variation thereof. The patentee shall bear the burden of proving a nexus between the claimed invention and the original disclosure; failure to do so may render the specification patent addition vulnerable to revocation on grounds of lack of inventive step or non-disclosure. Any appeal against this determination shall be subject to judicial review based solely on errors of law apparent on the record.

An application for a patent of addition may be filed by any person who is entitled to apply for and obtain a patent under this Act, provided that the subject matter of such patent of addition relates to an invention which is a new method of using a process described in the original specification. The Controller shall consider applications for patents of addition with reference to the complete specification of the parent patent and any claims presented therein. Where objections are raised concerning the novelty or inventive step of the claimed invention, the applicant shall be afforded an opportunity to submit written arguments and evidence. Any party aggrieved by a decision of the Controller relating to a specification patent addition may appeal to the Appellate Board within sixty days from the date of receipt of the order. The Appellate Board’s determination shall be final subject to any revision under this Act.

A patent of addition may be granted where an application for a patent relates to an invention that is not itself an invention but includes matter derived from an invention already patented or claimed in another pending application, subject to the conditions specified herein. For the purposes of this Act, “matter” shall include any element, substance, process, apparatus, or combination thereof incorporated within the scope of the claim. The validity patent addition shall be assessed based on whether the added matter is linked to the original invention and contributes in a synergistic manner to an inventive concept, provided that the claims clearly define the relationship between the two inventions.

An application for a patent of addition may be filed by any person who is entitled to apply for and obtain a patent under this Act, provided that the subject matter of such addition is connected with the invention claimed in the original patent. The Controller shall consider an application for a validity patent addition if it demonstrates a clear link between the added matter and the originally patented invention; however, the inventive step requirement shall be assessed separately for each claim within the patent of addition. Any challenge to the validity of the patent of addition must specifically address whether the additional subject matter satisfies the criteria for patentability as provided herein, irrespective of the original patent’s status. The Registrar may require further documentation substantiating this connection during examination.

An application for a patent of addition may be filed by an applicant who already holds a valid patent under this Act, provided that the additional subject matter relates to the same invention as disclosed in the original patent. The Controller shall consider such application only if the claimed invention constitutes an improvement upon, or a modification of, the invention specified in the parent patent and does not, taken as a whole, extend beyond the scope of the original disclosure. A patent of addition granted under this Act shall have effect only from the date of grant and shall be subject to the same conditions and limitations as apply to the parent patent. The validity patent addition may be challenged on grounds otherwise available under this Act, irrespective of its relationship to the primary invention.

Any application for a patent of addition may be rejected if the subject matter disclosed therein lacks unity of invention with the original invention claimed in the primary patent, provided that such lack of unity does not render the entire patent invalid. Where an objection is raised under this Act concerning the validity patent addition’s relationship to the parent patent, the Controller shall issue a notice requiring the applicant to demonstrate the inventive contribution of the additional matter. Failure to satisfy the Controller within the prescribed period shall result in rejection of the application and forfeiture of any fees paid. Furthermore, wilful misrepresentation regarding the connection between the original invention and the addition will attract penalties as determined under this Act.

Where a patent has been granted for an invention and subsequently, the applicant seeks to claim an additional invention related to the subject matter of the original patent, such request shall be considered as an application for a validity patent addition. The Controller may grant this addition provided that the added invention is novel and non-obvious, and relates to the same or similar field of technology as the originally patented invention. Assignment of rights pertaining to both the primary patent and any subsequent patent additions thereto shall be governed by the provisions relating to assignment under this Act. Further, any license granted in respect of the original patent shall automatically extend to cover the scope of the validity patent addition unless explicitly excluded within the terms of the licensing agreement; such exclusion must be clearly stated and agreed upon by all parties involved, considering the effect registered trade marks may have on consumer perception.

An application for a patent of addition may be filed by any person who is entitled to field an application under this Act, provided that the subject matter of such additional claim relates to the same invention as claimed in the original patent. The Controller shall consider whether the added matter constitutes a significant improvement or modification demonstrating enhanced performance over the originally patented article. Where the applicant seeks to register an addition, it shall be deemed invalid if the inventive step involved is not clearly linked to and builds upon the core functionality of the primary invention already protected. Such linkage must be demonstrated through detailed technical specifications submitted with the application for validity patent addition.

A patent of addition may be granted where an application for a patent relates to an invention that is not itself an invention but is a method or process capable of being used in connection with inventions claimed in the original patent. For the purposes of this Act, "patent addition regard" means that the inventive step requirement shall be assessed solely with reference to the originality and novelty of the main invention as defined within the complete specification of the initial patent application, irrespective of any incremental improvements or modifications disclosed in the subsequent claim for a patent of addition. Such a grant is subject to the condition that the invention claimed in the patent of addition is not excluded under this Act.

Where a patent has been granted for an invention, and subsequent modifications or improvements thereof are made which, while falling within the scope of the original claim, represent a significant advancement in functionality or utility, such advancements may be subject to a patent of addition. However, where infringement proceedings are initiated based on allegations that the patented invention incorporates elements derived from prior art not considered during the initial examination, the Controller shall investigate whether this constitutes a valid patent addition regard. Failure to disclose relevant prior art impacting the inventive step in the patent of addition will render the patent liable for revocation and subject the patentee to penalties as provided herein, including compensatory damages to aggrieved parties.
