For the purposes of this Act, an addition validity patent shall be deemed invalid if it is established that the additional matter introduced does not result in a material advancement over the prior art considered as a whole. The determination of materiality shall take into account the technical effect achieved and the overall contribution to the field of technology. Subject to this, a challenge to the addition validity may only be brought within five years from the grant of the patent or from the date of first commercial exploitation of the invention, whichever is earlier. Provided that, an objection based on obviousness relating solely to the main invention shall not invalidate the addition validity patent.

Where a patent has been granted and its validity is challenged based on prior usage or publication, the Controller may, subject to due process, order an inquiry into the matter. If, following such inquiry, it is determined that the claimed invention lacks novelty or involves a lack of inventive step in relation to the main invention described within the complete specification, the patent shall not be invalidated solely on this ground if the addition validity patent represents a significant and non-obvious improvement thereto. The patentee shall have the right to present evidence and arguments demonstrating the inventive contribution of the added subject matter. Furthermore, any party aggrieved by an order relating to the revocation or affirmation of such a patent may appeal under this Act to the Intellectual Property Appellate Board. Compensation for damages arising from infringement remains unaffected by challenges to the validity of the addition validity patent.

An application for a patent of addition may be filed by any person who is entitled to apply for and obtain a patent under this Act, provided that the subject matter of such patent of addition relates to the invention claimed in a patent already granted. The Controller shall not grant a patent of addition if it appears that the additional matter does not contribute directly to the improvement or modification of the existing patented invention. Further, an addition validity patent shall be deemed invalid where it is established that the inventive step, if any, resides solely within the original invention and does not constitute a substantial advance in the field. The applicant must demonstrate, through documentary evidence, how the claimed additional matter enhances the functionality or utility as compared to the initial patented subject matter, subject to examination under this Act.

An application for a patent may claim as an invention an addition to a process, machine, manufacture, or composition of matter already existing, provided that such addition results in a new and useful article or process. Where a patent has been granted based on a claim for an addition validity patent, the Controller shall not entertain any challenge questioning the novelty or inventive step solely on the basis that the underlying invention was previously known. Any party aggrieved by the grant of such a patent may institute proceedings under this Act seeking revocation; however, it shall be presumed that the addition confers a substantial and commercially exploitable advantage unless proven otherwise through expert testimony and demonstrable evidence of diminished utility. Failure to provide such evidence will result in dismissal of the challenge and imposition of costs as determined by the Controller.

The Controller may, upon receiving an objection from a third party challenging the validity of a patent, direct the patentee to furnish such information and clarification as the Controller deems necessary to substantiate the inventive step and industrial applicability claimed in the patent. Such direction shall not preclude the patentee from subsequently presenting counter-arguments or evidence refuting the grounds for objection. Where an addition validity patent is granted based on modifications to a previously patented invention, any challenge asserting that these modifications do not constitute a novel and non-obvious improvement over the prior art may be considered by the Controller; however, it shall be presumed that the claimed subject matter possesses inventive step unless proven otherwise through clear and convincing evidence presented under this Act. The patentee shall have the right to appeal any decision of the Controller relating to such objections.

An amend application for a patent may be entertained where the applicant demonstrates that the proposed modifications do not substantially alter the nature of the invention claimed. Such an amendment shall only be permissible if it is consistent with the disclosure initially presented in the complete specification and does not introduce any matter which lacks support in the original description. The Controller shall, prior to allowing an amend application patent, provide a written opportunity for objection by any interested party who has previously filed a document or communicated concerning the invention. Any such objection must be substantiated with evidence demonstrating prejudice resulting from the amendment. Further, the applicant shall pay the prescribed fee for processing the amended application.

Where an amendment is sought to an application for a patent after the first publication thereof under this Act, such amendment shall be permissible only if it relates to a matter which could have been objected to had the objection arisen during the examination of the original application. The applicant seeking the amend application patent shall furnish an affidavit verifying that the amended specification does not contain any information or substance which was not disclosed or reasonably derivable from the originally filed documents. Failure to do so renders the amendment void, and subject to penalties as determined by the Controller. The Agriculture Commissioner may be called upon to provide expert opinion regarding amendments pertaining to agricultural processes or products, if requested by either party in a dispute concerning patent validity. Any person aggrieved by an order allowing or rejecting an amend application patent may appeal under this Act.

For the purposes of this Act, an "application patent specification" means the full and detailed description of an invention presented in support of a patent application, which must disclose the matter intended to be claimed with sufficient clarity and completeness enabling a person skilled in the art to put the same into practice. The application patent specification shall include, but not be limited to, a title describing the invention, a summary thereof, a detailed description of the invention as provided herein, and any drawings necessary to understand the invention. Further, the specification must identify the best mode contemplated by the applicant for carrying out the invention at the time of filing.

An application for a patent shall include a detailed application patent specification describing the invention and setting forth the class or classes to which it relates. The applicant may submit drawings illustrating the construction and operation of the invention where necessary for understanding the said specification, provided that such drawings adhere strictly to the prescribed standards as determined by the Controller. Any alteration made to the application patent specification after its initial filing shall be accompanied by a declaration explicitly stating the nature of the modification and its impact on the claims asserted within the document. The Registrar may require further clarification regarding any ambiguity present in the description or drawings, and failure to provide such clarity may result in rejection of the application under this Act.

Where an application patent specification contains matter which does not satisfy the requirements of novelty and inventive step under this Act, the applicant shall be afforded a single opportunity to amend the specification to address such deficiencies. Such amendment may only relate to clarifying or adding details necessary for carrying out the invention as originally claimed; substantial alteration of the subject matter disclosed is prohibited. Failure to adequately rectify these shortcomings following notification by the Controller shall render the application liable for rejection, and any subsequent attempts at re-filing will be deemed barred. The applicant aggrieved by such a rejection may appeal under this Act to the Appellate Board, presenting evidence demonstrating compliance with novelty requirements. Any order of the Appellate Board is final, subject to further appeals as provided herein.

An application patent specification shall contain a clear and concise description of the invention, enabling any person skilled in the art to put the same into practice. The specification must disclose the best method known to the applicant for carrying out the invention at the date of filing the application. It is provided that the description need not extend to matters which are necessarily disclosed by the claims. Further, the specification shall include particulars of the apparatus or substance in which the invention is embodied, if such apparatus or substance is necessary for the performance of the invention. The applicant may incorporate drawings as part of the specification, subject to compliance with prescribed rules regarding their form and content. Any alteration made to the application patent specification after its publication shall be noted by a statement under the applicant's signature.

An application patent specification shall describe the invention and how to practice it in sufficient detail to enable a person skilled in the art to carry out the invention. The description must disclose the best method contemplated by the applicant for carrying out the invention, unless such method is withheld under this Act for reasons of national security or trade secrets; provided that any such withholding shall be reported to the Controller with full justification. Furthermore, where the specification refers to drawings, such drawings shall form part of the application patent specification and clearly illustrate essential features of the invention. The applicant may include examples demonstrating the working of the invention, but these are not a substitute for a complete and enabling disclosure as provided herein.

Any person found to have knowingly made a false statement in an application patent specification before the Patent Office shall be liable for a penalty of fifty thousand rupees and may also face prosecution under relevant provisions of the Indian Penal Code. The Controller may, at any time, require the applicant or patentee to furnish further information or clarification regarding the completeness and accuracy of the invention disclosed within the application patent specification; failure to comply with such a request within the prescribed timeframe shall render the application liable for rejection or, in cases where a patent has already been granted, revocation. Furthermore, wilful suppression of prior art relevant to assessing novelty under this Act constitutes an offence punishable with imprisonment and a fine.

Subject to the provisions of this Act and rules made thereunder, an applicant for a patent may grant a license under this Act in respect of the invention disclosed in the application patent specification, either wholly or partially, and either for consideration or without consideration. Such license may be granted to any person, including another entity engaged in research and development related to the field of the invention. The terms of such license shall be recorded in writing and filed with the Controller, along with a declaration by the applicant confirming their authority to grant said license. Further, the right to assign the application patent specification or any interest therein may be exercised freely, provided that all assignments are registered as per prescribed procedures. Any subsequent licensee shall be bound by the terms of the original license agreement and subject to restrictions imposed under this Act regarding compulsory licensing.

Where an objection is taken against an application patent specification under this Act on the ground of novelty or inventive step, the applicant may submit a written argument rebutting said objection and providing further clarification regarding the prior art disclosed. Such rebuttal shall be accompanied by a certified copy of the document relied upon for the objection, unless such copy has previously been filed with the Controller. The Controller shall consider the submitted argument and any counter-argument presented by the person raising the initial objection. A decision on the matter may be appealed to an Appellate Board as provided herein, subject to the prescribed fee and within the stipulated time limit; failing which, the appeal shall stand dismissed.

An application patent specification shall define the invention claimed with sufficient clarity and completeness enabling a person skilled in the art to put the same into practice. The said specification must disclose the matter which the applicant considers to be his invention and its relation to the prior art, as provided herein. It shall include a description of the invention in a manner clear enough to enable such a person to make and use it; furthermore, the specification may incorporate drawings where necessary for understanding the invention. The grant of patent rights is contingent upon adherence to these requirements regarding clarity and completeness within the application patent specification.

An allow application patent, as defined herein, signifies an instance where the Controller, acting under this Act, permits modifications to a pending patent application beyond those initially presented. Such permission may encompass alterations to the claims, description, or drawings of the invention. The request for an allow application patent shall be made in writing and accompanied by reasoned justification demonstrating that the proposed changes do not substantially alter the nature of the originally claimed invention. Further, any amendment sought under this provision must remain consistent with the disclosure described within the original specification; provided that such consistency is determined at the Controller’s discretion.

An application for a patent may be filed with the Registrar in the prescribed form and manner, detailing the invention and claiming its novelty and utility. The applicant shall furnish particulars regarding prior publication or use of the invention anywhere in the world. Upon receipt of an allow application patent, the Registrar shall acknowledge the same and initiate examination under this Act. Any person may file a representation with the Registrar objecting to the grant of a patent on grounds specified herein, including lack of novelty or inventive step. The Registrar shall provide the applicant and objector opportunities for reasoned argument and submission of evidence. A notice of such objections shall be published in the Patent Journal as provided herein.

An aggrieved party alleging infringement of a patent granted under this Act may institute suit in the competent civil court seeking an injunction restraining the infringing activity and damages commensurate with the loss suffered. Such damages shall be determined having regard to the prevailing market price of the patented article or process, as well as any profits derived by the infringer from the unauthorized use thereof. The Controller may, upon receiving a representation that a patent has been granted in error based on a material misstatement of fact or suppression of relevant information, direct the rectification of the register and revocation of the allow application patent. Further, where an injunction is refused under this Act, the party seeking it shall be entitled to costs proportionate to the work undertaken.

An application for a patent may be refused under this Act if it does not disclose or describe the invention in a manner clear and complete enough for a person skilled in the art to put the same into practice. Where an objection is taken on the ground that the invention lacks clarity, the applicant shall have the opportunity to address such concerns through written submissions and supporting documentation. The Controller may require the applicant to furnish further information or clarification regarding the claimed subject matter. Further, any amendment proposed by the applicant during the examination of the patent application shall be strictly confined to the disclosure as originally filed; substantial additions beyond the scope of the initial description are impermissible. A grant of an allow application patent is contingent upon satisfying all procedural and substantive requirements outlined herein.

An application for a patent shall be deemed to disclose and fairly describe the invention in respect of which it has been made, provided that the description contains sufficient particulars to enable a person skilled in the art or technology to make and use the invention. Where an applicant seeks to obtain an allow application patent relating to a process by which a substance is produced, such application must clearly state whether the process is applicable to substances already known or to new substances. The Controller may require the applicant to furnish further information concerning the working of the process if deemed necessary for proper assessment under this Act. Any alteration made to the invention during prosecution shall be consistent with the original disclosure and subject to compliance with prescribed guidelines.

An application for a patent shall be deemed invalid where it is established, through civil suit in the appropriate jurisdictional court, that the invention was previously known or used within India, notwithstanding the applicant’s good faith belief in its novelty. Any party aggrieved by the grant of an allow application patent may petition the High Court seeking revocation, presenting evidence demonstrating prior public knowledge undermining the inventive step. Failure to provide verifiable documentary proof substantiating claims of prior use shall render the petitioner liable for costs incurred by the patentee in defending the action. The Controller may issue interim injunctions preventing exploitation of a patent pending judicial determination under this Act, subject to conditions as deemed just and equitable.

Subject to the provisions of this Act and the regulations framed thereunder, an applicant for a patent may grant a non-exclusive license in respect of the invention claimed in the allow application patent to any person, provided that such grant is made prior to the sealing of the patent. The terms and conditions of such license shall be recorded in writing and filed with the Controller within thirty days of the grant, detailing the royalty rate and duration of the license. Further, a patentee may assign their entire interest in the allow application patent, including any licenses granted therein, to another party by way of an instrument in writing, duly executed. Such assignment shall be recorded with the Controller as provided herein, and shall become effective only upon such recording. The Controller may require further documentation demonstrating due diligence regarding the proposed licensee’s capacity to exploit the invention commercially.

An application for a patent shall be deemed invalid where it is demonstrated, through evidence presented before the relevant authority, that the invention was previously described in a publication accessible to the public prior to the date of filing. However, such demonstration does not automatically render the application void; the applicant may present arguments establishing grounds for an allow application patent based on novelty or inventive step despite the cited publication. The Controller shall consider whether the disclosure in the publication sufficiently discloses all elements necessary to enable a person skilled in the art to practice the invention. Any party aggrieved by the Controller's decision concerning validity may appeal under this Act to the Appellate Board, presenting reasoned arguments and supporting documentation.

An application for a patent may be filed with the Registrar in the prescribed form and manner, disclosing the invention clearly and completely for which protection is sought. The applicant shall furnish particulars relating to priority, if applicable, and pay the requisite fees as determined under this Act. Upon receipt of an application, the Registrar shall acknowledge its receipt and assign it a serial number. A patent shall be granted only upon satisfying the criteria stipulated herein, including novelty and non-obviousness. An allow application patent is deemed to have been registered when the grant of the patent has been sealed by the Controller. Cancellation justified registration may be sought by any interested person demonstrating that the invention was not new or was obvious at the time of filing.

An aggrieved party claiming damages arising from the infringement of an allow application patent shall institute a suit in a District Court having jurisdiction over the place where the infringement occurred or where the defendant resides or carries on business. The applicant for such patent, upon demonstrating to the satisfaction of the court that the infringing activity has caused demonstrable financial loss, may be awarded compensation commensurate with the extent of said loss, including lost profits and reasonable costs incurred in pursuing remedies under this Act. However, a claim predicated on an application section 35 objection relating to prior use or publication shall not be entertained unless it is established that the applicant had knowledge of such prior use or publication at the time of filing the patent application. The court may grant interim injunctions restraining further acts of infringement pending final determination of the suit, provided that sufficient cause is shown.

An allow application patent may be granted where the invention relates to a process for producing a substance and involves one or more steps; provided that the applicant demonstrates, under this Act, that the process is novel and non-obvious. The patent shall entered into the Register only if the description of the invention clearly and completely discloses the manner in which it may be performed, enabling any person skilled in the art to practice it. Further, where an application includes a claim referring to drawings, such drawings must conform to prescribed standards for clarity and accuracy; otherwise, the application shall be deemed deficient. Subject to compliance with these requirements, and after due consideration of all objections raised during examination, the Controller may proceed with grant.

An application for registration of a design may be amended by the applicant at any time prior to its publication under this Act, provided that the proposed amendment does not substantially alter the industrial applicability or novelty of the registered design. Where an amendment is sought after publication but before registration, the Registrar shall issue a notice requiring objections to be filed within three months. Any person may file such objection, stating reasons for opposing the amendment. The Controller may allow the application to proceed with the amendment if satisfied that it does not prejudice existing rights or unfairly impact prior users; however, an *application amend* shall not introduce matter which is essentially new and was not disclosed in the original design specification.

An applicant seeking to pursue an amendment of their patent application under this Act shall provide a written request detailing the proposed alterations and demonstrating their conformity with existing legal precedent. The Controller may permit such an *application amend* provided that the changes do not substantially alter the nature of the invention as originally claimed, nor introduce matter which extends beyond the scope of the prior disclosure. Any party adversely affected by the grant of a patent following amendment may petition the Controller within six months from the date of publication of the acceptance order seeking revocation or modification based on grounds of novelty or inventive step deficiency arising directly from the amended claims. The Controller shall afford all such parties an opportunity for hearing before rendering any decision concerning the validity of the patent.

An applicant seeking to obtain a patent under this Act may submit an application for amendment of the patent application at any time before the grant of the patent or during pending opposition proceedings. Such application shall be in the prescribed form and accompanied by the requisite fee, as determined by notification issued by the Central Government. The Controller shall consider such applications, subject to the condition that the proposed amendments do not substantially alter the scope of protection initially sought. Any amendment requested must relate only to matters of clarification or detail and cannot introduce new matter which was not disclosed in the original specification. The Controller may require the applicant to furnish further particulars or explanations supporting the request for an application amend, and shall provide a reasoned order detailing any decision regarding acceptance or rejection.

An applicant seeking to effect an amendment to a patent application under this Act shall submit a request in writing detailing the proposed modifications. Such request must demonstrate that the intended changes do not substantially alter the scope of protection initially sought and remain within the bounds of what would have been originally allowable had the applicant foreseen the need for such adjustment. The Controller may, after affording an opportunity to all interested parties to raise objections, permit the application amend if satisfied that the proposed alterations are merely clarificatory or reconciliatory in nature. Any amendment introduced subsequent to the first instance of publication shall be subject to a fee as prescribed and may only be allowed where such alteration does not introduce new matter which could reasonably have been included in the original specification.

An applicant seeking to effect an amendment to a patent application after its publication shall file a request with the Controller specifying the nature of the proposed alteration. Such amendment shall only be permissible if it does not substantially alter the scope of protection sought and is supported by the original disclosure, subject to exceptions determined by the Controller. Failure to adhere to this requirement will render the amendment void ab initio. The Controller may impose a monetary penalty, recoverable as a debt due to the government, upon any applicant found to have deliberately misrepresented facts in support of an application amend request. Any appeal against such determination shall be made within sixty days and is subject to a further fine for delayed filing.

Where an application for a patent has been granted and subsequently assigned or licensed under this Act, the assignee or licensee may, with the consent of the assignor or licensor respectively, file a request to amend the said application. Such amendment shall be permissible only if it does not substantially alter the scope of protection initially sought in respect of the invention as described in the original specification and claims. The Controller shall consider any such request for an application amend taking into account the impact on existing licensees or assignees, ensuring that no undue prejudice arises from the alteration. Further, where a license agreement contains provisions regarding further patent applications based on the licensed technology, the amendment process shall be conducted in accordance with those contractual obligations, subject to compliance with all other requirements under this Act.

An amendment to a patent application, whether made before or after its publication under this Act, shall only be allowed where such amendment is necessary for ensuring clarity and operability of the invention claimed; however, an applicant may seek to amend the specification to include matter which does not originally exist therein. Any party aggrieved by an order refusing an application amend may appeal to the Appellate Board within sixty days from the date of receipt of the order. The Board shall consider whether the proposed amendment substantially alters the scope of protection sought or introduces a new invention, and its decision shall be final subject to further appeal under the provisions relating to appeals to the Supreme Court.

An applicant seeking a patent shall be entitled to file an amendment to their application at any time before the first examination report is issued by the Patent Office Central, provided that such amendment does not alter the nature of the invention claimed. Any proposed alteration must be clearly identified and supported by reasoned argument demonstrating its consistency with the original disclosure. The Controller may allow or reject any proposed amendment; rejection shall be accompanied by written reasons. Where an application amend is rejected, the applicant may appeal to the Appellate Board under this Act within sixty days from the date of receipt of the order. Further, no amendment shall be permitted that introduces matter not disclosed in the original specification unless such introduction is permissible as a clarification or explanation thereof.

An applicant seeking to obtain a patent under this Act may submit an application amend, provided that such amendment does not alter the nature of the invention disclosed in the original application. The Patent Office shall consider any proposed amendment only if it is made within six months from the first date on which the application was notified for objections or deemed to be refused, whichever occurs earlier. Further, the amended portion must still satisfy all requirements for patentability as provided herein; specifically, novelty and non-obviousness relative to the prior art existing at the date of filing. The Patent Office shall issue a notification regarding acceptance or rejection of the amendment within three months from receipt thereof.

An assignment of patent rights under this Act shall remain valid notwithstanding any subsequent amendment to the original application. Where an applicant seeks to amend a patent application after the grant of a license relating thereto, such amendment must explicitly address and detail the impact on existing licensee rights as provided herein. The Registrar shall decide whether the proposed amendment materially alters the scope or subject matter of the invention as originally claimed, taking into consideration any contractual obligations arising from prior assignments or licenses. Any party with a vested interest in the patent, including licensees and assignees, may submit objections to the proposed amendment within sixty days of its publication. The Registrar shall provide an opportunity for such parties to be heard before rendering a decision regarding the application amend.

An applicant seeking to amend an application for patent may do so only with the prior written consent of the Controller and after providing a copy of the proposed amendment to all other parties involved in related proceedings under this Act. Such amendment shall be permissible solely if it does not substantially alter the scope of protection initially sought, as determined by the Controller’s assessment at the time of the original application's filing date. Failure to adhere to these procedural requirements renders the amended application void ab initio. Any party aggrieved by a decision allowing or refusing an application amend may appeal under this Act to the Appellate Board within sixty days from the date of such order, and notice rectification shall be afforded to all concerned during the appellate process.

Where a patentee seeks to enforce rights conferred under this Act against an infringement, the patentee shall be entitled to seek remedies including, but not limited to, injunctions restraining the infringing party from further acts of infringement and damages reflecting reasonable compensation for the loss suffered by the patentee as a consequence thereof. The amount of damages may include lost profits attributable to the infringement, a reasonable royalty, and costs reasonably incurred in prosecuting the action. Subject to an appeal under this Act, any order granting or refusing such remedies shall be final. A person aggrieved by an order made under this Act relating to enforcement proceedings may apply for redressal before the relevant judicial forum as provided herein. The patentee allow application for review of a decision concerning infringement remains open where demonstrable errors of fact or law are presented.

An application for a patent may be allowed by the Controller where the applicant demonstrates compliance with all requirements under this Act. The Controller shall examine whether the invention claimed in the patent application is novel and involves an inventive step, considering prior publications and the state of knowledge as it existed at the date of filing. Where deficiencies are identified during examination, the Controller shall issue a communication to the applicant outlining these concerns and providing an opportunity for response. Following such response, the Controller may require further clarification or amendment of claims. The patentee allow application process is subject to limitations; amendments cannot substantially alter the nature of the invention as originally disclosed. Any decision regarding allowance or rejection remains at the discretion of the Controller, guided by principles of fairness and adherence to established legal precedent.

Where an invention relates to a process for producing a substance controlled under regulations framed by the Central Government, the application for patent may proceed only if the applicant furnishes evidence demonstrating compliance with all applicable regulatory requirements pertaining to manufacture and distribution. Such evidence must be current at the time of grant and remain valid throughout the term of the patent. The Controller shall scrutinize this documentation diligently before proceeding; failure to provide adequate proof will result in rejection of the application. Further, a patentee allow application for an extension of the patent term may be considered if unforeseen delays due to regulatory approvals have demonstrably impacted commercial exploitation, subject to demonstrating substantial investment made post-grant.

Any person aggrieved by an order made under this Act may appeal to the Appellate Board within sixty days from the date of receipt of the order. The Appellate Board shall hear appeals against orders refusing a patentee allow application for rectification of the patent, or revoking a patent, and may confirm, vary, or reverse the order appealed from. Failure to comply with the prescribed procedures during an appeal shall render it inadmissible. Where a party fails to appear before the Appellate Board at any hearing appointed by that board, the board may proceed in absentia and its decision shall be binding on all parties. Costs of the appeal shall be determined as provided herein, subject to judicial review under appropriate law.

Where a patentee desires to grant a license in respect of the invention claimed in a patent, or to assign the entire interest in such patent, they shall submit an application to the Controller for approval. Such application must detail the terms and conditions proposed for the license or assignment, including royalty rates, duration, and geographical scope. The Controller may require further information or clarification regarding these details before proceeding. A licensee, upon receiving a license under this Act, shall be entitled to exercise the patentee’s rights to the extent specified in the approved agreement. However, any modification of the terms after approval requires fresh application and consent from the Controller. The patentee allow application process ensures transparency and safeguards the interests of both the patent holder and potential licensees or assignees as provided herein.

Where an objection is taken against a patent application under this Act concerning novelty or inventive step, the applicant may, within sixty days from the date of communication of said objection, submit a written response addressing the grounds raised. The Controller shall consider such response and may afford the examiner opportunity to file a rejoinder thereto. Following consideration of all submissions, if the Controller finds that the original objection remains unsubstantiated or has been adequately overcome, he shall direct acceptance of the patent application. However, any party aggrieved by this direction may appeal to the Appellate Board within sixty days, demonstrating prejudice arising from the Controller’s decision; and the Board's determination shall be final, subject to further appeal under the relevant provisions. The patentee allow application is a right exercisable in good faith.

An amendment specification, when submitted under this Act, shall relate only to matters disclosed in the original application or arising directly from it. Such an amendment may clarify any aspect of the invention described within the initial disclosure but cannot introduce new subject matter beyond the scope initially claimed. The Controller shall permit amendments provided that they do not substantially alter the nature of the invention as originally conceived and described, nor broaden the claims to encompass elements not previously indicated. Any alteration impacting the clarity or completeness of the specification requires prior approval from the Controller, ensuring adherence to standards prescribed herein for patentability.

An application for registration of a utility model may include an amendment specification relating to the matter disclosed in the original application, subject to the provisions herein. Such amendment shall be limited to clarifying or correcting descriptions, drawings, or claims; it shall not substantively alter the inventive concept underlying the utility model as initially presented. The Controller General shall require detailed justification for any proposed amendment, including a statement affirming its consistency with the disclosure in the initial application and demonstrating that the amended specification remains within the scope of what is considered obvious to a person skilled in the art. Any amendment affecting the essential features of the invention must be accompanied by the prescribed fee as determined under this Act.

Where an applicant seeks to introduce alterations to a patent application beyond those permissible under this Act relating to clerical errors or minor clarifications, such request constitutes an amendment specification. The Controller may allow an amendment specification only if it does not substantially alter the nature of the invention claimed and is consistent with the disclosure contained within the original complete specification as filed. Any party aggrieved by a decision granting or refusing an amendment specification may appeal to the Appellate Board under this Act. Failure to provide adequate written justification for the proposed amendments, demonstrating their relevance to the originally disclosed invention, shall be grounds for refusal. The Controller’s order regarding such refusals is final, subject to appeal as provided herein, and remedies are available only through that appellate process.

An application for patent protection may include an amendment specification relating to any matter disclosed in the original complete specification, subject to the provisions herein. Such amendments shall only be permissible if they clarify or explain aspects already described within the initial disclosure and do not introduce new inventive concepts beyond the scope of the originally filed document. The Controller shall scrutinize all proposed amendments with particular regard to whether they substantially alter the claimed invention’s nature. An applicant seeking to incorporate an amendment specification must submit a formal request, accompanied by a reasoned justification detailing its necessity for clarity or accuracy. This request will be considered by the examining officer and may be referred to a designated expert for technical assessment. The Controller's decision regarding acceptance or rejection of such amendments shall be final, provided that it is communicated in writing with reasons recorded.

An applicant seeking to introduce an amendment specification under this Act shall submit a request in writing detailing the proposed modifications. Such request must clearly identify the specific clauses or figures within the original specification affected by the intended alteration. The Controller may permit such amendments only if they do not substantially alter the nature of the invention as originally claimed, nor broaden the scope of protection sought beyond that disclosed in the initial complete specification. Further, any amendment shall be consistent with the disclosure contained within the accompanying claims and drawings. A request for an amendment specification shall include a declaration by the applicant affirming compliance with these conditions and attesting to the accuracy of the proposed changes.

Any person aggrieved by an order relating to the rejection of an application for patent or the revocation of a patent may appeal to the Appellate Board within sixty days from the date of such order. Failure to comply with prescribed procedural requirements during appellate proceedings shall render the appeal inadmissible, subject to the discretion of the Board. Where a patent has been granted based on an amendment specification not disclosed in the original application, and it is subsequently determined that said amendment substantially alters the scope of the invention, the Controller may initiate revocation proceedings under this Act. Any party affected by such revocation may then pursue remedies available for wrongful deprivation, including claims for damages and injunctive relief as provided herein.

Subject to the provisions of this Act, any patentee desiring to grant an exclusive license or assign the entire interest in a patent relating to a process or composition for producing a substance defined in the claim may execute a written instrument specifying the terms and conditions thereof. Such amendment specification shall clearly delineate the scope of the licensed rights, including territory, duration, and fields of use. The instrument must also detail any royalties or other consideration payable by the licensee to the patentee as provided herein. Failure to adequately define these parameters within the amendment specification may render the license unenforceable under this Act. Further, a subsequent assignee shall be bound by all terms stipulated in the original amendment specification relating to such licensing arrangements.

Where an applicant seeks to introduce alterations to a patent application beyond those permissible under this Act relating to clerical errors or matters of record, such proposed modifications constitute an amendment specification. The Controller may allow such amendment specification only if it does not alter the nature of the invention claimed and is supported by the original disclosure; however, any party aggrieved by the acceptance or rejection of an amendment specification may appeal to the Appellate Board within sixty days from the date of communication of the order. It shall be incumbent upon the appellant to demonstrate that the Controller’s decision was manifestly erroneous in law or fact, failing which the appeal shall stand dismissed with costs.

Any alteration to an amendment specification submitted under this Act shall be deemed invalid if it materially broadens the scope of protection sought or introduces subject matter not previously disclosed. Such invalidation may occur at any stage during examination or opposition proceedings and shall render the patent liable for revocation. Where a person is found to have knowingly induced such an unlawful alteration, they shall be guilty of an offence punishable with imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years, alongside a fine not exceeding five hundred thousand rupees. The Controller may, subject to provisions sub section (2), issue directions requiring the rectification of any amendment specification deemed in violation of this clause and impose costs proportionate to the offending party's actions.

Where an invention relates to a process for producing a substance controlled under this Act, the patentee may grant a non-exclusive license to manufacture such substance in an authorised prescribed manner. Such licenses shall be assignable and transferable subject to registration with the Controller. The terms of any amendment specification relating to the licensed process, including but not limited to variations in feedstock or reaction conditions, must be disclosed to all licensees prior to approval by the Controller. Failure to provide this information constitutes a breach of the patentee’s obligations under this Act. Further, any subsequent assignment of the patent shall include an undertaking that the assignee will continue to adhere to the previously notified amendment specification and maintain transparency with existing licensees. The Controller may issue directions regarding the equitable distribution of benefits arising from such licensed processes.

Where an applicant seeks to introduce alterations to a patent application beyond those permissible under this Act relating to clerical errors or typographical omissions, such proposed changes constitute an amendment specification. The Controller may allow such amendment only if he is satisfied that the amended matter does not substantially alter the nature of the invention claimed and maintains consistency with the originally disclosed subject matter. Any party aggrieved by the decision of the Controller regarding the acceptance or rejection of an amendment specification may appeal to the Appellate Board within sixty days from the date of communication of the order. The appellate board shall consider whether the controller acted reasonably in interpreting the scope of permissible amendments, taking into account prevailing standards of patentability as provided herein.

An application for patent protection may include an amendment specification relating to the claimed invention, subject to verification by the Controller. Such amendments must clearly articulate the modifications made to the original disclosure and demonstrate their consistency with the prior art search report. The applicant shall furnish a detailed statement outlining the rationale behind each alteration proposed within the amendment specification, along with supporting technical data where applicable. Furthermore, any published expiry period relating to an invention undergoing amendment shall be recalculated from the date of filing the amended application, provided that the Controller deems the amendments material and impacting novelty. This recalculation will be reflected in the patent grant documentation.

Where an application for patent contains any deficiency in respect of clarity or completeness of the disclosure relating to the invention, the Controller may require the applicant to submit within such time as may be specified, an amendment specification. Such amendment specification shall not extend beyond the matter disclosed in the original application and known at the date of filing thereof, subject to provisions regarding obviousness. Any person aggrieved by a decision requiring submission of an amendment specification may appeal to the Appellate Board. Further, where any false representation is made in the amendment specification with intent to deceive or mislead, such person shall be liable for prosecution under relevant sections of the Indian Penal Code, and the patent granted on the basis of that application may be deemed invalid.

An application for a patent may include one or more amendment specifications documents relating to the invention described therein. For the purposes of this Act, an “amendment specification document” means any written material submitted by the applicant after the date of filing the original complete specification, and which purports to clarify, correct, or add to the disclosure contained within said original complete specification. Such amendment specification documents shall be construed strictly in accordance with the principles governing patentable subject matter as provided herein. The Controller may allow an amendment specification document only if it does not substantially alter the nature of the invention originally claimed and is consistent with the prior art.

An application for registration of a utility model shall include with it a detailed set of amendment specification documents pertaining to any modifications made to the originally submitted design. These documents must clearly delineate each alteration from the initial submission and provide justification for such changes, referencing relevant technical data or experimental results where applicable. The Controller may require further clarification or supplementary materials regarding these amendment specification documents if deemed necessary for proper assessment under this Act. Any applicant seeking to incorporate revisions through amendment specification documents shall file an affidavit confirming the accuracy of the information presented therein. Failure to adhere to prescribed formats and submission protocols relating to amendment specification documents will render the application liable for rejection.

Where an applicant seeks to introduce modifications to a patent application beyond those permissible under this Act relating to clerical errors or obvious matters, such alterations must be presented through formally designated amendment specification documents. These documents shall clearly articulate the nature and extent of the proposed changes, accompanied by a reasoned justification demonstrating their consistency with the originally claimed invention and adherence to principles of novelty and inventive step as provided herein. Failure to adequately justify an amendment specification document may result in its rejection by the Controller. Any party aggrieved by a decision regarding an amendment specification document may appeal under this Act to the Appellate Board, seeking review based on demonstrable prejudice arising from the Controller's determination. The burden of proving such prejudice rests solely with the appellant.

An applicant seeking to amend a patent application after publication may submit an amendment specification document detailing the proposed alterations. Such documents must be filed with the Controller within three months from the date of the first publication of the application, subject to extensions granted under this Act based on demonstrable cause. The amendment specification document shall clearly identify the sections of the original complete specification being modified and provide a precise statement of the intended changes. Any alteration introduced through an amendment specification document must not substantially alter the nature of the invention as originally claimed. The Controller may require supporting data or expert opinions to verify the technical feasibility of any modification proposed in the amendment specification document, particularly if it relates to previously undisclosed matter. Decisions regarding acceptance or rejection of amendment specification documents are appealable before the Appellate Board.

Subject to the provisions of this Act, any patentee desiring to assign or license an interest in a patent, or in any invention disclosed in the patent’s amendment specification documents, shall execute an instrument in writing specifying the extent and nature of the assignment or license. Such instrument may be executed as a deed, and where it is so executed, it shall be attested by at least two witnesses. The assignor or licensor shall provide a certified copy of the relevant amendment specification document to the assignee or licensee, detailing the scope of the invention being transferred. Further, any subsequent modification or addition to said amendment specification documents, whether relating to claims or descriptions, shall similarly require written consent from all parties holding an interest under the initial assignment or license agreement as provided herein. Failure to obtain such consent may render the amended patent unenforceable against those original stakeholders.

Where an applicant seeks to introduce modifications to a patent application beyond those permissible under this Act, such proposed alterations must be submitted in the form of detailed amendment specification documents. These documents shall clearly articulate the nature and extent of the intended changes relative to the originally filed description and claims. The Controller may permit incorporation of these amendments only if satisfied that they do not substantially alter the inventive concept disclosed; otherwise, an objection shall be recorded, accompanied by reasoned justification for rejection. Any aggrieved party may appeal such a decision before the Appellate Board, demonstrating how the amendment remains consistent with the disclosure as originally presented and does not broaden the scope of protection sought beyond what was reasonably anticipated.

Any assignment or license granted in respect of a patent under this Act shall include, by implication, the right to assign or license any amendment specification documents relating thereto, whether filed before or after the date of such initial grant. The Controller may require submission of detailed records pertaining to all modifications made to the original complete specification, including digital backups and revision histories, as evidence supporting a claim of ownership under an assignment. Provided that, where registration is sought for an invention incorporating technology previously subject to a conflicting patent, the assignor shall provide a declaration confirming due diligence in assessing prior art searches relevant to the amendment specification documents. Further, any party seeking to initiate procedure cancelling registration based on grounds of non-disclosure within the amendment specification documents must demonstrate clear prejudice resulting from such omission.

Where an applicant seeks to introduce alterations to a patent application beyond those permissible under this Act concerning matters of form or minor clarification, such proposed changes must constitute a substantive amendment specification document. The Controller may allow such amendments only if satisfied that the original disclosure, read in light of the amended portions, would still satisfy the requirements for patentability as provided herein. Any design agent person acting on behalf of an applicant shall be held jointly and severally liable for any misrepresentation or fraudulent inclusion within said amendment specification documents. An aggrieved party may appeal to the Appellate Board if they contend that a permitted amendment substantially alters the scope of protection originally sought, thereby unfairly impacting their existing rights.

An application for patent registration shall include a complete specification describing the invention and setting forth the best mode contemplated by the applicant for carrying out the invention. For the purposes of this Act, an "amendment specification document" is defined as any written material submitted to the Controller after the initial filing date of the application, which alters or clarifies aspects of the original complete specification. Such amendment specification documents may include drawings, claims, or descriptions relating to the invention. The acceptance of an amendment specification document shall be subject to the condition that it does not alter the nature of the invention as originally disclosed and is consistent with the information provided during the application registration process.

Where an application for patent is granted, any subsequent modification to the original invention disclosed in the complete specification, or within related amendment specification documents filed during prosecution, shall require leave of the Controller. Such leave may only be granted if the applicant demonstrates that the proposed alteration does not substantially depart from the matter originally disclosed and claimed, and that it remains novel and inventive under this Act. Failure to obtain such leave will render any patent subsequently enforced liable to revocation proceedings initiated by an aggrieved party. Upon expiration registration of a patent, amendment specification documents previously filed shall be deemed public record and accessible for inspection, subject to restrictions protecting trade secrets as provided herein. The Controller may issue directions regarding the form and content of these documents to ensure clarity and prevent frivolous challenges.

An application for patent protection may include one or more claims defining the scope of the invention; however, subject to this Act, any claim specification amendment sought after the initial filing date shall only be permissible if it does not alter the inventive concept disclosed in the original complete specification. Such amendments are allowable solely to clarify language or correct minor errors that do not broaden the protection initially sought. A request for a claim specification amendment must explicitly state the basis for its necessity and demonstrate how it remains consistent with the disclosure contained within the originally filed documents, as provided herein.

An applicant seeking to amend a patent claim after the first examination but before the grant of a patent shall provide a written request detailing the proposed modification. Such requests are subject to review by the Controller and may only proceed if they do not substantially alter the nature of the invention originally disclosed. The Controller shall issue a notice to any interested party, affording them an opportunity to object to the claim specification amendment within sixty days. Objections must be supported by reasoned argument demonstrating that the proposed change introduces new matter or unfairly broadens the scope of protection sought under this Act. Failure to adequately address such objections may result in rejection of the amendment request and potential forfeiture of patent rights. The applicant shall bear the burden of proving the permissible nature of any alteration, provided that the original disclosure remains substantially intact.

An applicant seeking to amend a patent claim after the first examination but prior to grant shall file a request with the Controller specifying the proposed alteration. Such request must clearly articulate the basis for the amendment, demonstrating its consistency with the originally filed disclosure and adherence to principles of inventive step. The Controller may permit such an amendment if it is satisfied that the amended claim clarifies the scope of protection sought and does not broaden the subject matter beyond what was adequately described in the original complete specification. Any proposed claim specification amendment shall be accompanied by a reasoned statement addressing any potential impact on prior art or existing patent rights, as provided herein. The Controller’s decision regarding an amendment is final, subject to appeal under this Act. Further, no amendment shall be allowed that introduces new matter not implicit within the original disclosure.

An applicant seeking to amend a patent claim specification after the first examination shall file an application with the Controller detailing the proposed modifications. Such amendments are permissible only if they do not substantially alter the nature of the invention as originally disclosed and subject to verification by the Controller regarding novelty and inventive step. Failure to demonstrate compliance with these requirements will result in rejection of the amendment request, accompanied by a penalty of twenty thousand rupees for frivolous applications. Repeated or wilful attempts to circumvent established procedures relating to claim specification amendment may attract further penalties up to one hundred thousand rupees and potential revocation of pending patent applications as provided herein. The Controller’s decision on any such application is final, subject to appeal under this Act.

Where an invention is patented under this Act, the patentee shall retain exclusive rights subject to any licenses granted or assignments made prior to or subsequent to the grant of the patent. Any modification to the claim specification within a patent application, constituting a claim specification amendment, may be undertaken with the consent of all parties holding a vested interest in the invention’s commercialization, including licensees and assignees. Such consent shall be documented in writing and filed with the Controller. The Controller may permit a claim specification amendment if it does not substantially alter the scope of protection originally sought and is consistent with the disclosure contained within the complete specification. Further, any assignment or license agreement referencing a patent subject to a claim specification amendment shall be deemed amended concurrently to reflect the revised claims, provided that all assignees and licensees provide written acknowledgement of this modification.

An applicant seeking to amend a claim specification after the first examination under this Act shall file a request accompanied by a reasoned justification demonstrating the necessity of such alteration. The Controller may allow or reject the proposed amendment subject to the condition that it does not substantially alter the nature of the invention disclosed in the original application as initially presented. Any party aggrieved by an order allowing or rejecting a claim specification amendment may, within sixty days from the date of communication of said order, prefer an appeal to the Appellate Board. The Board shall consider whether the proposed amendment unfairly prejudices the interests of other parties and if so, may direct the Controller to reconsider the matter.

Where an application for patent protection is published under this Act, any person considering himself aggrieved by such publication may, subject to conditions as provided herein, file a notice of opposition with the Controller within three months from the date of such publication. Such notice shall specify the grounds upon which the opposition is based and must be supported by a duly verified statement. Failure to comply with these requirements renders the opposition invalid and without effect. The applicant for patent protection shall have the right to respond to the opposition, presenting counter-arguments and evidence in his favour. Any person found to have acted in bad faith during an application notice opposition proceeding shall be liable to a penalty as determined by the Controller.

Where an application for patent protection is published under this Act, any person possessing knowledge or reason to believe that the invention claimed therein does not fulfill the criteria for patentability as provided herein may, subject to fulfilling procedural requirements, file a notice of opposition with the Controller within the prescribed period following publication. Such notice shall clearly specify the grounds upon which the opposition is based and provide supporting documentation. The applicant shall then be afforded an opportunity to respond to the opposition in writing. Following consideration of both submissions, the Controller may direct a hearing where parties may present oral arguments. Any party aggrieved by the Controller's decision on an application notice opposition may appeal to the relevant appellate authority within the time stipulated under this Act.

The patent office register shall comprise a publicly accessible record maintained by the Controller General, detailing all applications for patents filed under this Act. This register shall include, but not be limited to, information pertaining to the applicant’s name and address, the title of the invention, the date of filing, and the status of examination as provided herein. Any modification to an application's claims or specifications shall also be recorded within the patent office register. Further, details concerning any opposition proceedings initiated against a granted patent, including the identity of the opponent and the grounds for objection, must be meticulously documented subject to rules framed by the Central Government.

The Controller shall maintain a comprehensive register of designs at each patent office, accessible for public inspection during normal business hours. This register shall include details pertaining to registered designs, encompassing the name and address of the proprietor, the title of the design, the date of registration, and particulars concerning any modifications or alterations made subsequent to initial entry. Any request for rectification of entries in the register relating to ownership or specifications must be submitted in writing to the Controller, accompanied by supporting documentation as deemed necessary under this Act. The patent office register shall serve as prima facie evidence of the proprietorship and validity of a registered design, subject to any challenge initiated through due process as provided herein.

Any person aggrieved by any entry in the patent office register relating to a patent shall have the right to appeal to the Controller within sixty days from the date on which such entry was made. The appeal shall lie on grounds alleging errors appearing on the face of the record or demonstrating material prejudice resulting from the decision under review. Subject to payment of prescribed fees, the Controller may entertain appeals and shall afford both the appellant and the patentee a reasonable opportunity for being heard. Where an appeal is successful, the Controller shall direct rectification of the register as deemed appropriate. Provided that any order made by the Controller in disposing of such an appeal shall be final, subject to further appeal under this Act to the Intellectual Property Appellate Board.

The Controller shall maintain a public register accessible for inspection during normal business hours, containing details pertaining to applications for patents and granted patents under this Act. Such register shall include, but not be limited to, the applicant’s name and address, the title of the invention, the date of filing, any priority claims asserted, and the grant or refusal decision rendered by the patent office register. The Controller may, upon application by an interested party and subject to procedural safeguards as provided herein, correct errors or omissions in entries within the public register. Any person aggrieved by a false or misleading entry shall have recourse to appeal under this Act. Information pertaining to trade secrets disclosed during examination proceedings will be treated with due confidentiality, consistent with the interests of fairness and transparency. The Controller is empowered to prescribe forms and procedures for accessing and amending information contained in the patent office register.

An applicant seeking entry of a patent onto the patent office register shall submit with the request a certified copy of the complete specification, including all claims, accompanied by a declaration verifying the accuracy and completeness of the information provided. The Controller General may require further clarification regarding any aspect of the invention described within the specification prior to acceptance for registration. Subject to compliance with prescribed forms and payment of requisite fees, the patent office register shall reflect the date of application, inventor’s name, title of the invention, and the status of examination as determined by the examining body. Provided that an appeal against a decision regarding registrability is filed within the stipulated timeframe under this Act, the entry on the patent office register remains provisional pending resolution of said appeal.

Any person aggrieved by an entry in the patent office register relating to a patent shall have the right to appeal to the Controller within ninety days from the date on which such entry was made. The Controller may, after giving notice to all concerned and affording them an opportunity of being heard, direct that any erroneous or unwarranted entry be erased or amended. Failure to comply with a direction under this Act shall render the defaulting party liable to a penalty not exceeding fifty thousand rupees, recoverable as civil debt. Further, repeated or wilful disregard of such directions may result in revocation of the patent itself, subject to confirmation by the Intellectual Property Appellate Board.

Any patentee desiring to grant a licence conferring rights to utilize, manufacture, or sell any invention for which he is registered in the patent office register shall file with the Controller a notice specifying the terms and conditions of such proposed licence. Such notice must include details regarding royalty rates, duration of the license, and geographical scope. The Controller may, after providing an opportunity for objection from interested parties including prior applicants or unsuccessful patentees, record the particulars of the licence in the patent office register. Assignment of a patent, or any right pertaining thereto, shall also be notified to the Controller and recorded as provided herein. Failure to notify such assignments within three months shall render the assignment voidable at the option of the assignee. The patentee may revoke a license under this Act if the licensee defaults in fulfilling its obligations as stipulated in the registered terms.

The Controller shall maintain a public patent office register detailing all granted inventions, accessible for inspection subject to payment of prescribed fees. Any person aggrieved by an entry in the register concerning their rights relating to a patent may within sixty days from the date of such entry file an appeal before the Appellate Board. The appeal shall be accompanied by a statement of grounds and supported by any evidence deemed relevant. Provided that, if the appellant fails to demonstrate prima facie good faith in challenging the accuracy of the register’s entries, the appeal shall be summarily dismissed. Further, the Controller may, upon receiving credible information regarding manifest errors or omissions within the patent office register, initiate suo moto rectification proceedings as provided herein.

The Controller shall maintain a comprehensive patent office register, accessible for public inspection during normal business hours, detailing all inventions granted protection under this Act. Entries within the register shall include the applicant’s name, address for service, the title of the invention, and the date of grant or subsequent modifications to the patent specification as approved by the Controller. Any alteration in ownership, including assignments and transmissions, must be formally recorded on the register through a prescribed process involving verification of supporting documentation. Furthermore, any request for surrender of a patent shall also be noted within the patent office register, indicating the effective date of cessation of rights conferred under this Act, provided that such surrender is deemed to be in the public interest.

The patent office register shall contain a record of all licenses granted in respect of inventions for which patents have been secured under this Act. Such licenses shall specify the scope of permitted use, including but not limited to manufacturing, sale, and importation, and the duration thereof. Any assignment or transmission of a patent, or any license agreement entered into concerning a patented invention, must be formally recorded within the register, subject to payment of the prescribed fee. The registrar shall right such assignments and licenses upon application by the relevant parties, provided that the proposed terms do not conflict with the provisions of this Act or any rules made thereunder. Further, where a licensee seeks to sub-license rights granted under an existing patent license, notification thereof must also be recorded in the register for transparency and enforceability.

Applications for registration of patents shall be examined by the Controller, who may require the applicant to furnish further information or clarification regarding the invention described in the application. Upon receipt of a complete application, the Controller shall initiate an examination to determine patentability, considering novelty, inventive step, and industrial applicability as provided herein. The Controller is empowered to direct the publication of a notice inviting representations from third parties concerning the claimed invention. Any party aggrieved by such publication may file objections within a prescribed period. Following consideration of any objections received, the Controller shall decide whether to proceed with the examination or request further amendments. A provisional acceptance shall be recorded in the office register patents upon satisfaction that the invention meets the requirements for patentability.

Where a patent has been granted, the Controller may, subject to provisions regarding compulsory licensing, permit assignment or licensing of the patented invention under conditions specified in writing. Such assignments or licences shall require registration with the Patent Office and shall include details pertaining to royalty rates, duration, and territorial scope. The grant of any such license does not prejudice the right of a patentee to seek revocation of a patent granted to another party, particularly where that other patent infringes upon the licensed invention’s core functionality or constitutes an unlawful exploitation thereof. Further, any request for revocations patents particulars relating to assignments or licences must be accompanied by a sworn affidavit verifying the accuracy and completeness of the information provided. Failure to comply with these stipulations may render such requests inadmissible.

Applications for registration of inventions shall include a statement specifying the class or classes to which the invention relates, as determined by the Controller. The Register of Patents maintained under this Act shall record all amendments made to granted patents, including alterations to claims, drawings, and specifications. Such amendments shall only be entertained if they do not substantially alter the nature of the invention originally claimed. A fee proportionate to the extent of the amendment shall be prescribed for each alteration registered. Any person aggrieved by a decision regarding registration of an amendment may appeal to the Appellate Board within sixty days from the date of communication of that decision, subject to such conditions as are provided herein. The Controller may require further particulars or clarifications concerning proposed patents amendments at any stage of the process.

The Controller shall, upon receipt of a request for amendment to a patent specification from the patentee or their authorized representative, examine whether the proposed amendment is merely clarificatory in nature and does not substantially alter the invention disclosed in the original patent. Such examination shall be conducted within a period of ninety days from the date of the request’s submission. If the Controller determines that the requested amendments fall outside this scope and would effectively constitute a new invention, he may reject the amendment proposal entirely or require the applicant to file a fresh application for patent under this Act. Notice of such rejection or requirement shall be served on the applicant, providing an opportunity for them to submit written arguments within thirty days. The Controller’s decision regarding patents amendments is final, subject to appeal before the Intellectual Property Appellate Board.

Where any patent has been amended subsequent to its grant, the Controller shall ensure that a record of such amendment is maintained in the public register. This requirement applies irrespective of whether the amendment relates to the scope of protection claimed, the description of the invention, or the claims appended thereto. Any party aggrieved by an amendment may, subject to provisions under this Act concerning appeals, petition the Intellectual Property Appellate Board for review if it is demonstrated that the amendment materially alters the originally granted patent and prejudices the interests of third parties. The Controller shall not register any amendment unless satisfied that it complies with prescribed formalities and does not extend the term of protection beyond what is permissible under these patents amendments.

Any person aggrieved by a decision relating to the grant, revocation or amendment of a patent shall have the right to appeal to the Intellectual Property Appellate Tribunal within sixty days from the date of communication of that decision. The Tribunal may, after giving notice to all concerned parties and affording them an opportunity for being heard, confirm, modify, reverse or remit the decision under appeal. Failure to comply with any order issued by the Tribunal shall render the defaulting party liable to a penalty not exceeding one million rupees, recoverable as civil debt. Repeated contravention of such orders may attract further penalties up to ten thousand rupees per day until compliance is achieved. These provisions regarding patents amendments are without prejudice to any other remedies available under this Act.

Where any application for patent is amended subsequent to its publication under this Act, the Controller shall issue a notification detailing the nature of said amendment. Any person aggrieved by such amendment, or by the decision of the Controller regarding its permissibility, may within sixty days from the date of such notification file an appeal before the Intellectual Property Appellate Board. The appellate board shall consider any evidence presented by the appellant demonstrating that the amendments substantially alter the scope of the invention as originally claimed and prejudice the interests of third parties who have relied upon the published application.
