It shall be the duty of the applicant to ensure that the terms of the relationship proposed registered do not contravene any provisions under this Act, particularly those concerning fair competition and public interest. Failure to disclose such a relationship or providing false information relating thereto shall render the application liable for rejection.

Where an application for registration of a semiconductor integrated circuit layout-design is filed disclosing a relationship proposed as a registered licensee, the Registrar may require submission of a detailed memorandum outlining the terms governing such arrangement. This memorandum shall be deemed part of the public record upon registration and its contents are subject to challenge under this Act. Any party aggrieved by the disclosed terms or their impact on existing rights may appeal to the Intellectual Property Appellate Board within sixty days of publication, demonstrating prejudice arising directly from the relationship proposed registered. The Board’s determination regarding the validity of the challenged aspects shall be final, provided that it does not affect the underlying layout-design registration itself.

Where an applicant seeks registration of a semiconductor integrated circuit layout-design and demonstrates a pre-existing relationship proposed registered with another person, that other person may apply to the Registrar for recognition as a co-owner of specified rights in the design. Such application shall detail the nature of the relationship and provide evidence substantiating its existence prior to the initial application date. The applicant’s entitlement to registration is subject to the Registrar's satisfaction regarding the validity of this proposed registered relationship, including verification that it does not prejudice existing or subsequent claims under this Act. Further, where a co-owner utilizes an authorised use mark in connection with the layout-design, they shall be liable for any infringement arising from misuse of said mark, provided that such usage is expressly permitted within the agreement establishing the relationship proposed registered.

Registration of a semiconductor integrated circuit layout-design shall be deemed to have been granted improperly, and consequently, provided cancelling registration, if it is established that the layout-design incorporates elements substantially derived from a previously registered layout-design without due authorization. For the purposes of this Act, “substantially derived” means that an examination of the allegedly infringing layout-design reveals a clear and demonstrable copying of key structural or functional features, such that the original inventive concept is replicated. The Registrar may require evidence demonstrating both the prior registration and the degree of similarity to ascertain whether provided cancelling registration applies under this Act.

Registration of a semiconductor integrated circuit layout-design shall be deemed to have been granted in error, and consequently, provided cancelling registration may occur, if it is established that the layout-design was substantially similar to an already registered design under this Act. The determination of substantial similarity shall consider the overall impression created by the designs, irrespective of minor variations. An application for cancellation must specify the grounds upon which it is based and identify the prior registered design. The Registrar may require further evidence supporting the claim of substantial similarity before proceeding with a hearing concerning the validity of the design registry registration.

Registration of a semiconductor integrated circuit layout-design shall be deemed to be invalid if, following its grant, it is established that the layout-design incorporates substantial elements derived from an earlier unregistered layout-design. The Registrar may initiate proceedings for cancelling registration registered under this Act where evidence demonstrates such unauthorized appropriation. An application for cancellation may also be filed by any interested person, subject to demonstrating a direct and demonstrable prejudice resulting from the infringing incorporation. For the purposes of determining substantial similarity, consideration shall be given to both the overall impression created by the layout-design and the replication of key functional elements as provided herein.

The registration of a semiconductor integrated circuit layout-design shall remain valid for a period of ten years from the date of its initial registration, subject to renewal as provided herein. An application for renewal may be filed within one year preceding the expiry of the said period. However, the registration registered under this Act may be cancelled by the Controller if it is established that the layout-design was not originally valid or infringed upon existing rights prior to the date of application. Such cancellation may also occur if the applicant fails to pay the prescribed renewal fees within the stipulated timeframe, or demonstrates a lack of diligent prosecution of the registration. The Controller shall provide an opportunity for the registrant to be heard before issuing any order for cancelling registration registered.

Where, following registration of a semiconductor integrated circuit layout-design, it comes to the notice of the Controller that any representation made in the application for registration was materially false, the Controller shall issue a notification directing the registered proprietor to show cause why the registration should not be cancelled. Such direction shall specify the grounds upon which the cancellation is sought and provide a reasonable opportunity for the proprietor to submit their response. If, after considering the response, or if no response is received within the stipulated time, the Controller finds that the representation was indeed false and prejudicial to the interests of other persons, the registration may be cancelled as provided herein. The effect of cancelling registration registered shall be that the layout-design ceases to enjoy protection under this Act from the date of cancellation.

An application for the cancellation of a registration, whether absolute or conditional, shall be made to the Controller in the prescribed form and accompanied by the requisite fee. The grounds for such an application include demonstrable misrepresentation during the original registration process concerning the originality of the layout-design, or where it is proven that the registered layout-design incorporates substantial elements copied from a prior unregistered design. Further, a cancellation may be sought if the registered proprietor has ceased to carry on business or has become insolvent. The Controller shall provide the registered proprietor with an opportunity to be heard and present evidence in their defense. Following due consideration of all submissions, the Controller may order the registration to be cancelled, subject to providing reasons for such decision in writing. It is provided that a registration already granted cannot be unilaterally altered; cancelling registration registered requires adherence to this procedure.

The registration of a semiconductor integrated circuit layout-design shall be deemed to be vulnerable to cancellation proceedings where it is established, through evidence presented before the Controller, that the applicant knowingly misrepresented facts pertaining to prior publication or availability of the design. Such misrepresentation must be material to the assessment of novelty and originality as required under this Act. Furthermore, registration may be cancelled if it becomes apparent that the layout-design incorporates elements substantially derived from an unregistered work, and the applicant failed to acknowledge such derivation in the application. The Controller shall issue a notice to the registered proprietor prior to any order for cancelling registration registered, affording them an opportunity to submit their response and counter evidence.

Where a registration of a semiconductor integrated circuit layout-design has been granted, such registration shall remain valid subject to the provisions herein. However, the Registrar may, acting upon an application made in the prescribed form by any interested party, initiate proceedings for cancelling registration registered if it is established that the assignor had not obtained prior consent from the original registrant before assigning rights pertaining to the layout-design. Further, a licensee of a registered layout-design shall be deemed an interested party for the purpose of such application. The Registrar may also entertain applications seeking cancellation where evidence demonstrates a material alteration of the layout-design post-registration without proper notification and consent as provided herein. Any person aggrieved by an order cancelling registration registered may appeal to the Intellectual Property Appellate Tribunal within a period of sixty days from the date of communication of the order.

Registration of a semiconductor integrated circuit layout-design shall be deemed to be invalid, and consequently subject to cancellation, if it is established that the registered layout-design incorporates elements substantially derived from an earlier unregistered layout-design or design. The Registrar may initiate proceedings for cancelling registration registered where evidence demonstrates such derivation, provided that the applicant demonstrating prior creation furnishes documentation satisfying the requirements as prescribed herein. Furthermore, a registered layout-design relating to services specified alphabetically within Schedule A may be cancelled if it is found that the description of those services was inaccurate or misleading at the time of application. Any party aggrieved by a proposed cancellation order may submit objections in writing detailing grounds for dissent and supporting documentation.

Registration of a semiconductor integrated circuit layout-design shall be deemed to be voidable if, following its grant, it becomes evident that the trade description furnished during the application process was false or misleading in a material respect. The Registrar may, sua sponte or upon receiving a complaint from an aggrieved party, initiate proceedings for cancelling registration registered under this Act. Such cancellation shall only occur after providing the registrant with a reasonable opportunity to be heard and present counter-evidence. Failure by the registrant to demonstrate the veracity of the original trade description will constitute conclusive proof warranting revocation. Any person suffering loss or damage as a direct consequence of such misleading information may pursue remedies available under this Act, including claims for compensation.

The registration of a semiconductor integrated circuit layout-design shall remain valid subject to its assignment or licensing under conditions as provided herein. Any registered proprietor desiring to grant a license conferring rights in respect of the layout-design may, through an instrument executed in the prescribed form and manner, assign such rights wholly or partially, irrevocably or revocably, to another party. Provided that where a registration is subsequently cancelled, any existing licenses granted prior to the cancellation shall remain enforceable for a period not exceeding three years from the date of the order cancelling registration registered, unless a case proceeding is initiated by the former proprietor seeking their termination. The Registrar may, upon receiving notification of such assignment or licensing agreement, record the details in the Register and issue certificates accordingly. Further, any alteration to the terms of an existing license requires prior approval from the Registrar.

A registration of a layout-design shall be deemed to have been cancelled by operation of law if, following an application made in the prescribed form and supported by affidavit, it is determined that the applicant has established, to the satisfaction of the Registrar, that the original registered proprietor failed to respond to a notice served under this Act regarding objections to the registration. For the purposes of determining whether a layout-design registration constitutes a cancelled registrar layout, the date of service of such notice shall be considered conclusive evidence for establishing non-response. Any subsequent application relating to the same layout-design is barred where a cancelled registrar layout exists.

An application for registration of a semiconductor integrated circuit layout-design shall be deemed to have been abandoned if, after the publication of the acceptance thereof under this Act, the applicant fails to comply with the requirements of sub-section (3) within the prescribed time. Where a registered layout-design is subsequently found to infringe upon prior art or has been obtained through fraudulent means, the Registrar may initiate proceedings for its cancellation. In such instances, a cancelled registrar layout shall remain open to challenge by any aggrieved party before the Intellectual Property Appellate Board within a period of ninety days from the date of publication of the order of cancellation. The applicant in such challenges must demonstrate substantial prejudice resulting directly from the cancellation.

Where a registration of a semiconductor integrated circuit layout-design has been granted, the Registrar shall have the power to initiate proceedings for its cancellation if it comes to their notice that the registered proprietor has failed to comply with any condition stipulated during the registration process relating to the manufacture or importation of integrated circuits incorporating the layout-design. Such failure constitutes grounds for cancellation under this Act. The applicant seeking cancellation must provide evidence demonstrating the non-compliance, and the Registrar may issue a notice to the registered proprietor allowing them an opportunity to be heard. If, following such hearing, the Registrar finds that the condition has not been met, they may order the registration cancelled; a *cancelled registrar layout* shall then be deemed void ab initio. Any person aggrieved by this decision may appeal under provisions as provided herein.

An application for registration of a semiconductor integrated circuit layout-design shall be deemed to have been abandoned if, following an invitation under this Act requiring the applicant to submit specific details regarding the fabrication process, the applicant fails to respond within the prescribed time limit. Furthermore, where a registered layout-design is subsequently found to be substantially similar to a prior unregistrable design, or where it has been determined that the registration was obtained through fraudulent misrepresentation, the Registrar may initiate proceedings for cancellation. In such instances, the cancelled registrar layout shall remain accessible for public inspection as provided herein, with appropriate notations indicating its status and the reasons for cancellation. Any party aggrieved by a decision of the Registrar concerning the cancellation of a registered layout-design may appeal to the Intellectual Property Appellate Board within sixty days from the date of communication of the order.

Where a registrar layout has been declared invalid under this Act, subsequent applications for registration relating to the same integrated circuit shall be considered only if the applicant demonstrates that the prior declaration of invalidity did not stem from an inherent deficiency in the underlying design principles. The Registrar may require submission of expert testimony substantiating such demonstration and assessing the novelty of the new application relative to the previously rejected layout. Further, any party aggrieved by a decision concerning a cancelled registrar layout is entitled to appeal to the Intellectual Property Appellate Board within sixty days of notification of the order. Provided that this right of appeal shall not revive the registration; it merely allows for judicial review as provided herein.

Where the Registrar, following a reasoned order published as per the prescribed procedure, determines that a registered layout-design has been obtained through fraudulent means or involves an infringement of prior rights, the registrar layout shall stand cancelled. Any person aggrieved by such cancellation may appeal to the Intellectual Property Appellate Tribunal within sixty days from the date of publication of the Registrar’s order. Failure to comply with this timeframe shall render the appeal inadmissible. The tribunal may, after affording opportunity for hearing to all concerned parties, confirm, vary or annul the cancellation order. Where a cancelled registrar layout involves ongoing commercial exploitation, penalties as provided herein shall be levied against those continuing such activity.

The Registrar shall, upon receiving an application from a third party demonstrating substantial investment made in reliance on a purportedly valid semiconductor integrated circuit layout-design registration, investigate whether such registration has been properly maintained. Where it is determined that the registered proprietor failed to adhere to prescribed maintenance protocols, or otherwise engaged in conduct detrimental to the interests of those relying on the public register, the Registrar may initiate proceedings for cancellation of the said registration. Should the cancellation be confirmed, any existing licenses granted by the original registrant relating to the layout-design shall remain valid and enforceable against third parties, subject to the terms thereof. Furthermore, assignment of rights under such licenses will not be affected by the cancelled registrar layout status, provided that the assignee was a bona fide purchaser for value at the time of grant.

Where a registrar has, pursuant to an order of the Intellectual Property Appellate Tribunal, revoked a registration for a semiconductor integrated circuit layout-design and subsequently reinstated it, that reinstatement shall not revive any rights or remedies accrued prior to the date of revocation. Any party aggrieved by such reinstatement may appeal to the High Court within ninety days from the date of communication of the Tribunal’s order. The appellate court may entertain an appeal only if the appellant demonstrates demonstrable prejudice arising directly from the initial cancellation and subsequent reinstatement, subject to the registrar's determination that the cancelled registrar layout was validly registered initially. Provided that a certificate issued by the Registrar confirming the validity of the registration shall be prima facie evidence thereof in any legal proceeding.

Where a registrar layout has been, at any time, declared invalid through judicial determination, such declaration shall constitute conclusive evidence for purposes of enforcement actions under this Act. Any party aggrieved by an order cancelling a registrar layout may appeal to the relevant High Court within ninety days from the date of that order; provided that the claim shall date back to the original filing of the layout-design application and any subsequent proceedings relating to its validity are deemed continuous therefrom. Failure to comply with prescribed timelines for appeals will render such appeals inadmissible. The court may, upon finding merit in an appeal, reinstate a cancelled registrar layout subject to conditions as it deems fit, and impose penalties on parties found to have acted in bad faith during the cancellation process.

Subject to the provisions of this Act, a license granted under section 26 shall continue in force unless revoked by the Registrar or terminated as per its terms. Where a layout-design registration has been cancelled by the Registrar, any assignment of rights relating to that design, whether executed prior to or subsequent to the cancellation, shall be deemed null and void; however, this provision shall not prejudice existing contractual obligations arising from such assignments. The Registrar may, upon application by an interested party demonstrating substantial reliance on a purportedly valid license linked to a cancelled registrar layout, order interim enforcement of the license pending determination of its validity. Furthermore, if a trade mark identical or deceptively similar to elements within the layout-design is also registered, this shall not automatically invalidate the licensing agreement but may be considered during disputes concerning infringement under this Act.

A registration for a semiconductor integrated circuit layout-design shall be deemed to have been cancelled if, following an inquiry as provided herein, the Registrar finds that the registered layout-design was obtained through fraud or misrepresentation. For the purposes of this Act, a “cancelled registrar layout” refers specifically to such a layout-design whose registration has ceased to have effect under these provisions. The notice applicant shall be afforded a reasonable opportunity to present evidence and arguments against the proposed cancellation. Further, any person aggrieved by an order of the Registrar cancelling a layout may appeal to the relevant appellate authority within a prescribed time period, subject to conditions as provided herein.

An application for registration of a semiconductor integrated circuit layout-design relating to a novel formulation process used in the manufacture of pharmaceutical compounds shall be deemed invalid if it is established that the applicant has failed to maintain accurate records pertaining to the design’s creation and modification, as required under this Act. Furthermore, where the Registrar reasonably believes that a registered layout-design incorporates elements substantially derived from an unregistered prior art design, or that representations made during the registration process were materially false, the registrar may initiate proceedings for cancellation. A cancelled registrar layout shall remain so until such time as any appeal against the order of cancellation is disposed of by the relevant appellate authority.
